0.text: The following persistent options apply to UIR commands. Run uir --help or uir <command> --help for command-specific options and output settings. OptionEnvironmentDefault and effect--dsn <string>UIR_DSNDatabase connection: a PostgreSQL DSN, sqlite:// URL, or .db path. A nonempty flag takes precedence over the environment variable; if both are empty, UIR uses ~/.config/uir/uir.db and creates its parent directory. Other SQLite paths need an existing parent directory.--schema <string>UIR_SCHEMAPostgreSQL schema. A nonempty flag takes precedence over the environment variable; if both are empty, UIR uses public. A non-default schema requires PostgreSQL.--cpuprofile <path>—Empty by default. Write a CPU profile for the command to the specified file.--memprofile <path>—Empty by default. Write a heap profile after garbage collection when the command ends.--trace <path>—Empty by default. Write a Go execution trace for the command. Before opening an existing database with a newer UIR version, back it up and consult the storage cutover instructions. Some older layouts lose index snapshots or legacy project history when opened and require reindexing.
0.title: CLI configuration

1.text: These flags are inherited by commands. Boolean flags default to false unless stated otherwise; string values default to empty. FlagsEffect-i, --interactiveFill command arguments using an interactive form.-P, --properties <key=value>Set system properties; accepts a string-to-string map, empty by default.--format <spec>Select pretty, json, ndjson, toon, yaml, csv, html, markdown, llm, pdf, or slack. A bare format writes to stdout; format=path writes a file. Combine comma-separated sinks, for example json=out.json,markdown=summary.md. The default is pretty output.--pretty, --json, --yaml, --csv, --html, --markdown, --llm, --pdfSelect the named output format. LLM output includes up to 25 rows with paging information.--table, --treeAdd table or tree structure to the selected output format.--filter <CEL>Filter output data with a CEL expression.--dump-schema, --no-colorPrint the output schema to stderr for debugging, or disable colored output.--log-level <level>, -v, --loglevelSet the default log level (default info), or increase verbosity with a repeatable count.--json-logs, --log-to-stderr, --report-callerUse JSON logs, send logs to stderr (default true), or include caller information.--timings[=<path>]Report resource timings: a bare flag writes a Server-Timing line to stderr; a path writes JSON.--no-progressDisable task progress display.--max-concurrent <int>, --max-retries <int>Limit concurrent tasks (default 4; 0 means unlimited) and retries (default 3).--retry-delay <duration>, --graceful-timeout <duration>Set the base retry delay (default 1s) and interrupt shutdown timeout (default 10s).-h, --help, --versionShow help or the version.
1.title: Shared flags

2.text: uir diff lists the symbols a module root added, removed, and changed between two Git commits, or between two revisions an external producer published with uir import (see external roots), and with --stat how many lines each symbol gained and lost. It reads the two commits' snapshots from the index and, for line counts only, the two commits' blobs from a registered checkout. With --auto-index, missing clean snapshots are generated from temporary Git worktrees without changing the registered checkout or its head snapshot. The design is in symbol-index-storage.md; the implementation is the symboldiff package.
2.title: Diffing two commits

3.text:
uir diff <range>     [--root <module>] [--location <checkout>] [--visibility exported|internal|all] [--change-type <pattern>...] [--stat] [--auto-index] [--include-tests] [--snapshot-from <uuid>] [--snapshot-to <uuid>]
uir diff <from> <to> [same flags]
uir diff <rev>       [--root <module>] [--location <checkout>] [--visibility exported|internal|all] [--change-type <pattern>...] [--untracked] [--stat]
git diff HEAD~3 | uir diff [-] [--visibility exported|internal|all] [--change-type <pattern>...] [--stat] Revisions are read as git diff reads them, by letting git resolve them rather than re-implementing its syntax: RevisionsComparesA..B, A.., ..BA to B; an empty side is HEAD.A BA to B.A...BThe merge base of A and B to B. More than one merge base fails.A^!, A^-, A^-nA's first (or nth) parent to A.AA to the worktree of the checkout it resolved in, through the patch path (see comparing with the worktree).pr:NThe head of pull request N, fetched from origin; usable on either side of .. and ... and as either of two revisions. Two revisions are each resolved as before: a full 40- or 64-character commit hash is used as is; anything else is resolved with git rev-parse --verify <rev>^{commit} in the root's registered checkouts, --location (or the current checkout) first. A single spec is expanded with git rev-parse --revs-only in the first checkout that knows it: one positive and one negative commit are a range, two positives and one negative (A...B) are the merge base to B, and a lone positive is a single revision only when the spec itself names one commit. Anything else (A^@, ^A, an A^! of a merge commit) fails, naming the commits the spec expanded to. In Go, symboldiff.ResolveRevisions returns the resolved pair, or the single commit and its checkout. FlagMeaning--rootThe module path (root_key) to diff. Defaults to the module of the registered checkout enclosing the working directory (the nearest go.mod); outside one, it is required with a range.--locationThe registered checkout to resolve and index revisions from, so HEAD and branch names mean that worktree's. Defaults to the checkout enclosing the working directory when it belongs to --root, else the primary checkout. A relative or symlinked path is canonicalized.--visibilityexported (default), internal, or all. A row is kept when the symbol's visibility on either side matches, except a structure row, which internal and all keep whatever the symbol's visibility and exported never does.--change-typeThe row classes to report: added, removed, signature, structure, body, format, moved, import. Repeatable or comma separated, with commons MatchItems patterns: * wildcards and ! exclusions, which win (--change-type '!format,!import' removes layout and import rows). Default all. It filters rows after symbols are paired, so it never changes a row's class; filtered rows count as hidden. A file left without a row is omitted and counted in its package's hidden_files (whose totals still include it), and a package left without a file is omitted. A pattern that matches no class fails.--untrackedWith a single revision, also compare the worktree's untracked files that are not ignored, as new files (see comparing with the worktree).--statAdds per-package, per-file, and per-symbol +added -removed counts. Requires readable Git blobs, or for an external root the source blobs its publications stored.--snapshot-from, --snapshot-toUse this snapshot for that side instead of the newest clean one. The snapshot must belong to the root and record that commit as its revision.--auto-indexSelect or generate a clean snapshot for each commit under the current standalone module configuration. Historical indexing reads the commit's go.mod and go.sum with GOWORK=off, so the current workspace cannot replace dependencies or hide the historical module. It leaves registered checkout files and heads untouched.--include-testsInclude Go test symbols in snapshots generated with --auto-index. Without it, test files are excluded, matching the usual indexing default. The command is a Clicky operation, so --format json, --format yaml, --format markdown, and --format html all render the same typed result, and uir serve exposes it as POST /api/v1/modules/diff with a body such as {"args": ["<from>..<to>"], "root": "example.org/service", "visibility": "all", "stat": true, "auto-index": true}. uir history [--root <module>] [--location <checkout>] and GET /api/v1/modules/history list local branches, recent commits, and up to 50 pull request refs from origin for the browser's History view. A pr:<number> revision fetches that pull request head from origin when selected. On the command line --root and --location default from the working directory as for uir diff; over HTTP the server's working directory is not the caller's, so root is required. To inspect one Git commit as change history, use uir history show <commit> [--root <module>]. It compares that commit with its first parent, indexes either missing clean snapshot on demand, and shows all symbol changes with line counts by default. --visibility exported|internal|all, --change-type, --include-tests, and --stat=false control the result. An initial commit has no parent and returns an error; use uir diff with an explicit range when comparing other revisions. uir history show HEAD --root example.org/ledger # from inside a registered checkout of example.org/ledger
uir diff HEAD~1..HEAD --visibility all --stat
3.title: Command

4.text:
--patch emits complete original Git hunks selected by --visibility and --change-type. It supports stdin, worktree comparisons and Git commit ranges. It writes patch bytes only; it does not stage changes. A hunk mixing selected edits with other edits fails before any output. Use smaller input hunks (git diff -U0; apply these with git apply --unidiff-zero) or separate the edits first. Fully selected file additions/deletions include package/import scaffolding and declaration separators. mkdir -p .tmp
git diff --full-index --no-renames | uir diff --patch --visibility all --change-type moved,renamed > .tmp/refactors.patch
git apply --cached --check .tmp/refactors.patch
git apply --cached .tmp/refactors.patch Use git diff to base the patch on the current index and preserve existing staged changes. uir diff HEAD --patch --untracked instead compares HEAD with the worktree, including untracked destinations; its patch requires an index matching that base. No matches emit an empty patch successfully. --patch is incompatible with formatted output, --stat, HTTP requests and external roots without Git hunks. renamed pairs unique Go declarations whose tokens differ only in their own declared name and resolved self references, with unchanged visibility and implementation. The row exposes name_before and its current name. Ambiguous candidates remain added/removed. Selected renames also include original reference-only edits proven by Go symbol resolution. Unresolved references are not selected by spelling, and a selected reference line containing other edits is rejected. No edits outside the supplied comparison are synthesized. uir diff <rev> is git diff <rev>: it runs git diff --full-index --no-renames <commit> in the checkout the revision resolved in (the current checkout, or --location) and diffs that patch as below, without the index. A pure rename would carry no blob ids, and symbols pair across files on their own. from.commit is the resolved commit and to.commit is worktree when any side was read from the worktree. --snapshot-from, --snapshot-to, --auto-index, and --include-tests apply to two commits and fail with a single revision; over HTTP a single revision is refused, because the server's worktree is not the caller's. Untracked files are not part of it, as with git, unless --untracked is set. Then the diff runs against a temporary copy of the index (GIT_INDEX_FILE) in which every file git ls-files --others --exclude-standard lists is marked intent-to-add, so those files appear as new files and a symbol moved into one pairs as moved. The checkout's own index is never written. --untracked with a range or a patch on stdin fails. A single revision needs no index, so outside every registered checkout, with neither --root nor --location, it is resolved and diffed in the git repository holding the working directory, and the root is that repository's go.mod module, as for a patch. A range there still requires a registered checkout (uir add .) or --root, because it compares indexed snapshots. uir diff HEAD --visibility all --untracked --change-type '!added,!removed'
4.title: Emit a patch for selective staging

5.text:
Without a range, or with -, uir diff reads a git patch from stdin and reports the same result for it, with no database and no indexing: git diff HEAD~3 | uir diff
git diff | uir diff --stat --visibility all Bytes. Each side of a file is the blob its index <old>..<new> line names, read in the repository holding the working directory (git rev-parse --show-toplevel). Every id of the patch, abbreviated or full, is written to one git cat-file --batch process and its answers are read in order, so a patch of any size costs the same few git processes. An all-zero id is an absent side and is never sent to git. An old side git does not have, an ambiguous abbreviated id (produce the patch with --full-index), or an id that names something other than a blob fails the command, naming the path and id. A new side git does not have is a worktree file (git diff without --cached): it is read from the worktree, and all such files are hashed by one git hash-object --stdin-paths process; each must still hash to the patch's id, otherwise the command fails with worktree changed since the patch was produced. The result's to.commit is then worktree, else patch:new; from.commit is patch:old. In Go, symboldiff.DiffPatch reads the sides through a SourceLocator; symboldiff.NewGitLocator is the one described here.Packages. A file's package is the nearest go.mod above it in the worktree joined with its directory below that module; the root is the module of the top-level go.mod. A file outside every module, or a repository without a top-level go.mod, fails the command.Symbols. Go files are extracted from syntax alone (syntax.Document, in indexer/syntax), so every file and row carries the syntax marker, and shapes are the canonical UIR layer shapes (method public (a (int)) ( (int))) rather than go/types-printed ones. Unlike a syntax document in the index, each symbol's public and private hashes are computed from its extracted node, so rows still classify as signature and structure. Package-level var and const declarations are symbols too: the shape is the declared type alone (package_variable (int) public, or package_variable public when untyped), so a changed value is body and a changed type signature. Symbols are matched by a stand-in for the canonical id: the identity key with a function's signature reduced to its parameter types, so a parameter rename is a signature row and a parameter-type change is a grouped removed plus added, as with an index.Files. A rename is the removal of its old path and the addition of its new one, so its unchanged symbols are moved. A file that is not Go source is listed with excluded: not Go source and no rows. A mode-only change is skipped. With --stat, lines are attributed from the same bytes; there is no manifest comparison.Refused input. A plain diff -u without index lines, a rename at 100% similarity (git writes no index line for it; use git diff --no-renames), copies (-C), and combined merge diffs fail. --root, --snapshot-from, --snapshot-to, --auto-index, --include-tests, and --location apply to a range and fail with a patch. Over HTTP a patch is refused: there is no stdin, and the server's working directory is not the caller's.
5.title: Diffing a git patch

6.text: For each commit the diff takes the root's snapshots whose revision equals the commit (through the (root_id, revision) index) and picks the newest whose worktree_state is clean. Indexing records clean only when git status --porcelain under the module is empty and every indexed file is tracked by Git. Untracked files that Git does not ignore are indexed and make the snapshot dirty; Git-ignored files are excluded from discovery. This keeps a clean snapshot's source bytes equal to the commit's bytes. No snapshot for the commit: without --auto-index, the diff fails and says the commit must be indexed first. With --auto-index, it creates a clean standalone snapshot from a temporary worktree.Only dirty snapshots: without --auto-index, the diff fails and names them, because a dirty snapshot's bytes may not be the commit's bytes. With --auto-index, it creates a clean standalone snapshot. Pass --snapshot-from or --snapshot-to to use a dirty snapshot explicitly; --stat then verifies each file's blob against the snapshot and reports the files whose bytes differ.Different configuration_hash on the two selected snapshots (another indexer version, GOOS, GOARCH, CGO_ENABLED, toolchain, or tags): the diff fails, because shape and body hashes are only comparable under one configuration. --auto-index selects or generates both sides under the current standalone configuration.
6.title: Selecting the snapshots

7.text: Both snapshots' active documents are derived with storage.ActiveDocuments without their content: changed-file detection compares document headers only (id, ordinal, coverage, revision). A path whose document id is equal on both sides is skipped without being read. A path present on one side only is an added or removed file. A path whose document changed only because a sibling in its package changed (same bytes, new input hash) is a changed file, but its symbols' fingerprints compare equal, so without --stat it is omitted without its document being decoded.
7.title: Changed files

8.text: Symbols are matched across the whole diff by identity, so a symbol that moved to another file is still one symbol. For changed indexed documents outside a package that is syntax or partial on either side, classification reads no document: both snapshots' effective symbols (storage.EffectiveSymbols, from the symbol deltas) give each defined symbol's public, private, and content fingerprints, the first eight bytes of its public_hash, private_hash, and content_hash, and the definition postings of each side's changed documents say which of them define each symbol. A symbol declared once on each side it appears on is classified by its handle: ClassConditionaddedonly on the new sideremovedonly on the old sidesignatureboth sides, public fingerprint differsstructurepublic fingerprint equal, private fingerprint differsbodypublic and private fingerprints equal, content fingerprint differsmovedfingerprints equal, defining path_key differsformatfingerprints and path equal, the declaration's source bytes differ (comments, whitespace, layout)importa file on both sides imports a path under an alias the other side does not, or under another pathomittedfingerprints, path, and source bytes equal The three layers nest (a public change is always a private change), so the class names the outermost layer that changed, and a row carries no separate layer field: ClassLayerWhat changedGo exampleSQL examplesignaturepublicwhat code outside the symbol's visibility boundary observesa parameter, a result, an exported fielda table's output columns, a procedure's parametersstructureprivatethe full declared structure onlyan unexported field added to an exported struct that already had one (the public shape's opaque line stands for every unexported field)an index, a foreign key, a defaultbodycontentthe implementation onlya function bodya view definition, a procedure or trigger body A package with a syntax or partial changed document on either side, and a symbol an external producer declares more than once on a side, are matched over their decoded documents instead: first by canonical symbol id, then by key wherever one side has no id (a syntax document, or an unproven declaration in a partial document). Each Go func init has its own file-and-ordinal discriminator and canonical id. Those rows use the same classes and compare the full public_hash, private_hash, and content_hash; when either side has no id the public and private hashes are not comparable, so such a pair can only be body or moved.
8.title: Classification

9.text: A document is decoded only when the output needs it. With --stat, every changed document is read, for its symbol extents. Otherwise the diff reads the documents of syntax, partial, and excluded files, both sides of a symbol declared more than once, and, for a row the visibility filter shows, the new side of an added symbol, the old side of a removed one, and both sides of a signature or structure change, whose shapes the row prints. With --visibility internal or all, both sides of every changed file on both sides are read too, for their imports. A shown body or moved row prints no shape and is named from the symbols row and its owners' names. The chosen documents' content is loaded in one batched read (storage.DocumentContents). content_hash digests the declaration's tokens without comments, whitespace, or layout tokens, with the names it binds renamed to their positions (content layer), so a comment added inside a function, a re-wrapped call, gofmt, or a renamed local leaves every hash equal. Such a symbol whose source bytes did change is a format row, kept apart from body so --change-type '!format' drops it. A patch diff compares the extents' bytes directly and reports format rows with or without --stat; a commit-to-commit diff has the bytes only from blobs, so it reports them only with --stat, when the symbol's line counts are nonzero. Imports are not symbols, and a syntax shape names a package by its alias (cel.Env), so a module path change behind an unchanged alias leaves every hash equal. Each document records its file's imports (alias and path, format 11), and a file on both sides gets one import row per alias whose path changed or that one side alone imports (a blank or dot import is keyed by its path): shape_before and shape_after are the paths. Reordering an import block reports nothing, and an added or removed file's imports are not reported. An import binds a name in its file only, so its visibility is internal: import rows are shown by --visibility internal and all, never by exported. A commit-to-commit diff that shows them reads both sides' documents of every changed file on both sides. A unique pure Go declaration rename is renamed, with name_before recording its old name. Ambiguous candidates remain removed plus added, because the name is part of the identity. A parameter-type change is also removed plus added, because parameter types are part of the identity; when exactly one removed and one added symbol share package, kind, owner, and name, both rows carry the same group, and the added row carries the old shape and a shape diff against it, so the change reads as one signature edit. A move to another package changes the identity too, because the package is part of it. After identity matching, the removed and added symbols are grouped by kind, owner, and name; a group of exactly one removed and one added symbol in different packages is paired when their full shapes are equal once the qualifiers naming either package (by its last import path element) are removed, since a move turns models.Item into Item and back. Both documents are read for it, and the pair is classified by its layer hashes like any other: moved only when nothing but its file changed, otherwise signature, structure, or body. moved is a pure move; a symbol that moved and changed keeps its changed class and is still reported under both files. The output never guesses other pairings: a name with two candidates on either side stays removed plus added. A row has kind, owner, name, visibility, both shapes when they differ, both paths, line counts with --stat, and coverage markers. A signature row's shapes are the public shapes (public_shape), so a Go struct shows its exported fields and opaque; every other row's shapes are the private (full) shapes (shape). It is reported under its new file, or under its old file when removed. A symbol paired across two files (a moved row, or a change whose defining file also changed) is reported under both: the row under its new file names the file it came from, and a copy with moved_away: true under its old file names the file it went to, so neither file appears to have silently lost or gained it. The copy carries no line counts; the symbol's lines count under its new file only. Renamed or retyped symbols and cross-package candidates that cannot be paired remain removed plus added. Nested symbols (struct fields, interface methods) are rows of their own, but their lines belong to the outermost declaration that contains them, so they carry no line counts.
9.title: Which documents are read

10.text: MarkerMeaningpartialThe package type-checked with errors on either side. Only proven symbols have ids; unproven ones are matched by key, and a symbol missing from a partial side may be unproven rather than removed.syntaxThe package did not type-check on either side. Symbols are matched by key and can only be added, removed, body, or moved.excludedThe file is not extracted (build constraints) on either side. All of its lines are file scope; symbols the other side declares are reported without line counts.manifestgo.mod or go.sum differs between the two commits (with --stat only). It has no rows; its whole diff is file scope.
10.title: Coverage

11.text: With --stat, each changed file's bytes are read at both commits with git cat-file -p <commit>:./<path> in a registered checkout of the root that contains the commit (the primary location first, then any other location where git rev-parse --verify <commit>^{commit} succeeds). Each blob is hashed with SHA-256, as the indexer hashes source files, and must equal the source revision's content_hash. Each side of a file is cut into segments: one per outermost symbol extent (widened to whole lines when nothing else shares them), plus a single (file scope) segment of everything between them: the package clause, imports, free comments, and blank lines. Segments are paired by symbol id (or key), the two file-scope segments are paired with each other, and each pair is line-diffed with a Myers diff. A symbol on one side only counts all of its lines as added or removed. A moved symbol is diffed against its old extent and counted under its new file. A file's total is the sum of every row reported under it, hidden rows included, plus its file scope; a package's total is the sum of its files. For a file without moved symbols this is normally what git diff --numstat reports; the two can differ when Git's whole-file diff aligns lines across a declaration boundary, which a per-segment diff never does.
11.title: Line attribution

12.text:
example.org/ledger old..new
╰── 📦 example.org/ledger/money  +5 -3
    ╰── ✏️ money/money.go (modified)  +5 -3
        ├── ✏️ Scale  signature  +1 -1
        │   ╰── - func Scale(a Amount, factor int) Amount
        │       + func Scale(a Amount, by int) Amount
        ├── 💻 Format  body  +4 -2
        ╰── (file scope)  +0 -0 A signature row shows a shape diff of the public shapes, and a structure row one of the private shapes. The tree groups those lines beneath their symbol; change icons identify each file and symbol class. With --stat, the + and - counts on body rows show changed content lines, and ANSI colors distinguish additions from removals. The two canonical shapes are line-diffed with Myers, treating lines that differ only in whitespace (gofmt realignment) as equal. Within a changed hunk, the i-th removed line and the i-th added line are a replaced pair when they share at least one non-blank token, and are token-diffed; short equal runs between edits are folded into the edit so a changed tail reads as one replacement. A Go root's lines are split into go/scanner tokens (tokenizer go). An external root's shapes are not Go, so they are split language-neutrally (tokenizer text): identifiers (which may start with @, #, or $), numbers, quoted strings and identifiers ('…', "…", `…`), and runs of any other non-space characters. The plain form (non-TTY output, String()) prints unchanged lines with two spaces, removed lines with - , and added lines with + . The rich forms print a replaced pair as one ~  line with token marks, through clicky api.Text: removed tokens red and struck through, added tokens green and bold. In a terminal that is ANSI; in markdown func Scale(a Amount, ~~factor~~**by** int) Amount (wrapped in colour spans unless colour is off); in HTML clicky's <s> and <strong>. JSON carries the structured form: shape_diff is a list of lines {op, text, paired, tokenizer, tokens: [{op, text}]}, where op is equal, delete, or insert, a paired line names the tokenizer (go or text) its tokens were split by, and a paired delete line's tokens are its equal and deleted runs while the paired insert line's are its equal and inserted runs. --visibility exported hides internal rows and structure rows, and --change-type hides rows of other classes, but neither hides their lines: a file with hidden rows says (N hidden rows) and its totals still include them, so the totals never silently add up to less than the file's diff.
12.title: Rendering

13.text:
A root whose locations are all external (a non-Go producer's URI, registered by uir import / indexer.Publish) is diffed without Git. A root is either Go or external; one that mixes the two location kinds fails. Revisions. <from> and <to> are taken literally, never resolved with git rev-parse: each must equal a published snapshot's revision or git_commit (for example schema-v1..schema-v2, or schema-v1 schema-v2). Only those two forms are accepted: A...B, A.., a single revision, and the other Git forms fail with a message asking for <from>..<to>. An unknown revision fails, naming it and the root.Snapshots. Each side is the newest import or historical snapshot of its revision. A producer's snapshot has no worktree to be clean or dirty, so its worktree_state (unknown) is not checked. --snapshot-from and --snapshot-to work as for a Go root.Line counts. With --stat, each file's bytes are the source blob its publication stored under the source revision's content_hash, verified against that hash; checkout is empty. An external root has no manifests.Shape diffs use the language-neutral tokenizer.No Git history. --auto-index fails, because a producer's revision cannot be indexed from Git: republish it with uir import. uir history and uir history show fail too; compare two published revisions with uir diff. uir import schema-v1.json
uir import schema-v2.json
uir diff schema-v1..schema-v2 --root example.org/schema --visibility all --stat
13.title: External roots

14.text: FailureEffectEmpty revision, malformed range, unknown --visibility, unknown rootThe command fails.Revision that no checkout resolvesThe command fails; pass the full commit hash.External root: revision with no published snapshot, --auto-index, or uir historyThe command fails, naming the revision or saying the root is published by an external producer.External root: no stored blob under a source's content hash, or a blob whose hash differs (--stat)That file's lines_error says so; its rows are still reported.Commit with no snapshot, or only dirty snapshotsThe command fails and names the commit or the dirty snapshots.Override snapshot of another root or another revisionThe command fails.Different configuration hashesThe command fails.A symbol that a changed document defines is not effective on exactly the sides whose changed documents define it, or a symbol whose effective fingerprints differ is declared by no changed documentThe command fails naming the symbol handle, because the symbol deltas are inconsistent with the documents.No registered checkout contains a commit (--stat)The result's lines_error and every file's lines_error say so; symbol rows are still reported, and manifests are not compared.Blob unreadable, or its hash differs from the source revision (--stat)That file's lines_error states the path, commit, and both hashes; its rows are reported without counts, and every other file completes. A moved symbol whose other file failed fails its destination file's counts with the reason.Manifest on a dirty snapshot (--stat)The manifest's lines_error says its bytes cannot be verified.
14.title: Failure modes

15.text: The package-level export_shape_hash pre-check that the design suggests for skipping packages under --visibility exported is not applied: skipping would hide exported body rows and line counts, so every changed package is read.
15.title: Not implemented

16.text: The History page compares any two selected branches, commits, or pull request heads. The Git log shows recent commits; selecting one compares it with its first parent and displays changed packages, files, symbol rows, signatures, and line counts. Comparison choices and the selected log commit are kept in the URL.
16.title: Browser history

17.text: UIR provides a Go model library and a CLI for indexing, querying, and comparing code.
17.title: Getting started

18.text:
Build from a checkout with Go 1.27.4 or newer, Node.js 24, and the pnpm version pinned in the root package.json: git clone https://github.com/flanksource/uir.git
cd uir
pnpm --dir web install --frozen-lockfile
make build The CLI is written to .bin/uir. Run make install to install it into your Go binary directory with the browser assets embedded.
18.title: Install the CLI

19.text:
From the repository root, index the included sample module in a separate SQLite database: mkdir -p .tmp
.bin/uir --dsn .tmp/quickstart.db add docs/examples/sql-go
.bin/uir --dsn .tmp/quickstart.db list add keeps discovery within the selected directory. Use --all when you also want the modules referenced by an enclosing go.work. See module indexing for checkout discovery, snapshots, and reindexing.
19.title: Index a Go module

20.text:
Select the sample's Run function, then follow its references: .bin/uir --dsn .tmp/quickstart.db query 'func:Run' --root example.org/service
.bin/uir --dsn .tmp/quickstart.db query 'func:Run <' --root example.org/service
.bin/uir --dsn .tmp/quickstart.db query 'func:Run :uses' --root example.org/service The first query returns the Run declaration in service.go; the callers query finds Entry and Replay. The query guide explains selectors and relation operators. SQL navigation provides an alternative syntax for navigating code and custom domains.
20.title: Query symbols

21.text: From the repository root, compare its current tracked changes with HEAD without indexing: .bin/uir diff HEAD --visibility all --stat The diff guide also covers indexed commit ranges, imports, and formatting changes. To enforce SQL architecture rules, add a .uir.yaml using the lint guide, then run uir lint. Rules select syntax or typed analysis automatically; --changed, --staged, and --tags restrict the source or build configuration being checked.
21.title: Compare changes and lint

22.text: .bin/uir --dsn .tmp/quickstart.db serve Open the local URL printed by the server to explore saved snapshots, source files, and symbols. The same server exposes a structured HTTP API; see browser and API.
22.title: Open the browser

23.text: go get github.com/flanksource/uir Use the root package for node types and builders, diff for structural comparison, and render for tree output. The model reference describes the shared JSON contract and the node and statement hierarchy.

27.text:
storage.EffectiveSources accepts EffectiveSourcesOptions{SnapshotID, Paths, Prefix, Suffix}. A nil Paths slice selects every effective source; an empty non-nil slice selects none. Prefix and suffix filters match literal paths, including percent and underscore characters. Filters apply while resolving source deltas, before loading revision records, so reading comparison metadata does not hydrate unrelated XML bindings. Every selection still validates the complete snapshot base chain and respects deletions. Pipeline.ReadModuleSources passes the requested document paths through this projection. It reuses the verified revision records during Git retrieval rather than querying all source revisions again. Run the focused checks: go test ./indexer ./query -run 'Test(Indexer|Query)$' -ginkgo.focus='Git-backed external publication|historical publication options|external delta publication|reading many module sources' -ginkgo.no-color
go test ./storage -run TestStorage -ginkgo.focus='UirDB|source blobs' -ginkgo.no-color

28.text: This document provides the detailed API specification for the Universal Intermediate Representation (UIR). The UIR is a universal Abstract Syntax Tree (AST) format designed to represent source code, data structures, and service definitions from multiple languages and domains in a unified structure.
28.title: Universal Intermediate Representation (UIR) API Specification

114.text: Synthetic nodes represent entry points created implicitly by framework annotations rather than explicit code declarations. These nodes provide a unified interface for framework-based routing patterns.
114.title: 4. Synthetic Nodes

115.text: Many frameworks (JAX-RS, Spring, JAX-WS, JMS) use annotations to declare API endpoints, message listeners, and service operations without explicit interface definitions. UIR captures these as synthetic nodes to maintain complete call graphs and dependency tracking.
115.title: 4.1. Overview

116.text: Synthetic nodes follow a consistent three-part structure: Synthetic Entry Point: A virtual node representing the public interface (e.g., HTTP endpoint, SOAP operation)Linking Statement: A statement connecting the synthetic node to its implementationImplementation Handler: The actual method or function containing the business logic
116.title: 4.2. Three-Part Pattern

117.title: JAX-RS REST Endpoints

118.title: Spring Controller Endpoints

119.title: NestJS Controller Endpoints

120.title: Express.js Routes

121.title: JMS Message Listeners

122.text: Complete Call Graphs: Synthetic nodes enable tracing from external requests to implementation codeFramework Abstraction: Unified representation across different frameworks (JAX-RS, Spring, etc.)Dependency Analysis: Track which endpoints depend on which services and databasesImpact Analysis: Understand the full scope of changes when modifying handler methods
122.title: 4.4. Benefits

123.text: Virtual paths provide a standardized way to represent AST sources that originate from non-file locations such as databases, URLs, or remote APIs.
123.title: 5. Virtual Paths

124.text: Not all code or schema definitions exist as files in a repository. Databases contain schema definitions, remote APIs expose OpenAPI specifications, and configuration systems store executable logic. Virtual paths allow UIR to represent these sources uniformly alongside file-based AST nodes.
124.title: 5.1. Overview

125.text: Virtual paths follow the pattern: virtual://<source-type>/<connection-or-url>/<resource-path> Components: source-type: The type of remote source (e.g., sql_connection, openapi_url)connection-or-url: Connection string, URL, or identifier for the sourceresource-path: Path within the source (e.g., table name, endpoint path)
125.title: 5.2. Path Format

126.title: SQL Database Schema

127.title: OpenAPI Specification from URL

128.text: virtual://config_source/consul://consul.example.com:8500/services/api-config Represents configuration stored in a Consul key-value store.
128.title: Remote Configuration

129.text: Virtual path nodes integrate seamlessly with file-based nodes in the AST: Relationships: Relationships can span between file-based and virtual nodes (e.g., a Java method calling a database stored procedure)Dependencies: Virtual nodes can be dependencies of file-based modulesCall Graphs: Function calls can traverse from application code (file-based) to database operations (virtual)
129.title: 5.4. Integration with File-Based Nodes

130.text: Unified Representation: All code and schema sources use consistent node structuresComplete Dependency Graphs: Track dependencies across files, databases, and remote APIsSource Traceability: Maintain origin information for remotely-sourced definitionsChange Impact Analysis: Understand the impact of database schema changes on application code
130.title: 5.5. Benefits

156.text:
Relationship Traversal: -- Efficient call graph query (forward)
WITH RECURSIVE call_chain AS (
  SELECT from_node_id, to_node_id, 1 as depth
  FROM ast_relationships
  WHERE from_node_id = $1 AND relationship_type = 'call'

  UNION ALL

  SELECT r.from_node_id, r.to_node_id, c.depth + 1
  FROM ast_relationships r
  JOIN call_chain c ON r.from_node_id = c.to_node_id
  WHERE c.depth < 10 AND r.relationship_type = 'call'
)
SELECT DISTINCT n.*
FROM call_chain c
JOIN ast_nodes n ON c.to_node_id = n.id; Materialized Views: Pre-compute common queries (public API surface, dependency counts)Refresh on AST updatesTrade storage for query speed

179.text: uir graph draws the calls around one function or method of the indexed snapshots: the functions that call it, the functions it calls, or both. Each call carries its call sites, and each site the conditions that must hold to reach it. The graph is built by the graph package from the symbol index (query/graph_source.go); the conditions are read from the hash-verified source of the snapshot (query/graph_guards.go) and lowered to UIR by the golang package.
179.title: Call graphs

180.text:
uir graph <selector> [--direction callees|callers|both] [--depth <n>] [--limit <n>] [--exclude <patterns>] [--root <module>] [--location <checkout>] [--snapshot <uuid>] [--all] [--since <rev> [--since-snapshot <uuid>]]
uir graph --symbol <id> [...] OptionMeaning<selector>, --selectorA compact symbol expression that selects the root, such as example.org/service/orders.Submit, orders.Submit, or func:Submit & pkg:example.org/service:orders. It must select symbols: a relation (<, >, <<) or a path (>>) is rejected. The first argument and the flag are the same option.--symbolThe canonical symbol id of the root, as a node's id or a candidate's id carries it. Give a selector or a symbol, never both.--directioncallees, callers, or both (the default).--depthHow many calls away from the root the graph reaches, from 1 through 8. The default is 2.--limitThe most nodes the graph holds, from 1 through 1000. The default is 150.--excludeComma-separated package patterns whose nodes the graph leaves out. The default is std,builtin,gorm.io/...; none excludes nothing.--root, --location, --snapshotThe snapshots to read, as for uir query. With none, the checkout enclosing the working directory, else the primary head of every indexed root. --location and --snapshot are mutually exclusive.--allEvery indexed root instead of the current checkout. Cannot be combined with --root, --location, or --snapshot.--sinceA revision to compare against, which makes the graph a change query.--since-snapshotA snapshot UUID to use for --since instead of its newest clean snapshot, as uir diff --snapshot-from does. The command is a Clicky operation: --format json and --format yaml print the envelope below, and the default format prints a tree. uir serve exposes it as GET /api/v1/modules/graph with the same options as query parameters (selector, symbol, direction, depth, limit, exclude, root, location, snapshot, since, since-snapshot); exclude is one comma list, exclude=std,gorm.io/.... uir graph example.org/service/orders.Submit --direction both --depth 2 ƒ Submit example.org/service/orders orders.go:16
├── callers
│   ╰── ƒ Checkout orders.go:35
├── callees
│   ├── ƒ charge ×2 [order.Total > 0] orders.go:18
│   │   ╰── ƒ charge [order.Rush] orders.go:31 ↩ expanded elsewhere
│   ├── hook unresolved [hook != nil] orders.go:24
│   ├── ƒ Notifier.Notify orders.go:26
│   ╰── → dispatch ƒ Mail.Notify orders.go:26
╰── omitted: 1 unresolved A line is one edge: the neighbour, its package when that differs from its parent's, ×N when the edge has more than one call site, the guards and the path:line of the first site. → dispatch marks a call that reaches the neighbour through an interface method. unresolved marks a target the index could not resolve. A node is expanded once; ↩ expanded elsewhere marks every other edge that reaches a node which has neighbours of its own. The omitted: line summarises what was left out, and an excluded: line, printed when exclusion patterns left nodes out, tallies them per package, most first: excluded: fmt 3, builtin 1.
180.title: Command

181.text: The root is one function or method. A selector that matches exactly one is drawn. A selector that matches several draws nothing: the response has empty roots, nodes, and edges, the matches in candidates, and a resolve stage that counts them. Narrow the selector, or pass a candidate's id as --symbol. A selector that matches symbols but no function or method (a type, a package) is an invalid_query error, and one that matches nothing is symbol_not_found.
181.title: Choosing the root

182.text: FieldMeaningrootsThe id of the root node.nodesOne node per symbol: id (the canonical symbol id), identifier, kind (func, method, builtin, unresolved, package), label (the name within its package, Store.Save), group (the package path, or builtin for a predeclared function such as len), depth (0 for the root, negative for callers, positive for callees), in and out, and location.edgesOne edge per caller, callee, and type: id (`fromtotype), from, to, type (callordispatch), sites, and properties`.groupsThe packages of the nodes, as id and label, for a renderer that clusters by package.omittedWhat the graph leaves out: node_limit, beyond_depth, unresolved, unreadable_source, and excluded.excludeThe effective exclusion patterns: the ones given, or the defaults.packagesEvery package the walk reached, drawn or excluded: path, external, nodes, and excluded.stagesHow the request was resolved: the scope, the index coverage, the root, and the size of the graph.candidatesThe functions and methods an ambiguous selector matched.sinceThe answer of a change query; absent without --since. A node's location is where the symbol is declared: root_key, checkout_path, snapshot_id, source_id, path, line, column, and identity_key. source_id and identity_key together are the id of the same declaration in GET /api/v1/modules/browse (<source_id>:<identity_key>). A symbol declared outside the selected snapshots, such as fmt.Errorf, has no location. A symbol declared more than once, such as a function with one declaration per build tag, is located at the first by path, and properties.declarations counts them. in and out count a node's incoming and outgoing edges in the index, not only the edges drawn, so the difference from the edges drawn is how many more there are to expand. They are totals only in the direction the graph was walked: out for the root and its callees, in for the root and its callers. In the other direction they count the edges drawn. Edges to excluded nodes are not counted. An edge's sites are its call sites in order of path, line, and column. A site has path, line, column, text (the whole call as written, arguments included, channel.Send(order.Kind)), and guards. A site in a file listed in omitted.unreadable_source keeps the callee as the index recorded it, channel.Send, because the call cannot be read back. An edge's properties are string facts its source knows beyond the sites, such as the configurations that select a dispatch target; the Go index sets none, and the key is absent when there are none. When several steps of a source fold into one edge, the first non-empty properties are kept. A dispatch edge runs from a caller to a method that implements the interface method the caller calls. The same site therefore appears on two edges: the call edge to the interface method, and a dispatch edge to each implementation in the selected snapshots. A call the index could not resolve, such as a call of a function value, is an edge to an unresolved node. Its id names the caller, because two callers' unresolved calls of one name are not known to be one target. A call made outside any declaration, in a package-level variable initialiser, is an edge from a package node.
182.title: What the graph holds

183.text: A site's guards are the conditions that must hold for control to reach the call, outermost first, as plain text. A site with no guards is reached whenever its function runs. The call is inGuardan if bodythe conditionan else blockthe condition negated, !(a && b)an else if bodythe earlier conditions negated, then its owna tagged switch casetag == value, joined with || for a case with several valuesa tagless switch casethe case expressiona default clausethe negated disjunction of every other casea case reached by fallthroughits own condition or the condition of the case that falls into ita type switch casex.(type) == Ta select casethe communication as written, value := <-ch, or defaulta for body or post statementthe loop condition A call in an if condition or init statement, a switch tag, a case's own value list, or a for init or condition is not guarded by that statement. A for with no condition and a range loop add no guard. A function literal keeps the guards around it. Negation is not simplified: the else of if !ok is !!ok. Guards are syntax, not proof. They are the conditions of the statements written around the call, read without type information, so err != nil is the text of the condition and nothing is evaluated. An early return above a call is not a guard on it, and neither is the left operand of && or || on a call in the right operand. The source of a site is read as GET /api/v1/modules/content reads it: the local file when its hash still matches the snapshot, else the stored blob, else the pinned Git blob. When none can be recovered, or the source does not parse, the file is listed in omitted.unreadable_source, a guards stage names the first failure, and the file's sites carry no guards and only the callee as their text. Their edges are still drawn.
183.title: Guards

184.text: Calls into the standard library, builtins, and database layers crowd out the calls a reader follows, so by default the graph leaves them out. --exclude (exclude over HTTP) takes a comma list of patterns, and the list given replaces the defaults: PatternMatchesstdthe standard librarybuiltinGo's predeclared functions, len, append, panic, whose group is builtinexternalevery package outside the modules in the query scope: the standard library, builtins, and dependenciesexample.org/libthat package onlyexample.org/lib/...that package and every package below it, as a Go package patternnonenothing; it must be the only pattern With no patterns the defaults std,builtin,gorm.io/... apply. An excluded node is not drawn, walked, or counted in in and out, and omitted.excluded counts the distinct excluded nodes per package. A node that only a node at the depth bound reaches is not counted there, nor in beyond_depth. The root is never excluded, even when its package is: its package's other nodes are. packages lists every package the walk reached, drawn or excluded, ordered by nodes (drawn and excluded nodes together), most first, then by path. external marks a package outside the modules in the query scope, which the external pattern matches, and excluded a package the effective patterns match. A viewer builds its package filter from this list, so an excluded package can be switched back on. A pattern that is empty, repeated, a glob such as gorm.io/*, a ... anywhere but a trailing /..., or none beside another pattern is an invalid_query error.
184.title: Excluding packages

185.text: The graph is breadth-first from the root, to depth calls and limit nodes. omitted.beyond_depth counts the nodes at the depth bound that have neighbours further out. Raise --depth, or draw the graph of one of them.omitted.node_limit is true when nodes were left out because the limit was reached. Nodes nearer the root are kept first.omitted.unresolved counts the call sites on edges to unresolved nodes.A node at the depth bound is still asked for its neighbours, so its edges to nodes already in the graph are drawn, and recursion and calls back towards the root are visible.Callees are walked from the root and its callees, callers from the root and its callers. A caller's other callees and a callee's other callers are not part of the graph. Only the selected snapshots contribute edges. Callers in a module that is not indexed are absent, and dispatch reaches only the implementations in the selected snapshots. The stages entry named coverage reports packages that are partially indexed; a call graph over them is incomplete in the same way a query is. uir graph <symbol> --direction callers --depth N and uir query '<symbol> <<N' walk the same caller edges. The query returns rows with a depth and fails beyond 10000 symbols; the graph returns nodes, edges, and guards, and truncates at --limit.
185.title: Limits

186.text:
--since <rev> asks whether anything in the root's call graph changed between <rev> and the selected snapshot. The revision resolves in the root's registered checkouts as one side of uir diff does, and selects that commit's newest clean snapshot (or --since-snapshot). The scope must hold exactly one snapshot of the same root, indexed under the same configuration hash. The walk is the ordinary graph walk over callees: --direction defaults to callees and any other direction is an invalid_query error. uir graph example.org/chain.A --since v1.4.0 --depth 6 ƒ A example.org/chain chain.go:11
├── callees
│   ├── ƒ B chain.go:12
│   │   ╰── ƒ C changed: body chain.go:16
│   ╰── ...
╰── changed since v1.4.0
    ╰── body C: A → B → C The root is walked in both snapshots with the same depth, node limit, access and exclusion options. The top-level graph remains the selected snapshot's graph; since.before holds the earlier graph, including removed nodes and their source locations. A newly added root has no earlier graph. Other roots in the scope stay pinned to the same selected snapshots in both walks. The changed set is computed from storage.EffectiveSymbols of both snapshots, by symbol handle: a symbol that is new is added, one whose public fingerprint differs signature, private fingerprint structure, content fingerprint body, and one that is gone removed. A changed symbol reached in either walk is reported with a shortest path in that snapshot. Added and removed edge identities are reported separately, so losing an interface dispatch target is a change even when the implementation method's own fingerprints did not change. A node of a module-cache dependency whose selection in snapshot_dependencies changed (selected version, replacement, or resolved target snapshot) is dependency-version, because dependencies have no per-symbol facts. When either walk reached such a dependency through a package the exclusions leave out, the dependency is listed with excluded: true; rerun with --exclude none to see where it is entered. since fieldMeaningrevision, from_snapshot_id, to_snapshot_idWhat was compared.changedTrue when either walk reached a changed symbol, an edge was added or removed, or a changed dependency was reached through an excluded package.beforeThe earlier bounded graph, absent when the root was added. Its omitted field reports that walk's limits.nodesEach changed node reached in either snapshot: id, reason, snapshot_id, module (for dependency-version), and path, the node ids of a shortest walk from the root, root first.edgesEach added or removed edge: id, reason (added or removed), snapshot_id, and path from the root through the edge's destination.symbolsThe root's changed symbols counted by reason, reached or not.dependenciesEvery dependency whose selection changed: module, from, to, excluded. A change's snapshot_id identifies whether its node, edge and path belong to the top-level graph or since.before. A since stage summarises the counts and says when either walk stopped at its depth or node limit. Edge changes describe these bounded walks; raising a limit can reveal more changes. The answer is only as complete as the call edges the index records, so changed: false is not a proof. Known false negatives: an implementation outside the import closure of the interface it satisfies gets no dispatch edge;dispatch through generic or type-set interfaces is not recorded;calls through method values, and through func-typed fields or variables, produce no call edge (they are unresolved nodes at best);changes beyond --depth or --limit, behind an unresolved call, in another root of the scope, or in the Go toolchain's standard library are not reported.
186.title: Changes since a revision

187.text: The graph package knows nothing about Go. A frontend for another language, or for business rules held outside source files, draws the same graph by implementing graph.Source: MethodReturnsDescribe(ctx, id)The node for an id; an id the source does not know is an error.Out(ctx, id)One graph.Step per call or data access the node makes: the neighbour Node, and an Edge with its Type (call, dispatch, read or write), Kind, Sites and Properties.In(ctx, id)One step per call made to the node, in the same shape. graph.Build(ctx, source, roots, graph.Options{Direction, Depth, Limit, Exclude, Access, Theme}) walks it and returns the graph.Graph envelope described above; Build sets each edge's ID, From and To, merges steps to one neighbour of one type, and bounds, orders and counts the result. A node with Unresolved set is a leaf that is never asked for its neighbours. Nothing in Options is defaulted. An edge's type is not limited to calls: a source may report read and write edges to the data a body accesses. Options.Access lists the types Build follows (graph.Follows): a step of any other type is not drawn, counted in in and out, or walked, call also follows dispatch, and an empty list follows every type. graph.ParseAccess reads the call, read and write values a request names, comma-separated and in any case, into that list, and returns an empty list, every type, when they name none. Build refuses an entry that is not a uir.RelationshipType. graph.FromRelationships serves call, dispatch, read and write relationships, so Access chooses among them.
187.title: Custom sources

188.text: HelperDoesgraph.FromResolver(resolver)Serves a graph.Resolver (Describe, References, Referrers) whose edges are references made by name. A reference's Resolution draws a call to the one target of a static name, a dispatch to each implementation of a dynamic name (its Properties naming what selects it) and to each candidate of an ambiguous one (with status: ambiguous), and a call to the unresolved:<kind>:<name> leaf (graph.UnresolvedID) of an unresolved one. Reference.Steps and Reference.EdgeTo are the same mapping for a source that lists references itself.graph.Absorb(source, absorbedInto)Folds structural nodes into their parent. Among callees, a step to an absorbed node is replaced in place by that node's own callees, each site drawn once; among callers, an absorbed node is drawn as the node its parent id describes. Absorbed nodes whose callees absorb one another are a cycle, and an error.graph.FoldMembers(steps, graph.Folding{MemberOf, Owner, Fold})Folds the data steps of one body into one per node and type. Folding (the columns toggle off) draws a member, such as a column or field, as its owner, the edge listing the members in its Member.Property; drawn apart, an owner's site that a covering member stands for on the same line is left out. Each returned Folded names the input steps it stands for, and members of one owner listed under different properties are an error. graph.Surviving names the steps drawn apart before any is folded, for a source that names a node only once it is drawn.graph.FillGuards(graph, guards)Sets every positioned site's guards from a function of the edge and site; a site whose source is unreadable (graph.ErrUnreadableSource) keeps the guards its source gave it and is listed in omitted.unreadable_source.graph.ExcludeKindsGroups(kinds, groups)An Options.Exclude matching node kinds and groups case-insensitively and whole, with * wildcards, comma-separated lists and ! negations as collections.MatchItems reads them.graph.DataID, graph.SplitDataID, graph.SplitMember, graph.IsDataKindData node ids: table:, column:, procedure:, sqlfunction:, entity: and field: followed by the name, which clicky-ui's CallGraph reads to tell data from code. A column's table is before its last dot, a field's entity before its first.graph.FilterThe flags and query parameters every call-graph route spells alike (direction, depth, limit, access, columns), as clicky-ui's CallGraphFetchParams sends them; Filter.Options() turns them into Options. The exclusion and guard flags name a frontend's own kinds, groups and conditions, so a route declares them with its own help.graph.Cache (Load), graph.Params, graph.CachedStore built graphs under the canonical encoding of their request and inputs (Params.Encode, keyed by graph.ParamsKey); Cached serves a stored result or builds and stores one. Graph.Pretty() draws the result as the tree shown under Command. A node's name is its label, after the icon and in the colour of its Kind when that is a UIR node type; Graph.Tree(graph.TreeOptions{Name: ...}) draws it with a renderer of the frontend's own, which is how uir graph adds the Go symbol icons.
188.title: Helpers for a custom source

189.text: Over HTTP an invalid request returns 400 with code: "invalid_query", a message, and a hint: a depth, limit, or direction out of range, an exclusion pattern it cannot match, neither or both of selector and symbol, a selector that does not parse or selects no function or method, or a symbol id that names something else. A selector or symbol id that is not in the selected index returns 404 with code: "symbol_not_found".
189.title: Errors

190.text:
External producers can publish a resolved Git commit without changing the current location head. Create a publication JSON using the publication format and examples. Set PUBLICATION to its path, COMMIT to the full ID resolved in the source repository with git rev-parse HEAD^{commit}, and PRODUCER to a fingerprint identifying the producer executable and effective lowering configuration. Supply options.historical, options.git_commit and options.producer in the publication JSON, or pass those values as flags: mkdir -p .tmp
uir --dsn .tmp/history.db import "$PUBLICATION" --historical --git-commit "$COMMIT" --producer "$PRODUCER" git_commit is a full lowercase SHA-1 or SHA-256 Git object ID. producer identifies the executable and effective lowering configuration. Missing historical identity, unresolved commit names and conflicting flag/publication metadata are rejected. The zero-value options publish a current head. Matching historical requests reuse a retained snapshot when commit, revision, content, producer configuration, context, dependencies and coverage match. A changed producer fingerprint invalidates reuse. Publication records a delta from the current head when one exists while preserving that head and its version. A location created only through historical publication has no current head: location listings omit head metadata, and the snapshot browser and explicit snapshot queries can read its retained history. Producer sources can combine or transform Git files. External source bytes therefore remain in UIR's source blob store; their commit identity does not imply that a corresponding source file can be reconstructed directly from Git. The OIPA offline producer resolves and archives committed rules, lowers them through its existing filesystem VFS, and atomically publishes modules plus a complete catalog manifest: oipa-cli symbols index --dir /path/to/rules-repository --revision HEAD --dsn .tmp/rules.db
oipa-cli symbols index --dir /path/to/rules-repository --revision HEAD~1 --historical --dsn .tmp/rules.db It fingerprints its executable and effective OIPA configuration by default; --producer supplies a producer identity that is still combined with the configuration. --memprofile writes a heap profile; global CPU and execution-trace flags support profiling. The command runs offline without initializing the live environment database. Its generated HTTP action requires administrator permission because it reads server files and writes a caller-selected output database. Sources and embedded source locations are relative to the archived repository root, including when --dir selects a subtree. Temporary archive directory names do not participate in source or document identity, so unchanged committed sources can reuse their stored revisions across archive extractions. Complete historical manifests are reused before lowering. New current catalogs retire heads for roots they no longer contain. All catalog changes and automatic pruning share one transaction; a failed manifest write rolls back every module. Automatic pruning keeps historical snapshots, while explicit pruning can remove them according to the requested retention count. For the real-corpus Gavel replay, see the snapshot benchmark runner.
190.title: Historical external snapshots

191.text: Universal Intermediate Representation is a language-agnostic model for describing code: modules, packages, types, methods, records, tables, endpoints, and the statements inside method bodies. Extractors emit UIR; generators and analysers consume it. The Go package is the canonical model, with parallel Python and Java ports. The CLI indexes Go modules into immutable snapshots so you can navigate symbols, trace call relationships, and compare revisions.
191.title: UIR

192.text: Getting started: install the CLI and index a local module.Module indexing: manage module roots, snapshots, and non-Go publications.Compact queries and SQL navigation: find symbols and follow relationships.Call graphs: explore callers, callees, and the guards around calls.Symbol diffs: compare code structure across Git commits.Browser and API: browse saved snapshots and use the HTTP endpoints.
192.title: Start here

193.text: import "github.com/flanksource/uir" The model reference covers nodes, statements, builders, identifiers, and serialization. Symbols and references explains identity and reference resolution; storage describes persisted snapshots and the database schema.
193.title: Use the model

194.text: Benchmarks records measured indexing and query performance. Additional design records live in the repository and retain their original implementation or proposal status.
194.title: Design and performance

195.text:
uir add [path] discovers and immediately indexes Go modules; uir reindex [path] refreshes an already registered module location. Both load packages with go/packages, use go/types for proven symbol identities and references, and retain syntax facts from go/ast when typed extraction is incomplete. They publish immutable, module-root snapshots. See module-root indexing for commands, scope flags, dependency indexing, and the storage hierarchy. uir add .
uir add ./internal/service
uir reindex .
uir reindex ../service-feature --force A path inside a package is resolved to its nearest enclosing go.mod and the entire module is scanned. Adding a directory discovers every visible nested module under it; nested module files are excluded from their parent's source set. In Git checkouts, discovery includes tracked and nonignored untracked files. Directory symlinks, hidden and underscore-prefixed directories, vendor, and testdata are not traversed. Tests are excluded unless --include-tests is set. uir add stays within the requested directory. uir add --all also selects modules named by an enclosing go.work outside it. Local dependencies required by a selected module are indexed through dependency resolution in either case. A module that an enclosing go.work does not use is loaded with GOWORK=off. For each module, indexing resolves its full go.mod module path as logical root key and canonicalizes the physical location. It records parent location and mount path for nested modules; .gitmodules distinguishes a declared submodule from other nested modules. A Git worktree's .git file is accepted as a repository marker. Multiple checkouts of the same module path share logical root identity but maintain separate heads.
195.title: Incremental Go indexing

196.text: Discover modules and included .go paths, capture Git revision and build configuration, and hash source bytes and dependency manifests.Resolve dependencies and compare package inputs with the previous head, or the primary head for a new location. Reuse unchanged analysis; finish package loading and document extraction before opening the publication transaction.Verify inputs have not changed, then publish source revisions, content-addressed documents, postings, coverage, dependency links, and source, document, and symbol deltas. Unchanged bindings inherit from the base snapshot; deleted paths receive tombstones.Write the immutable snapshot and advance the location's head with a version-checked update in the same transaction. A publication error rolls back that transaction; dependencies already published in separate calls remain available. An unchanged run reuses its head when revision, source and manifest hashes, configuration, package context, and dependency set still match. --force re-extracts and verifies documents and publishes a new snapshot. A revision-only snapshot can have no file delta. Readers start from a location head or an explicit snapshot and reconstruct effective sources, documents, and symbols by walking its base chain newest first. A snapshot exists only after publication commits; there is no building or failed snapshot state. No automatic snapshot compaction or retention policy exists.
196.title: Snapshot lifecycle

197.text: Documents record declarations, signatures, visibility, source ranges, layered hashes, identifier occurrences, calls, writes, and embedding facts. Typed declarations receive canonical symbol IDs; local bindings and unresolved targets keep their positions without invented identities. File and callable metrics are stored alongside documents for SQL queries. Symbols and references explains display, identity, and call locators. CoverageAvailable factsindexedThe package type-checked without diagnostics; declarations and references have proven identities.partialType checking or an individual document failed; only proven typed facts are recorded, with diagnostics.syntaxThe package could not be type-checked, or syntax analysis was explicitly selected; AST declarations and call locators remain, without canonical IDs or postings.excludedBuild constraints exclude the file under the recorded variant; an empty document records the reason. A file that cannot be parsed is published as an empty document with a uir/index warning; its package's other parseable files retain syntax facts and uir/coverage diagnostics. Load and type errors remain visible in CLI warnings and query coverage. Database failures, changed inputs, cross-document invariant failures, and recognized dependency-download or filesystem failures stop indexing instead of publishing misleading coverage. Build selection uses the recorded GOOS, GOARCH, CGO_ENABLED, toolchain, and GOFLAGS. Lint analysis also accepts explicit build tags through uir lint --tags; add and reindex have no --tags flag. Dirty and non-Git snapshots store source blobs; clean snapshots can retrieve pinned Git blobs. The browser verifies every source's SHA-256 before displaying it. Queries traverse recorded facts within selected indexed snapshots. Interface dispatch uses recorded implementation facts; dynamic calls and dependencies outside that scope are not whole-program proof. An ambiguous selector returns candidates rather than choosing a declaration arbitrarily, and an empty result under incomplete coverage is inconclusive. Use uir query 'service.Run <' --root example.org/service to inspect references and callers, and uir query 'service.Run :uses' --root example.org/service for resolved symbols used by its own body. Unresolved calls remain available through outgoing call queries (>), while :uses requires resolved targets. See the query guide for grammar and scoping.
197.title: Extracted facts and coverage

198.text: uir lint selects syntax or typed analysis from each rule's SQL requirements. Syntax analysis reads declarations, metrics, and build headers without loading imported packages; typed rules load the selected module's type information. Analysis heads are stored separately from normal index heads and do not advance them. --no-index requires matching, fresh analysis; --snapshot evaluates explicit historical facts. See SQL architecture linting for configuration, build tags, and changed/staged sources.
198.title: Lint analysis

199.text:
The request-state example rejects package-level variables of the exact request-scoped context, configuration, runtime and database types used by OIPA's Ruleguard rule. It uses symbol.type, including inferred types and aliases, and preserves each variable name's source location. Run uir lint --config lint/testdata/request-state/.uir.yaml with an isolated database to inspect the example. The example is a self-contained module; use GOWORK=off when running it from this development workspace. Incomplete typed coverage or missing type facts fail this rule's query rather than silently passing it. uir lint executes rules from .uir.yaml. Each SQL row becomes a Gavel violation with its original source location, even when the SELECT list only contains metric values. Queries can combine metrics with the existing definitions, callers, callees, reads, writes and implementation navigation functions. Copy the runnable example to your project root as .uir.yaml. It flags files with fewer than 100 lines and three definitions, functions with more than three parameters, and bodies longer than 50 lines. uir lint
uir lint --all
uir lint --rule too-many-parameters --format json --no-progress
uir lint --config path/to/.uir.yaml --no-index
uir lint --config path/to/.uir.yaml --snapshot SNAPSHOT_ID
uir lint --include 'cmd/**' --exclude '**/*_test.go'
uir lint --exclude function-parameters
uir lint --exclude function-parameters --group-by symbol
uir lint --group-by file --format json
uir lint --changed
uir lint --changed HEAD~3..HEAD
uir lint --changed main...HEAD --group-by symbol
uir lint --staged
uir lint --tags integration,feature --tags accepts repeated or comma-separated Go build tags. Tags select files for syntax analysis and typed loading and participate in analysis freshness checks; changing tags requires fresh analysis before --no-index can reuse it. Explicit snapshots already fix their build configuration and reject --tags. When running through Gavel, gavel lint uir --generated=false --tags integration,feature also suppresses generated-file findings while retaining generated source for type resolution. Configuration discovery merges home configuration first, then configuration from the filesystem root down to the current directory, including ancestors above the Git root. Each directory loads .uir.yaml followed by the .yaml and .yml files directly inside .uir.d/ in filename order. Home configuration includes both ~/.uir.yaml and ~/.uir.d/ and is loaded once. Hidden files and other extensions inside .uir.d/ are ignored. Each fragment uses the same complete version 1 document shape as .uir.yaml. Rules merge by id: a later file replaces the complete rule definition, while other inherited rules remain in their original order. lint.include_tests inherits when omitted; an explicit true or false overrides it. Every unexpired discovered file is validated, including overridden rules. --config selects one explicit file without inheritance. An optional top-level _expires accepts an RFC3339 timestamp, for example _expires: "2026-10-22T12:00:00Z". During configuration loading, UIR deletes a file whose timestamp has passed and does not validate or merge its rules. Future-dated files load normally and remain on disk; files without _expires are persistent. Invalid timestamps and deletion failures stop the run with the file path. Expiration is checked before analysis, not continuously during execution. If every configuration has expired, lint reports that no unexpired configuration exists. The nearest configuration inside the repository defines the project root for file filters. A fragment's project root is the directory containing .uir.d/, not .uir.d/ itself. With only home or external ancestor configuration, lint uses the Git root, or the current directory outside Git. Outside Git, a non-home ancestor configuration defines the project root. An explicit file defines its own project root. Discovery follows ancestors of the invocation directory; it does not recursively load configurations below it. Analysis selects the enclosing Go module at the invocation directory, or at the explicit configuration's directory with --config. Running in a package subdirectory still analyzes its whole enclosing module. Nested modules are separate and require explicit selection. A directory without an enclosing go.mod fails with an actionable error. --all selects every registered module's primary location, applies the selected configuration to all of them, and pins their snapshots into one combined query scope. Register modules with uir add first. Cross-module callers, callees and other navigation can then traverse those selected modules. External producer locations use their existing snapshots. Under --all, include/exclude file patterns are relative to each module. --all cannot combine with --changed, --staged or --snapshot; it supports --no-index. Version 1 accepts version, optional _expires, lint.include_tests (default false) and lint.rules. Every unexpired file requires at least one rule with a unique id, SQL query and nonempty message. Severity is error by default, or warning or info. The IDs uir/coverage and uir/index are reserved for index warnings. Unknown fields, duplicate YAML keys, extra documents, invalid queries and invalid templates fail validation. For shared rules, save this as ~/.uir.yaml: version: 1
lint:
  include_tests: true
  rules:
    - id: function-parameters
      query: SELECT symbol.name AS name FROM func:* WHERE symbol.metrics.param_count > 3
      message: '{{.name}} has too many parameters'
      severity: warning Save a project-specific replacement as .uir.yaml in the project root, then run uir lint there: version: 1
lint:
  include_tests: false
  rules:
    - id: function-parameters
      query: SELECT symbol.name AS name FROM func:* WHERE symbol.metrics.param_count > 4
      message: '{{.name}} exceeds the project parameter limit'
      severity: error The project now checks its four-parameter limit without test files. Other home rules still run. Put another .uir.yaml in a subdirectory and run uir lint from that directory to apply its overrides to the enclosing module. Use file filters to restrict findings to a subtree. Use uir lint --config .uir.yaml to run only the project file. --exclude disables exact configured rule IDs before execution, including rules selected with --rule. Other exclusion values and all --include values filter reported file paths relative to the project root, or each module with --all. Repeat either flag or comma-separate values; rule IDs and file globs can be mixed, for example --exclude 'function-parameters,**/*_test.go'. Exact rule IDs take precedence over file paths with the same name. Includes are alternatives; exclusions take precedence. File patterns use the SQL MATCH syntax: * stays within a path segment, ? matches one character, ** matches zero or more segments, and /... abbreviates /**. Quote globs to prevent shell expansion. Invalid globs fail before opening the database. File filters apply after querying the selected module scope, so excluding a callee's file does not hide a violation in an included caller.
