Fileless coverage warnings are always retained when rules run. Excluding every selected rule succeeds with zero rules and skips analysis and queries. The repository's .uir.example also provides guideline-based warnings, including command files over its configured size threshold and Cobra references outside any cmd/ path segment. The command size threshold is a configurable heuristic for moving business logic into backend packages. Cobra detection uses canonical target package identities, so import aliases do not bypass it; it requires typed reference facts. The example also includes hack-build-tag, a warning for indexed .go files under root or nested hack/ directories whose modern build expression does not require hack. It accepts compound expressions such as hack && linux, but flags missing headers, legacy-only headers, ignore, !hack, and hack || linux. The query explicitly includes build-excluded files, so an unsuitable constraint or filename suffix cannot hide the file. Paths inside SQL remain module-relative. This rule reads snapshot-verified source headers and reports an execution error if the indexed bytes are unavailable; it never adds tags automatically. See build-constraint queries for semantics and cold-query cost. Run the self-contained hack build-tag example from this repository root: make binary
GOWORK=off .bin/uir --dsn .tmp/hack-build-tag-example.db lint --config lint/testdata/hack-build-tags/.uir.yaml --rule hack-build-tag --format json --no-progress The fixture deliberately includes violations and reports eight warnings, including an excluded platform file, a test file and a nested hack directory. myhack/ and files that require hack do not produce findings. Warning-only runs exit zero. Use gavel fixtures fixtures/hack-build-tag.md for executable acceptance. Messages use Go text/template with SELECT aliases as map keys. For example, SELECT symbol.name AS name exposes {{.name}}. Use {{index . "symbol.name"}} for an unaliased dotted column. Missing keys accessed by name fail execution. Rules return every matching row: explicit LIMIT and terminal graph()/path() results are rejected. The interactive query limit does not apply to lint. Lint infers analysis requirements from the selected SQL rules. File metrics, build headers and direct callable metric queries use syntax analysis without loading Go packages or resolving imported modules. Type fields, canonical identities, references, relationships and navigation functions use typed analysis. Typed analysis loads imported type information to resolve the current module's facts; it publishes documents only for the selected module and never recursively indexes dependencies. Normal uir add and uir reindex retain their existing dependency indexing behavior. Syntax and typed snapshots have separate persisted analysis heads and do not advance normal index heads. Repeated runs reuse unchanged analysis, including dirty checkouts, without loading packages or publishing another snapshot. Reuse validates source bytes, manifests, build options, test selection and the indexer version. Typed reuse also validates imported local package source and workspace module manifests; changes in unrelated workspace package source do not invalidate it. --no-index requires fresh analysis of each needed mode and fails explicitly when it is missing or stale. It never publishes snapshots. --snapshot selects historical indexed facts and skips freshness checks; combine it with the configuration that should evaluate that history. The two flags are mutually exclusive. Mixed configurations execute syntax rules before typed rules, then restore configuration order in the report. A typed-analysis failure preserves completed syntax findings. --changed reports tracked differences from HEAD plus nonignored untracked paths while analyzing the live checkout. An optional commit or range selects an immutable source: a single commit compares with its first parent (or the empty tree for an initial commit), A..B compares endpoints and analyzes B, and A...B compares the unique merge base with B and analyzes B. Omitted range endpoints mean HEAD. --staged analyzes the exact captured index, including its staged .uir.yaml and module manifests; later staged or unstaged edits cannot alter that capture. Conflicted indexes fail explicitly. Both modes require a local Git checkout. Changed paths intersect the normal include/exclude filters. Analysis retains the full module context, findings retain original checkout paths, and grouping and the exit verdict use only the filtered findings. Deletions remain part of the selection and renames are deletion/addition pairs. A selection with no reportable paths succeeds without opening the database or indexing; it never becomes an unrestricted run. Fileless coverage warnings remain when a selected run executes. A manifest or configuration change selects that path; it does not automatically widen the selection to every Go file. Git source preparation belongs to commons-db/git. Bare --changed requires Git 2.45 or newer to disable lazy object fetching explicitly. Pinned source trees are materialized under project .tmp/, with raw Git blob bytes and no checkout filters or LFS hydration. Unsafe symlinks and gitlinks fail explicitly. Commit and staged snapshots publish historically under original checkout locations and do not advance saved checkout heads. Staged snapshots use the captured tree ID as their revision and store their source bytes. Pinned extraction follows historical indexing's isolated Go configuration: GOWORK=off and local replacements removed from a temporary module manifest, so it cannot borrow mutable external checkout replacements. --config names a path in the selected repository; pinned modes load its captured contents rather than the current file. Without --config, discovery merges captured ancestor configurations up to the selected source root, excluding home and mutable external ancestors. Bare --changed uses normal home and ancestor inheritance from the live checkout. --changed and --staged are mutually exclusive. Neither combines with --snapshot. Bare --changed supports --no-index; commit/range and staged sources require indexing and reject --no-index. A positional revision without --changed fails before database access. The shared Gavel linter runner provides execution timeout, metadata, violation filtering and failure verdicts directly in-process; this command does not invoke gavel lint uir. Every diagnostic of a package that is not fully indexed is a warning on its file (fileless when the toolchain gave no file), grouped with that file's findings and scoped by --changed and --staged like them: uir/coverage for a load or type error, uir/index for a file whose own document failed and was indexed degraded (from its syntax only, or as an empty document) so the rest of the module still indexes; rules continue against available facts. Intentional syntax analysis has no load diagnostics, so it reports only uir/index warnings. A typed rule against an explicit syntax snapshot fails rather than silently returning no rows. Missing required metrics, catalog binding errors, analysis failures and message failures are execution errors. Findings completed before an execution failure remain in the JSON report. File-level findings have no invented line or column. --group-by symbol|file groups findings for review. File grouping is the default display. Symbol grouping combines findings from different rules under the declaration owning the source location; call and relationship findings belong to the caller/source symbol, independently of the SQL projection. Groups use module, file and declaration span, so syntax and typed findings for the same declaration combine while identically named declarations stay distinct. Syntax findings carry a declaration witness without an invented canonical symbol ID. Findings without a symbol appear under file findings, and fileless coverage warnings appear under run diagnostics. Grouping preserves every finding, its severity and location, and the command's exit status. Explicit grouping also adds group_by and a groups array to JSON when findings exist; each group contains file, optional declaration_key, symbol_id and symbol, and violations. The flat violations array remains available for Gavel consumers. Omitting the flag preserves the standard report JSON. Error findings and execution failures exit nonzero. Warnings and info alone exit zero. JSON output is an array containing the Gavel LinterResult fields, including success, error, duration, violations, file_count and rule_count. success describes execution, so an error-severity finding may appear in a successful report while the command exits nonzero. Gavel discovers global and project UIR configuration and runs the installed uir binary as a native linter. Use gavel lint uir for Gavel snapshots, baselines, summaries and UI. Native documents configured through lint.linters.uir.config in .gavel.yaml are written into a unique project .uir.d/gavel-*.yaml fragment with a deadline-based _expires, then removed when execution finishes. UIR performs configuration validation and merging; Gavel does not import the UIR library. Analysis runs with the selected module context; a normal file scope filters reported findings afterward. Changing .uir.yaml or a .uir.d/ fragment reports the full owning module. Fileless run warnings survive file scopes. The Gavel report APIs and commons-db prepared-source APIs are available in the released dependencies pinned in go.mod. A sibling checkout is optional for development. Use GOWORK=off make build to validate those published dependencies independently of a local workspace. To run the included sample against an isolated database: make binary
GOWORK=off .bin/uir --dsn .tmp/lint-example.db lint --config lint/testdata/project/.uir.yaml --format json --no-progress The sample reports one warning and one parameter-count error. GOWORK=off selects the sample's own module rather than the repository's development workspace. To see a warning-only successful run, add --rule small-files. A repeat run reuses the index of an unchanged checkout but evaluates every selected rule again. Reusing each rule's findings while the symbols it read are unchanged is planned in Lint findings as generation-gated facts.
199.title: SQL architecture linting

200.text:
The root-level uir commands index Go modules. A module path from go.mod is the stable root key; a canonical filesystem path is a location of that root, not its identity. Two clones or worktrees declaring the same module path share a root but have independent location heads. The first registered location remains the primary location, and uir query reads its head by default. uir add .
uir list
uir get example.org/service
uir reindex .
uir dependencies --snapshot 6f8b2c6e-79af-4b59-8736-e45696f0c546
uir query 'service.Run =' --root example.org/service
uir query 'service.Run <' --root example.org/service --location ../service-feature
uir query 'service.Run =' --snapshot 6f8b2c6e-79af-4b59-8736-e45696f0c546 uir add [path] defaults to . and indexes immediately. Discovery follows these rules: A directory scan finds every visible go.mod beneath it, including nested modules without a separate .git marker.A package directory selects its nearest enclosing go.mod and scans the whole module. Nested modules' files are excluded from their parent module's scan.In a Git checkout, discovery includes tracked and non-ignored untracked files, respecting nested .gitignore rules and repository excludes. Outside Git, it scans the filesystem.A nested location records its nearest parent and mount path; .gitmodules provenance marks a declared submodule.Symlinked input paths are canonicalized, but discovery does not traverse directory symlinks. add indexes only the selected directory; add --all also adds the use paths of an enclosing go.work that lie outside it, and fails on a missing or invalid use path. A module below a go.work that does not use it is loaded on its own, with GOWORK=off, as the Go toolchain requires. uir reindex [path] accepts only previously registered module locations and uses the same extractor. uir reindex --all indexes only registered Go checkouts without heads, in parent-first order, and skips external roots, which only their producer refreshes; it does not accept a path or --force and stops on an unavailable or failed checkout. --include-tests includes _test.go files; --force re-extracts every file, fails if a stored document differs from the fresh extraction under the same indexer version, and publishes a new snapshot even when the content is unchanged. Each new snapshot records the root's go.mod requirements, including indirect ones, their declared replacements and Go-selected versions, and the exact target snapshot when one can be resolved. Indexing a requirement through a local go.work module or directory replacement also registers and indexes that target, including during reindex; the workspace flags above still control bulk addition of unrelated go.work use modules. Local dependency cycles publish their member snapshots and cross-links together, and a changed member causes a new linked set. A versioned target is indexed from a matching tag or pseudo-version commit in an already registered local checkout; cycles among registered tagged versions likewise publish their snapshots and links together without moving checkout heads. UIR does not fetch Git remotes. Missing selected versions, tags, or checkouts leave an explicit unresolved edge. Historical commits use standalone module resolution and ignore current workspaces and local directory replacements; failed package loading retains parseable source with syntax coverage and dependency diagnostics. Every snapshot records coverage_deterministic: whether extracting the same commit, configuration and dependency set again must reach the same coverage. It is true when the whole go/packages load ran and every error of every package it loaded, dependencies included, is a parse or type error, or a list error proving an import absent from the commit's pinned, already fetched module versions or the toolchain's standard library (import lookup disabled by -mod=readonly, no required module provides package, is not in std, and the like), and every dependency edge is resolved or unresolved for a reason module selection or version registration decides. A whole-load failure, an unknown error, an unrecognised list error, any error naming a network, proxy, checksum-database, module-cache or file-system failure, and an edge whose module selection failed or whose local directory could not be resolved are not deterministic: classification fails closed. A list error of any loaded package that names one of those infrastructure failures (for example one module download failing with dial tcp, a proxy 502 Bad Gateway, a checksum mismatch or permission denied) fails the index with an error naming the package and the message, and publishes nothing: a transient failure is never cached as coverage. An unknown or unrecognised error without such text still publishes, marked not deterministic. Rows published before the column existed are null and count as not deterministic; nothing backfills them. A snapshot's coverage is settled when it is complete (indexed or excluded) or degraded and marked deterministic; that one rule decides both the historical and the versioned-dependency reuse below. A historical commit whose stored clean snapshot under the same configuration and dependency set hash has settled coverage is reused without type-checking, and a versioned dependency whose stored snapshot has settled coverage and a complete closure is linked without checking its version out. Otherwise the commit is extracted, and a stored snapshot identical to the extraction (context hash, coverage and coverage determinism) is reused instead of publishing a duplicate, so re-extracting a commit whose only snapshot predates the column publishes a classified one. The reuse-check phase counts why the early check missed, from the closest stored snapshot of the commit: miss-none (no clean snapshot of the commit), miss-configuration, miss-dependency-set, or miss-coverage (degraded and not known to be deterministic); sibling-recorded counts a snapshot that read a workspace sibling. A reused revision reports the stored snapshot's file count as both its files and its reused files. The no-extract probe uir diff --auto-index runs before starting an index task makes the same early check over the same dependency set: it links each versioned dependency to its stored version snapshot by the rule above, without checking out, indexing or publishing anything, so an indexed commit whose dependencies are all stored is reused without a task. A version that indexing would have to index first (none stored, a moved tag, an unsettled coverage or an incomplete closure) makes the dependency set differ, and the probe misses. Dirty Git-backed snapshots use git-{full commit}-dirty-{latest UTC file mtime} as their revision, including when a linked local dependency makes an otherwise clean parent dirty. git_commit separately records the raw commit. Older snapshots remain readable but report dependencies as not captured until reindexed. The Explorer Dependencies pane opens linked target snapshots directly, including historical snapshots; dirty source bytes are stored so later local edits do not change what those snapshots show. The CLI selects a nonempty --dsn, then UIR_DSN, then SQLite at ~/.config/uir/uir.db, creating the default directory if needed. Existing databases at other paths are not moved. Plain .db paths, sqlite:// URLs, and PostgreSQL DSNs are supported. See the CLI configuration reference for schema and profiling options. The database owner is storage.UirDB; its embedded HCL is applied to the selected target before queries or indexing.
200.title: Module-root indexing and queries

201.text: uir serve exposes the root-level operations as structured JSON at GET /api/v1/modules, GET /api/v1/modules/by-key/{root}, POST /api/v1/modules/add, POST /api/v1/modules/reindex, POST /api/v1/modules/import (below), and POST /api/v1/modules/query. GET /api/v1/modules/locations?root=... lists registered checkouts; GET /api/v1/modules/snapshots?root=...&location=... pages through one checkout's immutable snapshots. GET /api/v1/modules/browse?snapshot=... returns effective sources and the node projections read from their documents; GET /api/v1/modules/content?snapshot=...&path=... returns hash-verified source bytes; GET /api/v1/modules/dependencies?snapshot=... returns declared dependency edges and linked target snapshots. URL-encode full module paths and checkout paths in request parameters. Positional CLI arguments are the JSON args array; flags are JSON fields, for example {"args":["service.Run <"],"root":"example.org/service"} for a query. HTTP add takes the same all field to include an enclosing go.work's external uses. These operations use Clicky's typed result path, so HTTP clients receive data rows rather than captured terminal tables. Indexing operations appear as module-index runs at GET /api/v1/tasks and in the browser's Tasks view. The browser's Cmd+K palette searches module roots plus files and symbols in the selected snapshot. GET /api/v1/modules/heads returns a plain JSON array of each indexed checkout's current head and effective source files without symbol payloads. Symbol and typed-selector suggestions are also plain arrays; these routes do not wrap results in {items, warnings}. Registered checkouts without a head are skipped and reported by uir status (GET /api/v1/modules/status) and the Overview dashboard. The Explorer Files pane groups those heads by module, adding checkout rows when a module has multiple locations, then by source folder. Selecting a file switches the active module, checkout, and snapshot together. File and folder rows use bundled VS Code icons. See browser and API for response shapes and asynchronous index runs. The sidebar's System details dropdown shows the frontend build version, backend binary version, and live database type, version, location, and size. GET /api/v1/system/info provides the backend and database fields without exposing connection credentials. SQLite size is the live page count multiplied by page size; PostgreSQL size is pg_database_size(current_database()). make build VERSION=... and make install VERSION=... embed the same version in the frontend and backend.
201.title: Module API

202.text:
ModuleRoot (go.mod module path)
├── ModulePrimary ── primary ModuleLocation
├── ModuleLocation (canonical checkout path, parent location and mount)
│   └── ModuleLocationHead ── latest published ModuleSnapshot for that checkout
└── ModuleSnapshot (immutable, optional base snapshot)
    ├── SourceDelta (set revision or delete path)
    │   └── SourceRevision (path, content hash, and package)
    │       └── Document (content-addressed typed or syntax facts for that revision)
    ├── DocumentDelta (set document ordinal or delete path)
    ├── PackageCoverage (package input hash, export shape, and coverage diagnostics)
    ├── SnapshotDependency (go.mod requirement and optional target ModuleSnapshot)
    └── SymbolDelta (set or delete of one defined symbol, with public, private, and content fingerprints)

Symbol (canonical id, global; database-local handle numbered through SymbolModule and SymbolPackage)
└── SymbolPosting (document ordinal, role, occurrence count) modules.root_key is the full module path; name is its basename. locations uses (root_id, canonical_path) as its unique physical identity. A location head is scoped by root and location, references a snapshot of that same location, and carries a monotonically increasing version. The primary row is set once, when the first location is registered; adding a second location does not redirect default queries. Each new location bases its first snapshot on the current primary head, if one exists. A later run at the same location bases on that location's previous head, including after a branch switch. A run publishes a child snapshot unless its revision, content-set hash, configuration hash, context hash, and resolved dependency set all equal the base snapshot's; --force always publishes. The content set is the included .go files plus the dependency manifests: the module's go.mod and go.sum under their module-relative paths, and the go.work and go.work.sum of the enclosing workspace, wherever it sits, under the fixed keys go.work and go.work.sum. The manifests enter only the hash; they are never stored as source revisions. A dependency bump with unchanged Go source therefore publishes zero source deltas, while documents are reused wherever their extracted facts still match. The configuration hash covers the indexer version, test inclusion, and the build variant that go env, run in the module directory, reports for the toolchain: GOOS, GOARCH, CGO_ENABLED, GOVERSION, GOFLAGS, and an empty explicit build-tag list for normal indexing. A new variant changes the configuration and requires fresh extraction; if go env fails, indexing fails. The context hash digests every package input hash, so a different context with identical bytes also publishes. Changes to other non-Go files that do not change the Git revision are outside the snapshot trigger. A snapshot stores only changed path operations. set points to a SourceRevision keyed by root, path, content hash, package path, and any explicit Git binding. delete is a tombstone and has no revision ID. Unchanged content reuses a revision row across locations and snapshots. The extracted facts live in a document keyed by root, path, and a digest of its source revision, package, indexer version, coverage, and canonical JSON. A package input hash decides whether extraction is needed; it covers configuration, package path, source hashes, and direct imports' export shapes. Re-extracting a package does not duplicate documents whose rendering is unchanged. A package that type-checks under go/packages gets typed documents (indexed, or partial when it has type errors) with proven canonical symbol ids and symbol_postings. A package that cannot be type-checked retains syntax declarations and call locators without canonical ids or postings. A file whose own document fails is published with syntax facts or an empty document and a warning; see coverage. Each snapshot records package_coverage, its context_hash, and document bindings as document_deltas. It also records symbol_deltas: changes to its defined-symbol set and layered fingerprints, computed from changed packages. EffectiveSources, ActiveDocuments, and EffectiveSymbols reconstruct their respective views from the base chain; queries do not assume every snapshot physically contains every source, document, or symbol row. Discovery, hashing, and type-checked extraction finish before the publication transaction opens; revision, symbol, document, dependency edge, and posting writes happen inside it, as does the allocation of new symbols' handles and new documents' and the snapshot's ordinals. On PostgreSQL a publication that loses an allocation race to a concurrent writer is retried from the start, at most three times. Modules published together share that transaction: a database or invariant failure rolls back its root, location, revision, document, snapshot, and head writes. Dependencies published in earlier calls remain available. A snapshot row is written only in the transaction, after its documents, and together with its deltas and package coverage, before its location head is advanced; there is no building or failed snapshot state. Each snapshot records worktree_state: clean when its Git sources and dependency inputs match the commit, dirty when either changes, and unknown with an empty revision outside Git. Existing heads use a version-checked update; a concurrent writer changing the version makes publication fail instead of silently overwriting it. Additional go.work paths selected by uir add --all are separate indexing requests, so a later request's failure does not roll back an earlier successful publication.
202.title: Storage hierarchy

203.text: The compact PEG grammar accepts a qualified symbol followed by <, >, =, <<n, :impl, :inherits, :methods, :uses, or ~w; filters, set operators, and bounded >> call paths compose these operations. :uses lists resolved symbols that a declaration's own body reads, writes, or calls. See the query guide. --root selects a module path, --location selects one registered checkout, and --snapshot selects one historical immutable snapshot. --location and --snapshot cannot be combined. Without an explicit location or snapshot, queries read the primary head of each selected root. On the command line inside a registered checkout, an empty --root and --location default to that checkout; --all selects every registered root instead. The symbol operations resolve a spelling to canonical symbols and read the postings of those symbols in each selected snapshot's active documents. One identity declared at several heads is one target whose declarations are listed separately; if a spelling matches several identities in scope, the command returns candidate rows with their full query name, root, checkout, source position, and snapshot instead of choosing one arbitrarily. Select --location, --snapshot, or a full import path to disambiguate. Every result lists the packages in scope that are partial, syntax, or excluded, because those hold no or only some proven facts. The extractor type-checks each package with go/packages under the recorded build variant and records only what the type checker proves; a package that cannot be type-checked falls back to syntax coverage from the AST extractor, and a file that build constraints exclude gets an excluded document. It skips hidden, underscore-prefixed, vendor, and testdata directories and excludes tests unless requested. A long chain of tiny snapshots keeps writes small but makes effective-view reads traverse more ancestors; compaction and retention are not implemented. PostgreSQL is appropriate for shared writers; SQLite remains a local single-process store.
203.title: Query scope and call references

204.text:
A producer that is not the Go extractor, such as one lowering business rules from XML, publishes a symbol set it built itself, and uir query then answers over it exactly as over a Go module. uir import reads one publication, a JSON file or - for stdin, and publishes it; POST /api/v1/modules/import does the same with the publication object as the body's publication field. Go callers use indexer.Publish(ctx, db, publication). The docs example is two roots, Co/Prod and Co/Prod/PlanA, of rule, screen, and record sources; a spec keeps it equal to the fixture the publication specs run (UIR_UPDATE_EXAMPLES=1 go test ./indexer regenerates it): uir import docs/examples/import/co-prod.json
uir import - < docs/examples/import/co-prod-plana.json
uir query 'kind:test.rule'
uir query 'field:Policy.Amount < mod:Co/Prod/PlanA'
uir query 'records.Policy.Amount ~w'
uir query 'func:Apply >' FieldMeaningroot_keyThe root's identity, as a Go module path is one: any non-empty string.nameThe root's display name when the publication registers it.location.uriWhere the producer read the root from. It is stored as the location's canonical path with location kind external.revisionThe producer's revision of its sources, such as a commit; may be empty.kindsCustom kinds the publication uses, {name, category, metrics?}, registered as storage.RegisterKind does (a namespaced name and one of container, type, callable, member). Optional metric declarations describe non-negative integer symbol.metrics.<name> fields; see producer metrics.symbolsThe identity of every symbol the documents name, declared or referenced, owners included: module_key, package_path, kind, owner_id, name, parameter_types, and visibility.documentsPer source: path_key (a relative slash path), package_path, source (the text), content_hash (its lowercase hex SHA-256), and content, the typed document of its facts (current format 12). Optional git_path binds original source to a repository file. Every declared symbol in a document's content carries the layered hashes a Go symbol does (hashes and identities), and validation refuses a symbol without them: content_hash (64 hex, the implementation; required on every symbol), and, on every symbol with an id, public_shape and public_hash (what a consumer outside the symbol's visibility boundary observes) and private_hash (the full declared structure, digesting public_hash, so a public change is always a private change). shape stays the private shape text. The package's export shape digests its exported symbols' public_hash, so a private-only change re-keys no importer. A document carries only canonical ids, and an id's module, package, kind, owner, and parameter types cannot be recovered from it, so a publication lists the identities beside the documents. Everything else comes from the documents, as for Go: definitions from their declarations, references from every occurrence with a symbol, call edges from call occurrences with a target and a statement path, writes from write occurrences. A producer computes each id with indexer.SymbolID(indexer.Identity{ModuleKey, PackagePath, Kind, OwnerID, Name, ParameterTypes}), the function Go extraction uses, so a symbol published by two roots, or by Go and a producer, is one id. A document declares only symbols of its own root and package: a selector matches a symbol only in the root its module_key names, and symbol deltas group declarations by package. A symbol of another root that a document references, such as a field of Co/Prod read by a Co/Prod/PlanA rule, is listed in the referencing publication's symbols as well. Publication shares the Go publication core (indexer/publication.go). Publish validates the whole publication before writing anything, against the database's kinds plus the kinds it declares: required fields, paths, hashes, kinds, owners, every document through storage.DecodeDocument (so an enclosing id must be declared in the same document), and every named id against symbols. A failure names the root and the document or symbol, wraps indexer.ErrInvalidPublication (a 400 invalid_publication over HTTP), and leaves the database untouched, declared kinds included. Publish then registers the declared kinds and hands the core the same extraction IndexModules builds for a Go module, which, in one transaction, registers the root and its external location, compares the publication with the location's head, and otherwise publishes an import snapshot: source revisions, documents and postings, source and document deltas, package coverage, symbol deltas against the head, stats, and a compare-and-swap head update. Content-addressed documents are reused by (root, path, content digest) even when their package input hash changes. A publication whose revision, sources, and documents all equal the head's publishes nothing and reports unchanged. Snapshots record worktree state unknown; generated sources use stored blobs, while original sources can use explicit Git bindings. See Git-backed publication for repository bindings, historical deltas, and verified source reads. A root is either Go or external: publishing into a root indexed from a Go checkout, or adding a Go checkout whose module path is an external root's key, fails. Only the producer refreshes an external root: uir add and uir reindex given its URI or root key fail saying it is published by an external producer, and uir reindex --all skips it even when the handle cutover left it without a head; republish it with uir import.
204.title: Publishing from a non-Go producer

205.text: A producer that already holds its root as UIR nodes, such as a database catalogue lowered into uir.RecordTable and uir.MethodNode values, does not build documents by hand: indexer.PublicationFromNodes(indexer.NodePublication{RootKey, Name, Location, Revision, Options, Documents: []indexer.NodeDocument{{PathKey, PackagePath, Nodes}}}) returns the Publication to hand to indexer.Publish, so there is no second publication path. Symbols. Every node and every member is a declared symbol: a table's columns, indexes, foreign keys, and triggers, a record's fields, and a class's or interface's variables, constructor, destructor, methods, and nested types. Its kind comes from its node type (table, column, index, foreign_key, record, field, type for a class, interface, endpoint, constructor, and func or method for a callable without or with an owner; a view is a table). Any other node type is an error. A package node is not a symbol: the document is the package.Classes. A uir.TypedNode class is the builtin type kind, whose type_form validation checks against the form its shape classifies as (storage.ClassifyTypeShape). The shape is the one source of that form, in either shape language a type has: a Go indexer shape is a Go type declaration, classified with go/parser, and a class's uir.Shape opens with class and is struct, since UIR models no alias or defined non-struct type (a UIR interface is the interface kind, which has no type form). PublicationFromNodes fills type_form from the same function, and a shape that is neither is an error, so no Go parse is attempted on a UIR shape and no producer-supplied form can disagree with it. type_form is what a struct: selector filters type symbols by.Identity. module_key is the root key, package_path the document's, owner_id the owner's id (a column is owned by its table, so two tables' id columns are two symbols), name the identifier's name, and parameter_types a callable's parameters, each its SQLType, else its field type, else its type reference, so overloads differ. Build tables with uir.NewTable, which stamps each member with its table, and give a class's members its package and Type in their identifiers; two symbols with one id or one identifier key are an error, as is a node without a name.Visibility. Indexes, foreign keys, and triggers are private members, so they are internal; any other symbol is exported when its UIR visibility is public or unset and its owner is exported, else internal.Layers. public_hash, private_hash, and content_hash are uir.Fingerprint's layers, public_shape and shape are uir.Shape's public and private text, payload is uir.MarshalNode, and semantic_hash is Hash(). A node with no implementation anywhere beneath it has an empty content layer, which is published as the SHA-256 of uir-node-content-none-v1, so every symbol has a 64-hex content_hash and two bodiless declarations compare equal.Source. The source is always generated, never supplied, so its spans cannot disagree with its symbols: per top-level node, its private shape with each symbol's name after its kind and each member's line, the line uir.MemberLine says the shape embeds it as, expanded in place to the member's own text (table customers sql:table {,   column id bigint (int) not null identity pk,   primary key (id), }). A symbol's lowered body — a function's, method's, or trigger's Body, and a view's Definition — follows its last member line, before its closing brace, as the plain text of the body's Pretty() rendering indented under the symbol (  method orders_audit () event=insert timing=after,     audit_log()). The same nodes always produce the same bytes, every symbol's extent nests inside its owner's, and a changed column or index changes only its own line and an edited body only lines inside its symbol's extent, so a line diff of two revisions' stored sources attributes each changed line to the symbol whose extent holds it, and uir diff --stat counts body edits on the symbol that owns them.
205.title: Publishing UIR nodes

206.text: The earlier uir project ... command, project browser API, and project GORM tables are removed. Opening an existing database discards those old tables after applying the module schema; it does not backfill project snapshots. Back up the database before opening it with this version if that history is needed. See storage design for the exact table allowlist and dependency checks. A database indexed before compact symbol handles is recognised on open by modules lacking its ordinal column. Before migration, in one transaction, its index (snapshots, heads, source revisions and deltas, documents, symbols, postings, and package coverage) is discarded, while the registered roots, locations, and primary locations are kept and the roots are numbered. Run uir reindex --all to rebuild registered headless checkouts; opening the database logs a warning saying so. Until then uir list and uir get show the root with an empty snapshot id and head version 0. Unscoped queries and readers skip missing heads, which uir status lists, while an explicit root or checkout selection without a head fails. A read-only open refuses such a database. The same applies, by the same mechanism, to a database whose symbol deltas still carry the two-layer shape_fp and body_fp fingerprints (documents of format 4, with shape_hash and body_hash): its index is discarded on open, its registrations are kept with their ordinals, and uir reindex rebuilds it with the public, private, and content layers.
206.title: Legacy cutover

207.text:
uir import normally reads a publication JSON file. A producer plugin lets uir ask an external executable for the publication of a checkout instead. repomap uses this to publish dependencies, container images, Kubernetes resources and security advisories as queryable symbols (dep.package, security.advisory, k8s.container, ...). uir import --plugin repomap .
uir import --plugin repomap --security ../service
uir import --plugin repomap --plugin-path ./.bin/repomap . With --plugin, the positional argument is the checkout path (the working directory when omitted). --security asks the plugin to include security advisories and fails if the plugin cannot reach its advisory source. --producer, --historical and --git-commit apply to the returned publication as they do to a file. The import is a command-line operation only. POST /api/v1/modules/import refuses plugin with 400, because it would execute a binary and read a checkout on the server; send the publication in the body instead.
207.title: Producer plugins and uir import --plugin repomap

208.text: The executable named after the plugin is resolved in this order, and a miss lists every location searched: --plugin-path$UIR_PRODUCER_PATH (a path list)./.binthe directory of the uir executable$PATH
208.title: Discovery
titles: Producer plugins and uir import --plugin repomap

209.text: uir runs <bin> uir and speaks newline-delimited JSON-RPC 2.0 over its stdin and stdout. The plugin's stderr is for logs; uir includes its tail in any error. MethodParamsResultinitializenone{"name":"repomap","version":"...","protocol":"uir-producer/1","methods":["initialize","publication","shutdown"]}publication{"path":"<checkout dir>","security":false}an indexer.Publication object, the format uir import readsshutdownnonenull, after which the process exits uir fails the import, with upgrade guidance, when protocol differs or publication is not listed. The publication is decoded strictly (unknown fields are rejected). A JSON-RPC error object, non-JSON on stdout, or the child exiting early also fail the import; the plugin's error.data and stderr tail are included. Cancelling uir kills the child. When the publication does not set options.producer, uir sets it to <name>/<version>+sha256:<binary digest>.
209.title: Protocol uir-producer/1
titles: Producer plugins and uir import --plugin repomap

210.text:
SELECT symbol.name, r.severity, r.target_version, path, line FROM security.advisory:* AS r WHERE r.severity = 'high'
SELECT path, line FROM references(traverse(dep.package:"golang.org/x/net", via => 'dep.provides')) references(traverse(...)) composes: a navigation function accepts another navigation function as its source.
210.title: Related queries
titles: Producer plugins and uir import --plugin repomap

211.text: uir query reads the snapshot-aware symbol index using SQL or a compact symbol expression. It resolves canonical symbols and traverses recorded declarations, occurrences, implementations, calls, and native relationships. Queries run against the primary head of each selected registered root unless --location or --snapshot selects another indexed view. A leading unquoted SELECT chooses the Participle SQL parser; --language auto|compact|sql overrides detection. SQL errors retain their diagnostics without retrying compact parsing. The compact parser is generated from query/grammar.peg with make query-parser. See SQL navigation for projections, predicates, functions, stored file/callable metrics, custom-domain publication, and completion. The compact grammar and structured flags documented below remain available; structured navigation flags are compact-only.
211.title: Querying indexed modules

212.text:
uir query 'store.Store.Save' --root example.org/service
uir query 'store.Store.Save <' --root example.org/service
uir query 'store.Store.Save <' --root example.org/service --group-by=file,module
uir query 'store.Store.Save < -pkg store' --root example.org/service
uir query 'store.Store.Save < -pkg example.org/service/...' --root example.org/service
uir query 'example.org/service/store.Store.Save =' --root example.org/service
uir query 'example.org/service/store.Save*' --root example.org/service
uir query 'api.* >> store.Store.Save' --root example.org/service --format json
uir query 'pkg:example.org/service:store & struct:Store' --root example.org/service
uir query 'func:Store.Save < pkg:example.org/service:api/**' --root example.org/service
uir query 'func:* +pkg:example.org/service:api -func:Test*' --root example.org/service
uir query --methods --calls --include 'example.org/service/api/**' --root example.org/service
uir query 'store.Store.Save' --callers --exclude 'example.org/service/internal/**'
uir query --types --inherits --root example.org/service
uir query --modules --packages --format json
uir query '"Add Rider" < mod:"Example Regional/Group Life/..."'
uir query 'Plan:PlanField1 ~w kind:oipa.rule:"CopyBook-*"' An expression is optional when a structured flag is present. --methods, --vars, --types, --modules, and --packages select node kinds; combining kinds forms a union. --callers, --calls, --implements, and --inherits traverse incoming calls, outgoing calls, interface implementations, and direct struct or interface embedding respectively. Multiple relation flags union their witness rows. With no kind or expression, a relation starts from its compatible symbol kind (func:* for calls and type:* for type relations). Repeatable --include and --exclude accept full module, package, or qualified symbol path globs; includes form a union, and exclusions win. These flags compile into the same expression tree as the text grammar before execution. For example, --methods --calls is method:* >, and --types --inherits is type:* :inherits. --root is a registered module path. --location selects a registered checkout and --snapshot selects a historical published snapshot; they cannot be combined. On the command line, inside a registered checkout (the nearest go.mod above the working directory) an empty --root and --location default to that checkout; --all searches every registered root instead and cannot be combined with --root, --location, or --snapshot. Outside a registered checkout, an empty --root means every root. The same defaults apply to uir suggest, uir suggest-selectors, uir graph, uir browse, and uir prune; over HTTP nothing defaults from the server's working directory. --limit defaults to 100 and accepts 1–1000. The root command's --dsn selects the UIR database. Without an explicit scope, queries use available primary heads and warn about registered checkouts that have no head; an empty result is inconclusive while any head is missing. An explicitly selected root or checkout without a head still fails with "… is registered but not indexed; run uir reindex on its checkout". The HTTP equivalent is POST /api/v1/modules/query with optional args: [expression], the same structured flag names as JSON fields, and optional root, location, snapshot, and limit fields. Human-readable results use a colored symbol tree. --group-by selects the tree levels and their order from module, package, and file; the default is module,package,file. The root package is folded into its module, and a definition on the declaration line appears only on the symbol node. Other matching source positions remain as leaves. Call-path results follow hop order. CLI JSON/YAML and the HTTP JSON response retain the full query envelope.
212.title: Quick start

213.text:
expression   := chain ("&" chain | "|" chain)* | expression ">>" [depth] expression
chain        := primary modifier* (relation filter* primary? | relation filter*)*
primary      := selector | entity-field | symbol | "(" expression ")"
selector     := "pkg:" package-glob | "pkg:" module-glob ":" relative-package-glob
              | "mod:" module-glob | "func:" name-glob | "field:" name-glob | "struct:" name-glob
              | ("all:" | "method:" | "var:" | "type:" | "module:" | "package:" | "path:") glob
              | "kind:" kind-name [":" name-glob]
entity-field := entity-glob ":" field-glob
modifier     := ("+" | "-") selector
symbol       := qualified-name | symbol-glob | quoted
relation     := "<" | ">" | "=" | "<<" [depth] | ":impl" | ":inherits" | ":methods" | ":uses" | "~w"
filter       := "-f" file-suffix | "+pkg" package | "-pkg" package | "~w"
depth        := 1..8
quoted       := '"' (char | "\" char)* '"' Every glob, name, and kind name in a selector, both parts of an entity field, and a symbol may be a quoted string. An unquoted entity is a letter, _, *, or ? followed by letters, digits, _, -, *, or ?; an unquoted field uses the same characters. Parentheses group sets and path endpoints. & binds more tightly than |; >> joins two complete endpoint expressions. Both << and >> are bounded, with defaults of 3 and 8 hops respectively. Invalid or incomplete expressions fail at the parser. The symbol is a qualified name, never a predicate or a bound variable. Typed selectors return sets of active declared canonical symbols. pkg: and mod: select symbols declared in packages or registered module roots; they do not create package or module result entities. module: and package: select the actual indexed tree nodes. all: selects all declared symbols, method: selects methods, var: variables, and type: every kind of the type category (Go named types, and the interface, record, and table kinds of other producers). func: includes every callable kind (functions and methods, and constructors, endpoints, and callable custom kinds such as oipa.rule), field: includes struct fields, and struct: includes defined non-alias Go types with a struct underlying type in the selected snapshot. kind:oipa.rule selects every symbol of one registered kind, builtin or custom, and kind:oipa.rule:Rate* those whose name the glob matches; an unregistered kind is an error. A kind's category, not its name, decides what a relation does with it: < and > read the call occurrences of a callable, and > refuses any other kind. Short typed names may select several symbols without an ambiguity error. An exact typed selector with no active match returns an empty result. Selector globs are case sensitive and anchored to the whole key. * matches within one slash-delimited segment, ? matches one character within it, and ** must occupy a whole segment and can match zero or more segments. A trailing /... is shorthand for /** in any typed selector, including the module part of a two-part pkg: selector. Periods and literal @, #, $, and ! have no special meaning; escape operator characters with \. A colon outside quotes and escapes remains a selector separator. One-part pkg:example.org/service/store matches a full import path. Two-part pkg:example.org/service:store matches the store package relative to that registered module root; pkg:example.org/*:internal/** searches matching module roots without crossing a nested module boundary. Use . only as the complete relative pattern for a module's root package and ** for the root plus descendants. For func:, field:, struct:, and the name glob of kind:, a pattern with no dot or slash matches a name; a dot selects the owner-qualified name; a slash selects the complete query_name. Postfix +kind:pattern keeps symbols and -kind:pattern removes them. Multiple positive modifiers of one kind are ORed, multiple negatives are subtracted, and different kinds are ANDed. For example, func:* +pkg:example.org/service:api +pkg:example.org/service:store -func:Test* keeps functions from either package except matching test names. Parenthesize a unary relation before filtering its projected result: (func:Save <) +pkg:example.org/service:api. A leading exclusion is invalid. ExpressionResultsub.Thing.DoResolve a symbol and show its declaration.sub.Thing.Do <Incoming call sites, including known interface dispatch for methods. For other symbols, incoming references.sub.Thing.Do >Call sites within that function or method.sub.Thing.Do =Definition locations.sub.Thing.Do <<3Callers up to three edges away, with a depth on each row.sub.Thing.Field ~wWrite references. sub.Thing.Field < ~w is equivalent.sub.Iface :implTypes indexed as implementing the interface.sub.Base :inheritsTypes that directly embed the named struct or interface. Older snapshots without embedding facts require reindexing.sub.Thing :methodsMethods owned by the type.sub.Thing.Do :usesWhat the declaration itself reads, writes, and calls: every resolved occurrence inside its body, each row naming the symbol used. Works from any declaration kind, not only callables.kind:sql.procedure:Load :uses ~wThe writes the body makes.sub.Thing.Do < -f _test.goIncoming rows excluding paths with that suffix.sub.Thing.Do < +pkg apiIncoming rows inside a package named api; a full import path selects exactly that package.sub.Thing.Do < -pkg subIncoming rows outside package sub; use the full import path when several packages share the name.sub.Thing.Do < -pkg example.org/mod/...Exclude callers in the module root package and every subpackage. +pkg accepts the same pattern.os.Exec.Command < & io.ReadAll >Symbols shared by the two projected result sets.main.* >> sub.Thing.DoShortest recorded call chain, if one exists.func:Save < pkg:example.org/service:apiIncoming call sites whose enclosing caller is declared in that package.func:Run > func:Store.SaveOutgoing call sites whose resolved callee is that method.struct:Store :methods func:SaveMethod witnesses of matching struct types, narrowed to Save.func:Run :uses pkg:example.org/service:storeUses within Run of symbols declared in that package. A name with / is matched against its full import path; without /, the package portion is suffix matched. Bare symbol globs are case sensitive and anchored: * matches within one slash-delimited segment, ? matches one character, and ** matches across whole slash-delimited segments. The existing .* form selects direct children of the named package or owner. Other globs expand to all matching active canonical symbols, including variables, without an ambiguity prompt. An exact spelling that resolves to several canonical symbols returns positioned candidates with their full query_name; use a full path to disambiguate. & and | compare canonical symbol identities after each side's location rows are projected to symbols. Chaining a relation traverses the projected symbols from the previous step. Package filters without /... match one package. A filter ending in /... matches that full Go import path and every descendant at a / boundary. Use the full go.mod module path followed by /... to cover a whole module. Pass --all (or omit --root outside a registered checkout) to search every registered primary root; the filter then removes callers from the selected package or module while retaining indexed consumers in other roots. Binary relations keep the unary relation's witness rows and retain only rows whose projected canonical symbol belongs to the right operand in the same selected snapshot. < projects the enclosing caller or referrer, > the resolved callee, <<N the caller after traversal, :impl the implementing type, :methods the owned method, :uses the symbol used, and ~w the enclosing writer. = has only a unary form. Use parentheses to make a set the right operand, as in func:Save < (pkg:example.org/service:api & func:Run). A bare right operand binds before &, so func:Save < pkg:example.org/service:api & func:Run intersects the binary relation result with func:Run. The older space-separated +pkg value and -pkg value filter location rows; colon modifiers filter projected canonical symbols. :uses is the outgoing counterpart of < for any declaration, not only callables: X < lists what reads, writes, or calls X; X :uses lists what X's own body reads, writes, or calls. Its rows are the occurrences inside the extent of each declaration of X (or enclosed by it) that resolve to a symbol, other than definitions and the uses of declarations nested inside X, which are part of X rather than used by it. Each row is positioned at the occurrence, keeps its role (reference, write, call, or a producer role), its source_id/source_name name X, and symbol_id, identifier, node_kind, and props describe the symbol used, taken from its declaration in scope (the row's own snapshot first). path, line, and package_path stay those of the occurrence, as for >. ~w keeps the writes. A right operand keeps the rows whose used symbol belongs to it; a pure mod:/pkg: scope keeps the rows whose used symbol is declared in an admitted module or package, wherever X itself sits. An unresolved call is not a use; > lists those. Like the other relations, :uses on a container kind is an error, and an unresolved symbol on its left fails.
213.title: Grammar

214.text: Producers other than Go publish names that the unquoted grammar cannot spell, such as rules named CopyBook-CycleA, Add Rider, or Premium Calc (Annual), and module keys such as Example Regional/Group Life/GL. Enclose such a value in double quotes wherever a symbol or a selector value is accepted: "Add Rider", func:"Premium Calc (Annual)", kind:oipa.rule:"CopyBook-CycleA", mod:"Example Regional/Group Life/GL", and pkg:"Example Regional":"Group Life/**". A quote encloses one whole value; each part of a two-part selector is quoted on its own, and a colon inside quotes is literal. Quoting changes only how the expression is split into tokens, not how the value matches. Inside quotes, *, ?, **, and a trailing /... are still globs, / still separates segments, and . still separates an owner from a name, so "Premium Calc*" matches every rule whose name starts with Premium Calc. A backslash makes the next character literal, as it does unquoted: \" is a quote, \\ a backslash, and \* or \? a literal * or ?. A kind name is never a glob. A bare quoted symbol resolves like an unquoted one: by its full path when it has a /, and otherwise by its name or a dotted suffix of its owner-qualified name. A module selector matches only the module it names. mod:"Example Regional/Group Life/GL" selects the symbols of that module and not of Example Regional/Group Life/GL/Scheme A. Add /... for the module and every module below it, or a * segment for one level: ExpressionResultmod:"Example Regional/Group Life/GL"Symbols of the GL module only.mod:"Example Regional/Group Life/..."Symbols of Group Life and every module below it.mod:"Example Regional/*"Symbols of each module directly below Example Regional."Add Rider" < mod:"Example Regional/..."References to Add Rider from any module of the company.
214.title: Quoted values

215.text: OIPA writes an entity field as Entity:Field, such as Plan:PlanField1, Policy:StatusCode, or Segment:Amount. An unprefixed token of that form selects the field symbols named Field whose direct owner is named Entity, the symbols field:Plan.PlanField1 selects for a top-level Plan. Both parts are globs, so Plan:* is every field of Plan and *:PlanField1 every field of that name. Like any typed selector, an entity field with no active match returns an empty result. It is an operand of every relation and set operator: ExpressionResultPlan:PlanField1The PlanField1 field of Plan, and not one of another entity.Plan:PlanField1 ~wWrites of the field.Plan:PlanField1 < (mod:"Co/Prod" | mod:"Co/Prod/GL")References from either module.Plan:* & mod:"Co/Prod/GL"Fields of Plan declared in that module.Plan:"Field With Space"A field whose name needs quotes. A selector prefix always wins: type:Code is a type selector, pkg:a/b:Sym a package selector, and kind:x:y a kind selector, so write "type":Code for an entity named like a prefix (pkg, mod, func, field, struct, all, method, var, type, module, package, path, kind). A colon followed by impl, inherits, methods, or uses is a relation, so Thing:methods lists the methods of Thing; write Thing:"methods" for a field of that name. An unquoted entity has no . or /, so sub.Iface:impl remains the :impl relation.
215.title: Entity references

216.text: The JSON envelope contains operation, total, matches, symbols, declarations, coverage, and stages. An unscoped query skips registered checkouts without a head; the coverage stage counts them and uir status (GET /api/v1/modules/status) lists each root_key and location. A found >> query also contains path with ordered symbols and the call-site calls connecting them; total is one. When no path exists, total is zero and path is absent. HTTP sets X-Total-Count to total. Result rows include root, checkout, snapshot, source position, package path, role, canonical symbol ID, and enclosing symbol ID where available. coverage lists packages with partial, syntax-only, or excluded indexing, so an empty result is not proof of absence in those packages. The browser expression field uses a Monaco language for compact queries. Completion shows selectors, modifiers, relations, filters, set and path operators at the cursor. It suggests active canonical symbols for bare names without globs, indexed modules, packages, or typed names for selector prefixes, and the fields of an entity after Entity:. A quoted symbol is completed by its literal text, and a suggested name or value that needs quotes is inserted quoted. Arrow keys select suggestions; Enter or Tab inserts one and opens the next relevant choices. Ctrl/Cmd+Space opens suggestions; Ctrl/Cmd+Enter runs the query. GET /api/v1/modules/suggest?prefix=store.Store.S&root=example.org/service&snapshot=<uuid> supplies qualified symbol names. GET /api/v1/modules/suggest-selectors?prefix=pkg:example.org/service:st&root=example.org/service&snapshot=<uuid> supplies typed selector completions. The symbol prefix is literal text without quotes or wildcards; a selector prefix may quote each value, and a value containing whitespace must be quoted (prefix=mod:"Example Regional/Gr). prefix=Plan:Pl completes the fields of Plan. Both accept location or snapshot and an optional limit up to 100. Suggestion responses are plain arrays; unscoped suggestions skip missing heads, which uir status lists. Failed runs mark the expression in Monaco on both the Query page and Cmd+K palette. Invalid syntax returns HTTP 400 with code: "invalid_query", a readable message, a hint, and context.line and context.column when the parser has a position. A symbol absent from the selected index returns HTTP 404 with code: "symbol_not_found" and a hint to check the symbol or snapshot. The editor marks a reported position; errors without one mark the full expression. Editing the expression clears the marker. Other API failures show their structured message and hint without an HTTP status wrapper. Only registered roots and their selected snapshots contribute graph edges. uir graph draws the same call and dispatch edges around one function or method as nodes and edges, with the guards of each call site, bounded by its own depth (1 through 8) and node limit (1 through 1000). Interface dispatch includes relationships recorded by the index; it cannot prove calls through interfaces outside the indexed import closure. The path query is reachability over calls, not dataflow or sanitizer-aware taint analysis. Joins over two free variables belong in a full query language such as CodeQL or Joern. This grammar replaces the former from/where style, nodes, search, and unresolved calls query expressions; those spellings now fail parsing.
216.title: Results and limits

217.text:
Opening an older database can discard legacy project history or indexed snapshots. Back it up before opening it with this version; the storage cutover instructions describe affected layouts and reindexing. Build and serve UIR against a local SQLite database or PostgreSQL: pnpm --dir web install
make build
mkdir -p state
go run ./cmd/uir --dsn ./state/uir.db serve --host localhost --port 8080 --host defaults to localhost and --port to 8080. The database is migrated and checked before the listener opens. The command serves embedded Vite assets and Clicky operations on one origin. For live frontend development, use go run ./cmd/uir --dsn ./state/uir.db serve --dev; the command starts the Vite server and proxies its UI while API requests remain on the same origin. Dev mode and frontend tests use @flanksource/clicky-ui source from the sibling clicky-ui/packages/ui/src directory when it exists, or from CLICKY_UI_ROOT/packages/ui/src when configured. That checkout needs its own dependencies installed. When the source directory is absent, they use the installed package. Production builds always use the pinned package. Dev mode requires the local web/node_modules/.bin/vite executable. The browser lists module roots, their registered checkout locations, and immutable snapshots. The scope picker in the top-right of the header defaults to "All modules"; choosing a root scopes the browser to that root's primary checkout head. Select a checkout to inspect effective sources and node projections; source content is displayed only after its bytes match the indexed content hash. The Query tab runs compact queries and SQL navigation against the selected scope: with "All modules", clicky.StartTask < reads the primary head of every indexed root and returns recorded callers with their Root column. Add indexes a directory or package path, discovering enclosing and nested Go modules; Reindex refreshes a registered location. The URL retains module, location, snapshot, source, node, the revealed line and column, search, expression, and offset so a view can be reopened. The browser uses these Clicky routes: Method and routePurposeGET /api/v1/modules and GET /api/v1/modules/by-key/{root}Root list and detail.GET /api/v1/modules/headsPlain array of indexed checkout heads and their effective files; headless checkouts are skipped.GET /api/v1/modules/statusIndex coverage and registered checkouts without heads.GET /api/v1/modules/locations?root=...Registered checkouts for one root.GET /api/v1/modules/snapshots?root=...&location=...Paged snapshots for one checkout.GET /api/v1/modules/browse?snapshot=...Effective sources and node/call projections for one snapshot.GET /api/v1/modules/content?snapshot=...&path=...Hash-verified bytes for one module-relative source.GET /api/v1/modules/dependencies?snapshot=...Declared go.mod requirements, selected versions, linked target snapshots, and unresolved reasons.POST /api/v1/modules/querySQL or compact query with args containing the expression and optional language (auto, compact, sql), root, location, snapshot, and limit fields. Omitting scope fields reads primary heads across indexed roots. Compact results use the query envelope; SQL results use columns, rows, total, coverage, and optional graph or path. X-Total-Count reports total.GET /api/v1/modules/query-catalogSQL fields, functions, domains, and relationships used for completion.GET /api/v1/modules/graph?selector=...Call graph around one function or method, selected by selector (a symbol expression) or symbol (a canonical symbol id), with optional direction (callees, callers, both), depth (1 through 8), limit (1 through 1000), exclude (a comma list of package patterns, std,builtin,gorm.io/... when absent, none for nothing), root, location, and snapshot query parameters. Returns roots, nodes, edges, groups, and omitted beside the effective exclude patterns, the packages reached, stages, and candidates; an ambiguous selector returns its candidates with an empty graph. A pattern that is not an import path, a /... pattern or a keyword is a 400 invalid_query.GET /api/v1/modules/suggest and GET /api/v1/modules/suggest-selectorsPlain arrays of active symbol objects or typed-selector strings for prefix, with optional root, location, snapshot, and limit query parameters.POST /api/v1/modules/diffCommit-to-commit symbol diff with args containing <from>..<to> and root, visibility, change-type, stat, auto-index, include-tests, snapshot-from, and snapshot-to as JSON fields.POST /api/v1/modules/add and POST /api/v1/modules/reindexStart an index run for a new directory or registered location. Returns 202 Accepted with {"run_id":"..."}; follow the run through GET /api/v1/tasks and the Tasks view.POST /api/v1/modules/importPublish a non-Go producer's root with the publication object as the body's publication field. Answers synchronously with the ModuleResult (root_key, location, snapshot_id, head_version, files, parsed_files, reused_files, unchanged); a publication refused before anything is written is a 400 invalid_publication.POST /api/v1/modules/refactor/preview and POST /api/v1/modules/refactor/applyPreview a gopatch rename or move, then apply the reviewed diff. URL-encode module paths, checkout paths, and source paths in requests. /api/openapi.json describes the generated API, including the connection routes below. The removed /api/v1/project, /api/v1/snapshot, /api/v1/root, /api/v1/source, and /api/v1/node routes are not compatibility aliases. The heads, suggestion, SQL connection, and connection-database lists return JSON arrays directly, without an items or warnings wrapper. Snapshot listing remains paginated, and query results retain their compact or SQL envelope. Use the status route for missing-head diagnostics. For example, run a SQL metric query over one registered root: curl -sS http://localhost:8080/api/v1/modules/query -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"args":["SELECT symbol.name, symbol.metrics.param_count FROM func:* WHERE symbol.metrics.param_count > 3"],"root":"example.org/service"}' The content route first verifies that the requested path belongs to the selected snapshot and cannot escape its module location. If the current local file has the saved SHA-256 hash, it returns those bytes. Otherwise, dirty and non-Git snapshots read their stored source blob; clean snapshots can read the pinned Git blob. An imported snapshot uses its stored blobs or explicit Git source bindings; its producer URI is not treated as a checkout. Every source is hash-verified. If no source matches, the route returns an error instead of displaying current bytes as historical content. No remote repository is fetched automatically by the default reader. Explorer Rename and Move require a current, fully indexed local checkout and a gopatch executable. serve --gopatch-bin defaults to the Go bin directory; set it to an absolute path when gopatch is installed elsewhere. Symbol renames pass this server's UIR DSN to gopatch, which checks current indexed references in the module and its consumers. Preview sends snapshot, source, optional node, action, and either new-name or module-relative destination; Apply sends the same fields plus preview-hash. Apply rejects a changed diff, then reindexes affected registered checkouts. The preview includes changes to workspace and configured consumer modules. The refactor routes accept only local, same-origin requests.
217.title: Browser and API

218.text: Open /connections on the local server to save and test connections. UIR serves the commons-db connection service, the same one the commons-db query app uses, so every connection type its form schema offers can be saved, and secret references such as op:// are accepted. Stored passwords and certificates are never returned by the API, and leaving one blank while editing preserves its stored value. For a local SQLite source, create a saved connection through the browser or the API: curl -sS -X POST http://localhost:8080/api/v1/connection -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"name":"Local catalogue","type":"sqlite","url":".tmp/catalog.db"}' Test the saved connection, then choose it in Add a database. PostgreSQL, SQL Server, MySQL, and SQLite connections can back database modules; Git, hosted source control, and S3 connections can be saved and tested. Adding a database module takes its first read-only schema capture. Capture schema takes later captures manually. Captures store catalogue metadata, not table rows. A same-module comparison covers every schema; a cross-module comparison requires one schema from each capture and matches objects by exact name and SQL type. MySQL currently contributes relation and column names and types; comparisons involving MySQL omit metadata that its inspector does not capture. The local, same-origin API provides the commons-db connection routes: GET/POST /api/v1/connection, GET/PUT/DELETE /api/v1/connection/{id}, POST /api/v1/connection/test and POST /api/v1/connection/resolve (both act on an unsaved draft), GET /api/v1/connections/dashboard, and GET /api/v1/connections/health. GET /api/v1/connection with Accept: application/schema+json supplies the connection form schema. With Accept: application/json and ?types=postgres,mysql,sql_server,sqlite, it returns a plain array of saved SQL connections. A connection that a database module uses cannot be deleted until the module is removed; the database's foreign key enforces this. POST /api/v1/database-modules/connections/{id}/databases returns a plain array of database names the saved SQL connection can reach. GET/POST /api/v1/database-modules, POST /api/v1/database-modules/{id}/capture, GET /api/v1/database-modules/{id}/snapshots, and POST /api/v1/database-modules/diff manage captures and comparisons. The OpenAPI document lists these routes and their request and response shapes.
218.title: Connections and database captures

219.text: These examples cover all 15 UIR SQL source functions. The language reference defines selectors, fields, predicates, options, limits, and error behavior. Each SQL block is one complete query; paste it into the browser Query page or pass it as the quoted expression to uir query.
219.title: SQL examples

220.text:
From the repository root, build the CLI and index the included service module into an isolated SQLite database: make build
mkdir -p .tmp
.bin/uir --dsn .tmp/sql-language-go.db add docs/examples/sql-go
.bin/uir --dsn .tmp/sql-language-go.db query 'SELECT symbol.name FROM func:*' --root example.org/service For the Go queries below, use that DSN and --root example.org/service. The module declares Order.Total, a Repository interface, Store.Save, and an AuditedStore embedding Store. Its call chain is Entry → Run → Store.Save, with Replay → Run as a second entry. Save reads Order.Total and writes LastTotal; Load reads LastTotal. Process calls Save through the Repository interface.
220.title: Prepare the Go example

221.text:
Select concrete methods of Store; source positions describe their declarations: SELECT symbol.name, symbol.kind, path, line
FROM method:Store.*
ORDER BY symbol.name Find the declaration of the save method explicitly: SELECT symbol.query_name, path, line, column
FROM definitions(method:Store.Save) Select declarations belonging to one module's root package, using the contextual package selector: SELECT symbol.name, symbol.kind
FROM pkg:example.org/service:.
WHERE symbol.visibility = 'exported'
ORDER BY symbol.kind, symbol.name
221.title: Select declarations and definitions

222.text:
List direct callers of Run: Entry and Replay. The projected symbol names are callers; path and line identify their call sites. SELECT symbol.name AS caller, path, line, role
FROM callers(func:Run)
ORDER BY caller Follow Entry's call chain for up to two hops, retaining the site and distance of each hop: SELECT symbol.name AS callee, path, line, depth
FROM callees(func:Entry, depth => 2)
ORDER BY depth, callee Find callers of the functions that Entry calls. Nested navigation passes canonical identities, so this again finds callers of Run: SELECT symbol.name AS caller, path, line
FROM callers(callees(func:Entry))
ORDER BY caller Keep callers in one package while excluding methods by canonical identity: SELECT symbol.name, path, line
FROM callers(func:Run)
WHERE symbol IN pkg:example.org/service:. AND symbol NOT IN method:Store.*
ORDER BY symbol.name Inspect known interface implementation targets reached from Process, using multi-hop callee traversal and a Boolean predicate. A direct depth-one callee query retains the declared interface method instead: SELECT symbol.owner, symbol.name, dispatch, path, line
FROM callees(func:Process, depth => 2)
WHERE dispatch = TRUE
ORDER BY symbol.owner
222.title: Find callers and callees

223.text:
Find all non-definition uses of a field, including their recorded roles. Here symbol.name is the referenced field, rather than the enclosing function: SELECT symbol.name, path, line, role
FROM references(field:Order.Total)
ORDER BY path, line Find reads of the package variable in Load: SELECT symbol.name, path, line, role
FROM reads(var:LastTotal) Find writes of the same variable in Store.Save: SELECT symbol.name, path, line, role
FROM writes(var:LastTotal) These functions search uses of their argument, not the uses made by its body. For outgoing resolved body uses in the compact language, use func:Run :uses; SQL has no uses() function. Direct reference selectors can also find imported identities such as references(func:fmt.Println) when their declaration is outside the indexed module.
223.title: Inspect references, reads, and writes

224.text:
List owned methods of Store: SELECT symbol.query_name, path, line
FROM methods(type:Store) Find the recorded types that implement Repository, including pointer implementation facts: SELECT symbol.name, path, line
FROM implementers(type:Repository)
ORDER BY symbol.name Find direct embedding declarations, such as AuditedStore embedding Store: SELECT symbol.name, path, line
FROM inheritors(type:Store)
224.title: Navigate types

225.text:
Traverse up to three outgoing call hops. Filtering for Save happens after traversal, so Run is still followed even though it does not match the predicate: SELECT symbol.name, depth
FROM traverse(func:Entry, direction => 'outgoing', depth => 3)
WHERE symbol.name = 'Save'
ORDER BY depth Return one shortest call path from Entry to Store.Save. Its path.symbols are Entry, Run, and Save, with call-site evidence between them: SELECT * FROM path(func:Entry, method:Store.Save, depth => 4) Draw outgoing calls, bounded by hop depth and node count, with package exclusions disabled: SELECT * FROM graph(func:Entry, direction => 'outgoing', depth => 3, nodes => 30, exclude => 'none') Draw read/write access from Store.Save instead of calls: SELECT * FROM graph(method:Store.Save, access => 'read,write', direction => 'outgoing', depth => 1) path() and graph() return structured results. They cannot have WHERE, ORDER BY, or SQL LIMIT. For JSON output, run the query with --format json and inspect path or graph, including graph omissions.
225.title: Traverse, find a path, and draw a graph

226.text:
Count functions and structs per indexed file, including files with no matching declaration: SELECT f.path, f.lines, f.definitions, f.functions, f.structs
FROM files() AS f
ORDER BY f.lines DESC, f.path Review callables with parameters and bodies, using a projection alias for ordering: SELECT symbol.name, symbol.metrics.param_count AS parameters, symbol.metrics.body_lines AS body_lines
FROM func:*
WHERE symbol.metrics.param_count >= 1 AND symbol.metrics.body_lines IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY body_lines DESC, symbol.name Read the proven package-variable type: SELECT symbol.name, symbol.type
FROM var:LastTotal
WHERE symbol.type = 'int' Find interface signatures with no body. IS NULL selects a known bodyless declaration; it does not turn unavailable metrics into a missing value: SELECT symbol.name, symbol.metrics.param_count, symbol.metrics.body_lines
FROM methods(type:Repository)
WHERE symbol.metrics.body_lines IS NULL Combine anchored name globs and explicit negation. Parentheses group the alternatives before the visibility condition: SELECT symbol.name, symbol.kind
FROM func:*
WHERE (symbol.name MATCH 'S*' OR symbol.name MATCH 'R*')
  AND NOT (symbol.visibility = 'internal')
  AND symbol.name NOT IMATCH '*play'
ORDER BY symbol.name Inspect explicit modern build headers, including excluded snapshot members. The sample file has no header, so its constraint is the empty string and it does not require hack: SELECT path, file.build_constraint
FROM files(include_excluded => TRUE)
WHERE file.build_constraint NOT REQUIRES 'hack'
ORDER BY path
226.title: Inspect files, callable metrics, and variable types

227.text:
The domain producer supplies an HTTP route, handler, topic, consumer, and Kubernetes objects with explicit native links. From the repository root: mkdir -p .tmp
go run -tags hack ./hack/sql-domains > .tmp/sql-language-domains.json
