Stage 2: prototype with the real CLI and Gavel fixtures

350.text: Adopt H64a handles with symbol deltas as a surrogate. Keep the SHA-256 id as the identity in documents, hashes and canonical keys. Postings shrink 3–7×, the database shrinks 16–22 %, cold indexing is 6–11 % faster, and query fixtures are 15–29 % faster, with byte-identical output.Do not use H128. It is larger than H64a on both engines, offers no query advantage, and is only portable across databases if the module and package fields are hashed. With a 16-bit hash, collisions are expected after about 256 modules by the birthday bound.Do not replace the identity with the handle, for the portability and extraction-order reasons above.Do not add a roaring dependency. Sorted slices are faster than maps at these sizes, and the sets are small.Prefer attribute-major (H64a) over owner-major (H64o). They are the same size, but H64a gives package, visibility and kind prefix ranges for selectors and the exported-API scan. Owner lookups need an (owner_id, kind, name) index either way: today owner_id = ? has no usable index and scans symbols.
350.title: Recommendation (adopted)
titles: Compact symbol handles and symbol deltas

351.text: Handles are local to one database. They must never leave it through the API, JSON output or documents. Only SHA ids are exposed.Visibility is packed into the handle. If the visibility algorithm changes, publication fails loudly on a mismatched handle, and a reindex into a fresh database is required.Existing databases need a rebuild. Their rows are not migrated to the new posting layout. Opening a pre-handle database (recognised by modules lacking ordinal) runs a cutover before migration, in one transaction:It drops the index tables: postings, package coverage, documents, symbols, source deltas and revisions, heads, and snapshots.It keeps the registrations in modules, locations and primary_locations, and numbers modules densely.It took about 5 s on a copy of the 777 MB fixture corpus database.uir reindex on each checkout rebuilds the index. Until then uir list and uir get show the root with no snapshot, and queries that select it fail saying it is registered but not indexed. OpenReadOnly refuses a pre-handle database.Concurrent writers.PostgreSQL: allocation conflicts (unique violation, deadlock, serialization failure) retry the whole publication up to three times. This is tested with a blocked concurrent publisher.SQLite: two writer processes can still fail with a busy error that is not retried.Registry headroom. The 11-bit module field is 10 % used by five checkouts.
351.title: Risks and costs
titles: Compact symbol handles and symbol deltas

352.text: SQLite per-process floor: found and fixed in commons-db, awaiting release.Cause: commons-db/migrate opened an Atlas SQLite transaction on every uir invocation, even with nothing to migrate. Atlas's OpenTx runs PRAGMA foreign_key_check over the whole database when the transaction opens and again when it commits.Fix: reconcileSQLite now computes pending changes read-only first, via sqlitemigrate.PendingChanges, and only opens the transaction when there is something to apply.Effect on main's code and database:MeasureBeforeAfterstorage.UirDB911 ms10 msone uir process0.94 s0.05 s77 SQLite query fixtures119.5 s50.1 sThe SQLite query comparison above predates this fix. After it, most of the SQLite gain attributed to handles disappears, because the handle design's smaller file mainly shortened this scan.Lazy document content in queries. ActiveDocuments now takes ActiveDocumentOptions{Content}, and the diff reads membership without content, but the query layer still passes Content: true and loads every active document's content up front (query/module_index.go, query/module_documents.go). Loading only the documents a posting selects, with DocumentContents, would help queries on both designs.Owner lookup index. Add (owner_id, kind, name), or read :methods through the owner's method buckets.func init identity. Fix the shared canonical id (TODO 34ea4d17).Documents. They are now 77 % of the SQLite database and 39 % of the PostgreSQL one. Both the per-document symbol table and the per-file input hash from benchmarks still apply.Missing dotenv. Gavel ignores a missing setup.dotenv, which is why the corpus and history fixtures carry a WORKAROUND(missing-dotenv) guard. The commons-db fix is tracked as gavel TODO 7d858863.
352.title: Follow-ups
titles: Compact symbol handles and symbol deltas

353.text: UIR has four related, non-interchangeable forms: a structured Identifier, rendered/searchable symbol strings, a canonical symbol id proven by the Go type checker, and a per-file document containing declarations and occurrences. The current database stores those documents as JSON in documents.content, one per file version and package input hash, and the canonical symbols in the global symbols table with an inverted index in symbol_postings and per-snapshot changes in symbol_deltas; the old uir_nodes and uir_relationships tables are removed.
353.title: Symbols and references

354.text:
FieldMeaningidOptional producer-supplied UUID.moduleHighest-level namespace, Go module, service root, or equivalent.packagePackage or namespace.typeType, class, table, record, or endpoint group.methodMethod or function name.fieldField, variable, parameter, or column name.signatureOverload or source-position disambiguator.node_typeExplicit kind; when omitted, GetNodeType() infers it from populated fields. {
  "module": "example.org/service",
  "package": "example.org/service/invoices",
  "type": "InvoiceService",
  "method": "Approve",
  "signature": "(InvoiceID)->error",
  "node_type": "method"
} Identifier.String() renders a common declaration as module.package.type:method#signature; an endpoint uses slash-separated components. SymbolKey() prefixes the lowercase node type, for example method:example.org/service.example.org/service/invoices.InvoiceService:Approve#(InvoiceID)->error. These strings are for display and discovery. Components can contain separators, and ParseIdentifier handles only the basic dot-and-colon declaration form; it does not round-trip explicit UUIDs, node types, signatures, or endpoint slash forms. Identifier.Equals currently compares rendered strings, so it inherits their collision limits. ValueScope and purposeIdentifier.String()Human-readable projection, not durable identity.SymbolKey()Node-kind-prefixed search projection, not globally unique.GetUUID()Supplied ID or deterministic SHA-1 UUID derived from SymbolKey(); cannot distinguish the same symbol in two roots.IdentityKey()Versioned encoding of every structured identifier component; stable lookup key within a logical module root.semantic_hashHash of semantic node content for change/diff detection, not identity. IdentityKey() version 1 is v1: followed by a compact JSON array in this order: node type, module, package, type, method, field, signature. Empty components remain, so punctuation inside one component cannot collide with separators elsewhere. The Go extractor leaves the module empty and writes a function's signature as gofmt prints its type without the func keyword, so func (s *InvoiceService) Approve(id InvoiceID) error is keyed: v1:["method","","example.org/service/invoices","InvoiceService","Approve","","(id InvoiceID) error"] Go lets a package declare func init() any number of times, several per file, so the signature slot of an init holds its overload discriminator instead: the file's base name and the init's 0-based position among that file's inits, for example v1:["method","","example.org/service/invoices","","init","","ast.go#1"] for the second init of ast.go. Nothing can reference an init, so renaming or reordering files changing the key is harmless. A module root's root_key comes from go.mod. The same identity key can occur in two roots, two source files, or two checkouts. The current SourceRevision is keyed by root, path, content hash, and package path, and its document by root, path, and package input hash. Each document symbol entry carries the identity key as key and retains the structured identifier, parent identity, slot/order, payload, semantic hash, optional field detail, and name and extent ranges. The browser's node ID combines revision ID and identity key for selection; it is not a global declaration UUID or an SQL foreign key.
354.title: Structured identifier

355.text: When a package type-checks, its documents are typed (indexed, or partial when the package has type errors) and every declaration and every identifier use that names a package-level object carries a canonical symbol id. The id is the SHA-256 of a length-delimited encoding of (identity_version, module_key, package_path, kind, owner_id, name, ordered parameter types, ordered result types, discriminator), stored as symbols.canonical_key; for example Store.Save(ctx context.Context, inv Invoice) error in example.org/service/invoices encodes as: 10:uir-symbol,1:2,19:example.org/service,28:example.org/service/invoices,6:method,64:<id of Store>,4:Save,1:2,15:context.Context,36:example.org/service/invoices.Invoice,1:0,0:, PartValuemodule_keyThe Go module path; std for the standard library; empty only for builtin.kindpackage, type, func, method, field, var, const, or builtin (universe objects such as len, int, error, nil).owner_idA method's receiver type or interface; a field's struct type, or the field or variable whose literal struct type declares it.Parameter typesFully qualified named types, composite types spelled out, type parameters by ordinal ($0), the variadic parameter as ...T. Parameter names, results, and field types are not identity.Result typesEmpty for Go, which has no overloading, so a result change keeps the id. A non-Go producer's callables carry their return types here, so overloads that differ only in what they return stay apart.DiscriminatorTells apart declarations a language lets a scope repeat with everything else equal. Go sets it only for func init, to the same <file>#<n> its identity key carries. indexer.SymbolID(indexer.Identity{...}) computes an id and Identity.CanonicalKey() its key; Go extraction uses them, and a non-Go producer calls them for the ids its documents carry, with its root key as module_key and its own kinds. Renaming a parameter or changing a result keeps the id and changes the symbol's public_hash and private_hash; changing a parameter type or a name creates a new id, and the old row is retained. visibility is exported only when the name and every owner in its chain are exported. Parameters, results, receivers, function-scoped declarations, type parameters, and labels are not canonical: their occurrences have a null symbol and a note. Builtins get symbol rows but no postings. The symbol row does not record where a symbol is declared; its definition postings do, per document, so one id can be declared in several checkout heads, and moving a declaration to another file moves only its posting. Each typed entry also carries shape (the canonical rendering of its full declared type: a signature on one line, a struct or interface one gofmt-aligned member per line), public_shape (the same rendering restricted to what code outside the package observes: exported fields and methods, plus an opaque line when unexported ones exist), public_hash over the public shape, private_hash over public_hash and the full shape, content_hash over the declaration's tokens without comments or layout, and implements for a type that satisfies interfaces declared in its package or its imports. symbol_postings indexes each document's definition, reference (every occurrence with a symbol, whatever its role), and implements facts with an occurrence count; the symbol operations of uir query read these postings for the heads or snapshot in scope and then only the documents they select. symbol_deltas records, per snapshot, which symbols its active documents newly define, redefine with a different public, private, or content layer, or stop defining, so whether a snapshot defines a symbol, and which of its layers changed between two snapshots, is answered without reading documents. symbols.search_name (the name lowercased and restricted to [a-z0-9]) backs exact name lookup and prefix search. A syntax document, produced when a package cannot be type-checked, has no ids, no postings, and no symbol deltas; its symbols keep only key. Inside the database, postings and deltas do not store the 64-character id. Each symbol row also has a database-local 64-bit handle that packs module and package numbers, visibility, kind, and a local counter, so a package's symbols, or its exported functions, form one contiguous handle range; documents, modules, and snapshots have local ordinals. Handles and ordinals depend on the order things were indexed, so they differ between databases and never leave one: documents, hashes, canonical keys, and every query and diff result carry the SHA-256 id. See symbol index storage for the layout.
355.title: Canonical symbols

356.text:
NodeRef embeds an Identifier and implements Node, allowing a statement to refer to a declaration without embedding it: target := uir.Identifier{
    Module:   "example.org/service",
    Package:  "example.org/service/invoices",
    Type:     "InvoiceService",
    Method:   "Approve",
    NodeType: uir.NodeTypeMethod,
}
ref := uir.NewRef(target) NodeRef.GetNode() currently returns the reference itself; lazy loading is not implemented. Before resolution, only identifier-facing operations such as GetIdentifier, GetType, and Pretty are safe. GetChildren, GetLanguage, and GetLocation delegate through GetNode() and recurse indefinitely. NodeRef.GetType() returns the explicit node_type; if omitted, infer the kind through ref.GetIdentifier().GetNodeType(). TypeReference represents a type expression (including generics, unions, arrays, tuples, and optionality), not a node locator. VariableRef and ScopedVariableRef refer to lexical bindings; RecordReference describes record-level mappings such as foreign keys. They must not be substituted for declaration identity. UIRRelationship connects From and To nodes with a relationship type such as call, reference, import, inheritance, implements, includes, foreign_key, read, or write. Statement-level call edges can leave From unset until a traversal attributes them to an enclosing declaration. NodeTree.GetRelationships() deduplicates by rendered endpoints and type, so it is not a lossless source of call occurrences.
356.title: Reference forms

357.text:
Every call occurrence carries a call locator: the enclosing declaration's identity key as enclosing_key, the structured target identifier as target, resolvable, local_root, statement path, range, and original text. In a syntax document the symbol is null and target is what the AST could name; in a typed document the symbol is the callee's canonical id, target names the callee's package and, for a method, the receiver type the type checker proved, and resolvable is whether the callee has a canonical symbol, so a call to an undefined function or a local closure is unresolved. Calls carry no target root, and query-time resolution does not use local_root. The compact query grammar compares canonical symbol ids: a reference is an occurrence whose symbol is the target's id, a definition a symbol entry with that id, an implementation a type whose implements names it, a caller a call occurrence of it, and a callee a call occurrence whose enclosing is it. One identity declared at several checkout heads resolves to one target with several declarations; different identities matching one spelling return candidates. Incoming method calls include known interface dispatch by default. Queries read the primary head of each selected root unless another indexed view is explicitly selected. They see nothing in syntax packages, which have no ids or postings, and only the proven facts of partial ones; every result lists such packages under coverage. uir query accepts these expressions: uir query 'example.org/service/invoices.InvoiceService.Approve <' --root example.org/service
uir query 'invoices.InvoiceService.Approve <' --root example.org/service --location .
uir query 'invoices.InvoiceService.Approve >' --snapshot 6f8b2c6e-79af-4b59-8736-e45696f0c546
uir query 'invoices.InvoiceService.Approve =' --root example.org/service
uir query 'invoices.InvoiceService :methods' --root example.org/service
uir query 'api.* >> invoices.InvoiceService.Approve' --root example.org/service These names are illustrative; inspect indexed symbols for a real module. See the query guide for grammar and resolution, and the storage design for snapshot scope. For an in-memory UIR document, NodeTree.Walk and structured identifier comparisons remain independent of the relational index. Find(...).WithName(...) compares GetName() and String(), but its skip-filter traversal may miss descendants of a heterogeneous root. Prefer Walk when searching the entire tree.
357.title: Persisted call projection and query behavior

358.text: storage.UirDB owns the GORM connection and applies the embedded Atlas HCL through commons-db/migrate. GORM models map rows; AutoMigrate does not own the schema. The seven base tables are specified by 04_module_roots.hcl and 05_source_deltas.hcl, the four symbol-index tables by 06_symbol_index.hcl, the handle registry by 07_symbol_handles.hcl, the kind registry and handle layout record by 10_symbol_kinds.hcl, and the symbol deltas by 13_layered_fingerprints.hcl; symbol index storage is their design, and compact symbol handles below describes the surrogate keys. The Facet ERD shows their keys and references. The integration tests assert, on both engines, that every model's columns and nullability match the migrated table and that every named index, foreign key, and check exists.
358.title: UIR storage design

359.title: Opening and cutover

360.text: Table / GORM modelIdentityResponsibilitymodules / ModuleRootunique root_key from go.mod, or from a publicationLogical Go module, or a root a non-Go producer publishes, independent of checkout path.locations / ModuleLocationunique (root_id, canonical_path)Physical checkout or nested module location, with optional parent, mount path, kind (module, git, or git-submodule), and repository URI; or, with kind external (LocationExternal), the URI a producer publishes the root from.primary_locations / ModulePrimaryone row per rootFirst registered location, used by default node queries and browse.snapshots / ModuleSnapshotUUID and unique ordinal; (root_id,id) and (location_id,id) for scoped referencesPublished index run for one root and location, optionally based on another snapshot of that root, with its worktree state, context hash, and coverage.location_heads / ModuleLocationHeadone row per locationSnapshot published for that checkout, with compare-and-swap version.source_revisions / SourceRevisionunique (root_id,path_key,content_hash,package_path)Reusable content-addressed file version: hash, package, and size, with no extracted facts.source_deltas / SourceDelta(snapshot_id,path_key)set to a revision of that path or delete tombstone.documents / Documentunique (root_id,path_key,content_digest)The facts extracted from one file version, keyed by DocumentDigest (revision, package path, indexer version, coverage, canonical content), so re-keyed packages whose files render the same keep their documents: a typed (indexed or partial) document from go/packages, a syntax document from the Go AST extractor when the package could not be loaded, or an empty excluded document. input_hash is provenance only.document_deltas / DocumentDelta(snapshot_ordinal,path_key)Per snapshot, how its path → document binding differs from its base's: set with a document ordinal of that root and path, or delete; a snapshot without a base sets every path.package_coverage / PackageCoverage(snapshot_id,package_path)Per snapshot, each package's analysis record: its input hash, coverage, export shape hash when indexed, file count, and diagnostics. It does not select documents.symbols / Symbol, symbol_postings / SymbolPostingid and unique handle; (document_ordinal,symbol_handle,role)Canonical symbol identities, global and never cascaded, each with a database-local handle, and the inverted index from each symbol handle to the documents that define, reference, or implement it.symbol_modules / SymbolModule, symbol_packages / SymbolPackagenumber, unique module_key; (module_number,number), unique (module_number,package_path)The numbering a handle packs: module keys and, per module, package paths.symbol_kinds / SymbolKindcode 1–63, unique nameThe kind registry a handle packs and symbols.kind references: the builtin kinds and the database's custom kinds, each with its category and namespace.symbol_layout / SymbolLayoutthe one row id = 1The bit layout the database's handles were packed with (H64b).symbol_deltas / SymbolDelta(snapshot_ordinal,symbol_handle)Per snapshot, how its defined-symbol set differs from its base's. root_key is the full module path, not a display basename. Canonical checkout path is physical location, not logical identity. Multiple worktrees and clones of one module share a root but keep separate heads. A source revision belongs to one root; reuse across its checkouts is intentional, but different module paths never share one row. The hash covers source bytes; package_path prevents reuse under a different interpretation, and extraction is versioned by the document key instead. The indexer supplies module-relative source paths, and the content reader rejects absolute or traversal paths; the HCL itself checks only that a stored path is nonempty. A snapshot references one root and one location in that root. A new location may base its first snapshot on the current primary head; subsequent runs base on its own head. Composite foreign keys enforce root agreement for locations, snapshots, bases, deltas, revisions, and documents; a head references its snapshot through (location_id, snapshot_id), so it cannot point at another location's snapshot, and a delta or document references its revision through (root_id, path_key, revision_id), so it cannot point at another path's revision. A snapshot row exists only once its publication committed, so there is no snapshot state and completed_at is always set. Each snapshot records why it was published (reason: add, reindex, refactor, local-dependency, versioned-dependency, historical, dependency-cycle, or import for a producer's publication; unknown only on rows published before reasons were recorded), when its extraction began (index_started_at), the task run that published it when one did (task_run_id), and its stats. storage.RecordSnapshotStats derives the stats inside the publication transaction from the rows it wrote: file_count, symbol_count, occurrence_count, and source_bytes from the effective documents and their source revisions, and files_added, files_changed, files_deleted, and symbols_changed from the snapshot's own source and symbol deltas. The change counts describe the publication against its original base and remain unchanged if pruning later rebases its physical storage; a snapshot published without a base counts every file as added. The stats columns are nullable only for rows published before they existed: opening the database backfills every such row with the same function, and reading a row without stats is an error. storage.ModuleSnapshots also derives each snapshot's kind: versioned when it has a module version, head when it is its checkout's head or another snapshot's base (every superseded head is the base of its successor), and historical otherwise. task_runs (09_task_runs.hcl) keeps the clicky task runs that finished, whichever uir process ran them. storage/taskruns.Store is the clicky RunStore every process installs while its database is open, so uir serve lists CLI runs and runs from before a restart beside its live ones, and opens their snapshots. A row holds the run's listing columns (kind, status, labels, start and finish), the errors of its failed tasks, the snapshot_ids it published (from the run's group details, which the indexer reads back from snapshots.task_run_id after each module), and the clicky run summary and task snapshots, each task bounded to its newest 500 log entries and the last 64 KiB of its output. A stored run cannot be controlled. An effective source set is not a full physical copy. storage.EffectiveSources resolves the whole base chain in one recursive CTE (WITH RECURSIVE plus ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY path_key ORDER BY depth), identical on SQLite and PostgreSQL) that returns the newest delta for each path, so the statement count does not grow with history depth; tombstones drop their path, and the referenced revisions are then loaded in batches of 256 and must match the delta's root and path. The walk is capped at 100,000 base links: a chain that reaches the cap with a base still pending is reported as a base cycle, a dangling base or a chain spanning roots fails, and a missing snapshot fails. storage.ActiveDocuments resolves a snapshot's path_key → document membership the same way from document_deltas (EffectiveDocumentOrdinals), then loads the bound documents by ordinal in batches; an unbound path, a document of another root, path, or revision, or a coverage row whose file count disagrees with the effective sources is an error. A database published before document deltas is cut over on its first read-write open (see document membership cutover); OpenReadOnly refuses it until then. storage.DecodeDocument validates a document against its revision before the indexer writes it and whenever a reader loads it, by the rules of its coverage: a syntax document has no ids; a typed document has an id and shape hash on every proven declaration, a role and either a symbol or a note on every occurrence, and enclosing ids declared in the same document; an excluded document is empty and states why. Document JSON preserves each declaration's canonical id, kind, visibility, shape, hashes, implemented interfaces, structured identifier, parent/slot/order, payload, semantic hash, name and extent ranges, optional field detail, and every identifier occurrence; these are not separate GORM node or relationship rows. Historical queries read the saved documents even after a later head changes or removes a file. Raw source bytes are not stored; source viewing verifies a local file's hash or a pinned Git blob against the saved hash, and fails if neither matches.
360.title: Relational hierarchy

361.text: indexer loads each module root once through golang.org/x/tools/go/packages (NeedName|NeedFiles|NeedSyntax|NeedTypes|NeedTypesInfo|NeedImports|NeedDeps|NeedModule) in the module directory, under the go env build variant the configuration hash records, with pattern ./... and test variants when tests are included. The whole dependency graph is type-checked from source. Every root file's bytes as parsed must hash to the discovered content hash, otherwise the run fails because the file changed while indexing. Extraction runs entirely before the publication transaction opens. Each discovered package gets one coverage. A file that build constraints exclude, or whose directory builds no package, is excluded, and a package whose every file is excluded is excluded. A parse error in a package's own files fails the run, as the AST extractor did. A go list error on the package itself (for example two package names in one directory), a variant without type information, or a file the load did not type-check makes the package syntax: its files keep the AST extractor's documents, with the load diagnostics attached, and have no postings. Any other error (type errors, an import that cannot be resolved) makes it partial: only proven facts are recorded, and the diagnostics are stored on the package row and on the documents they are positioned in. Otherwise it is indexed. A snapshot's coverage is the weakest of its packages' among indexed, partial, and syntax; excluded packages were deliberately not extracted, so a snapshot is excluded only when every package is, and indexed when it has no packages. Its diagnostics list, per package that is not indexed, the coverage and diagnostics. Canonical identities, visibility, shapes, and hashes follow symbol index storage. A symbol's search_name is SearchName(name): the name lowercased and restricted to [a-z0-9], empty when the name has none of those characters. Publication upserts symbols on id, refreshing search_name and visibility. package_coverage.export_shape_hash is set only for an indexed package. For the importers' input hashes every direct import still presents an export shape: the real one for a workspace package (the module's own, a go.work use module, or a directory replace) that type-checked without errors; for a workspace package with errors, whose shape is unproven, a digest of its package path, its files' names and content hashes, and its imports' export shapes, so any edit to it still re-extracts its importers; H(module path, version, toolchain) for a module-cache package (the replacement's path and version for a module replace); H("std", toolchain) for the standard library; and a digest of the path alone for an import no module provides.
361.title: Typed extraction

362.text: The SHA-256 symbol id remains the identity: documents, canonical keys, export shape hashes, and input hashes are unchanged, and nothing outside this database ever sees a handle. Inside it, postings and symbol deltas store compact surrogates instead of 64-character ids and UUIDs. Handle. symbols.handle is a unique bigint in the H64b layout of storage/symbolhandle, most significant bit first: 0 | module 11 | package 16 | visibility 1 | kind 6 | local 29 (KindBits, LocalBits). Visibility is 1 for exported; the kind is a code of the kind registry below. The sign bit is always zero, so handles sort by module, package, visibility, kind, then local, and symbolhandle.PackageRange, VisibilityRange, and BucketRange turn "every symbol of a package", "every exported symbol of a package", and "every exported func of a package" into one inclusive B-tree range. Pack fails naming the field that does not fit, and on the reserved kind 0; Unpack fails on a negative handle and on kind 0. H64b replaced H64a (kind 3 | local 32), which held only the eight Go kinds; a bucket now holds 2^29 locals.Kinds. Code 0 is reserved. The 18 builtin kinds are fixed in code and numbered upward from 1, each with a category: package 1 and module 9 are containers; type 2, interface 10, record 12, and table 14 are types; func 3, method 4, constructor 11, and endpoint 13 are callables; field 5, var 6, const 7, builtin 8, column 15, index 16, foreign_key 17, and annotation 18 are members. Opening a database inserts the builtins into symbol_kinds and fails if a stored builtin code names another kind. A non-Go producer declares a custom kind with storage.RegisterKind(ctx, db, "oipa.rule", symbolhandle.CategoryCallable): the name must be namespaced (<namespace>.<name>, lowercase; builtin names have no dot), registering the same name and category again returns its code, and another category is an error. A new custom kind takes the code below the lowest custom code in use, 63 for the first, read inside a transaction that RetryAllocationConflicts runs again when a concurrent registration took the same code or name; the code that would reach 18 is an error, the field being full. symbols.kind references symbol_kinds.name, so a symbol of an unregistered kind is refused, and AssignSymbolHandles resolves every kind through LoadSymbolKinds before it registers anything. The query layer reads categories, not kind names: func: selects callables, type: and struct: types, < and > read call occurrences of callables, and a member is named as a field of its owner.Registry. symbol_modules numbers module keys: '' (builtins) is 0, std is 1, every other key the next number from 2, up to 2047. symbol_packages numbers each module's package paths from 0, up to 65535. Check constraints enforce both ranges and the reserved numbers.Locals. A new symbol takes the next local of its (module, package, visibility, kind) bucket: 0 in a package the same allocation registered, otherwise one past the bucket's largest stored handle, read by ORDER BY handle DESC LIMIT 1 over the bucket's range of symbols_handle_key. No sequence or counter table exists. storage.AssignSymbolHandles allocates the rows it is given in their order and missing registry numbers in key order, so replaying the same publications produces the same handles. A stored symbol keeps its handle, and a stored handle that disagrees with the row's module, package, visibility, or kind is an error; since visibility is in the handle, a symbol whose derived visibility changes cannot be re-published and fails loudly.Ordinals. modules.ordinal (integer), snapshots.ordinal (bigint), and documents.ordinal (bigint) are unique, dense, database-local numbers from 1, allocated as one past the current maximum inside the publication transaction (storage.NextModuleOrdinal, storage.NextSnapshotOrdinal, storage.NextDocumentOrdinal; storage.CreateModuleRoot and storage.CreateSnapshot assign the ordinal themselves, storage.CreateDocument takes one the publisher assigned). A publication that loses the race for a document key to another writer leaves a gap in document ordinals; nothing depends on density.Postings. symbol_postings (document_ordinal bigint, root_ordinal integer, symbol_handle bigint, role integer, occurrence_count integer): role is 0 definition, 1 reference, 2 implements (only in documents older than format 6), or 3 embeds (storage.PostingRole). Implements facts are snapshot-level since format 6: implements_deltas and implements_facts, read through EffectiveImplements (design). The primary key (document_ordinal, symbol_handle, role) serves the per-document probe and the document cascade; symbol_postings_symbol_idx (symbol_handle, role, root_ordinal, document_ordinal) serves the per-symbol range. The root ordinal is the discriminator a reference lookup filters on, so a range over one root never reads other roots' postings; the publisher takes it from the document's root. Foreign keys reference documents(ordinal) and modules(ordinal) with CASCADE and symbols(handle) with NO ACTION.Concurrency. Every allocation reads the current maximum inside the publication transaction and relies on the unique keys to reject a duplicate. On PostgreSQL a concurrent publisher that took the same number makes the insert block and then fail with a unique violation (or a deadlock or serialization failure); those SQLSTATEs (23505, 40P01, 40001) at an allocating insert, and a symbol a concurrent publisher inserted with a different handle, are wrapped as storage.ErrAllocationConflict. storage.RetryAllocationConflicts runs the publication transaction again from the start, at most storage.AllocationAttempts (3) times; indexer.IndexModules and IndexRevision publish through it. Any other error is returned at once, and the head compare-and-swap still fails a publication whose head moved. SQLite has one writer, so it never retries.
362.title: Compact symbol handles

363.text: symbol_deltas (snapshot_ordinal bigint, root_ordinal integer, symbol_handle bigint, operation text, public_fp bigint?, private_fp bigint?, content_fp bigint?, content_generation bigint?) (13_layered_fingerprints.hcl) records, per snapshot, how its defined-symbol set differs from its base's. The defined set is every declaration with a canonical id in the snapshot's active documents; syntax declarations and unproven declarations of a partial document have no id and no handle and are never in it, so a package falling back to syntax deletes its symbols from the set. A fingerprint is the first eight bytes of the public_hash, private_hash, or content_hash as a signed int64 (storage.SymbolFingerprint). set carries all three fingerprints and delete none, which symbol_deltas_operation_check enforces. The primary key is (snapshot_ordinal, symbol_handle), and symbol_deltas_handle_idx (symbol_handle, snapshot_ordinal) serves one symbol's history. Foreign keys reference snapshots(ordinal) and modules(ordinal) with CASCADE, so the rows go with their snapshot or root, and symbols(handle) with NO ACTION. Unlike source deltas, no composite key ties the root ordinal to the snapshot's root; the publisher takes them from the snapshot it just created and that snapshot's root. The base-chain walk carries each snapshot's ordinal, so EffectiveSymbols and DefinedSymbols join the deltas on it. content_generation is the symbol's content generation at that link (storage.NextContentGeneration): 1 where the chain first defines it, the base's value when content_fp is unchanged, one more otherwise or on a re-add, and on a delete the value the symbol ended at. Publication reads the base's values for the handles it writes through SymbolGenerations, and pruning copies them into a rebased snapshot. It is null only on rows published before it existed: the symbol generation cutover (23_symbol_generations.hcl, symbol_generation_backfill) fills them on the first read-write open, one transaction per snapshot in ordinal order, resuming from its marker, and OpenReadOnly refuses a database whose cutover is incomplete. The publisher writes them in the publication transaction. It compares only the packages with a path whose bound document differs from the base's (added, removed, or rebound), each whole: the base's stored documents of all its paths, and the extraction for all its files. Documents of other packages are never read. Declarations are grouped by id across those documents; a symbol present on both sides with equal fingerprints, such as one that moved between two changed files, gets no row, a new or changed one gets set, and one only the base declared gets delete. A snapshot without a base records every defined symbol as set; a dependency bump that rebinds no document records nothing. This is sound because a canonical id includes its Go package, whose files share one directory, and a changed package is compared whole: a symbol that loses a declaration in a changed file while keeping another in an unchanged sibling is still folded over both. The publisher checks that every id it reads is declared in one package directory and fails otherwise. Go never declares one id twice, since each func init carries its own discriminator, but a producer may declare one id in several files; storage.FoldDeclarations combines such declarations order-independently, keeping a single declaration's fingerprints and otherwise hashing the distinct triples sorted by public, private, then content, each layer separately, so a body edit of one declaration that keeps its shape changes only the folded content fingerprint.
363.title: Symbol deltas

364.text: FunctionReturnsEffectiveSymbols(ctx, db, snapshotID)[]EffectiveSymbol{Handle int64; PublicFP, PrivateFP, ContentFP *int64} sorted by handle: one recursive CTE over symbol_deltas along the base chain, the newest row per handle, tombstones dropped. A base cycle (over 100,000 links), a dangling base, a chain spanning roots, and a missing snapshot are errors, as for EffectiveSources; so is a set row without fingerprints.DefinedSymbols(ctx, db, snapshotID, handles)The sorted, distinct subset of handles the snapshot defines: the EffectiveSymbols CTE restricted, before ranking, to IN batches of 256 handles, so its cost follows the handles asked about rather than the size of the snapshot. An empty list reads nothing; the chain errors are those of EffectiveSymbols.SymbolHandles(ctx, db, ids) / SymbolIDs(ctx, db, handles)map[string]int64 / map[int64]string, in IN batches of 256; an unknown id or handle is an error.DocumentOrdinals(ctx, db, ids) / DocumentIDs(ctx, db, ordinals)map[uuid.UUID]int64 / map[int64]uuid.UUID; unknown keys are errors. Document.Ordinal is also loaded with every document row, so ActiveDocuments already carries it.RootOrdinal(ctx, db, rootID)The root's int32 ordinal; ModuleRoot.Ordinal carries it too.NextModuleOrdinal, NextSnapshotOrdinal, NextDocumentOrdinal / CreateModuleRoot, CreateSnapshot, CreateDocumentOne past the table's largest ordinal (1 when empty), read inside the publication transaction / the inserts that use them. CreateModuleRoot and CreateSnapshot assign the ordinal themselves and refuse a row that already has one; CreateDocument requires the ordinal the publisher assigned and reports whether it inserted the row, a repeat of the (root_id, path_key, content_digest) key being a no-op. A lost race for an ordinal is ErrAllocationConflict.ActiveDocuments(ctx, db, snapshotID, ActiveDocumentOptions{Content})The snapshot's path_key → ActiveDocument membership. Without Content each document row omits its content column, so a reader such as symboldiff finds the paths it needs first and loads only those with DocumentContents; the query layer passes Content: true.DocumentContents(ctx, db, ids)map[uuid.UUID]JSON: the content of the given documents, in IN batches of 256; an unknown id is an error.DefinitionPostings(ctx, db, ordinals)The definition postings of the given documents, sorted by document ordinal then symbol handle: a prefix scan of the posting primary key per batch of 256 ordinals.OwnedSymbols(ctx, db, handles), OwnedSymbol.Identifier(), DeclarationIdentifier(packagePath, symbol, owners)Symbol rows with their owner names, outermost first, loaded by following owner_id in batches (an unknown handle or owner is an error), and the structured identifier the typed extractor gives a declaration. DeclarationIdentifier is the single rule: the indexer calls it for declarations the AST extractor does not project, and Identifier() applies it to a stored row.ParsePostingRole(name), PostingRole.String()The role code of definition, reference, implements, or embeds, and back.SymbolFingerprint(hash), DocumentSymbol.Fingerprints(), FoldDeclarations(triples)The fingerprint of a document's hash, and the fold of several declarations, to compare documents with deltas.symbolhandle.Pack, Unpack, PackageRange, VisibilityRange, BucketRange, ParseVisibility, ReservedModuleNumberHandle layout arithmetic; a range is symbolhandle.Range{Low, High}, inclusive, with Contains. MaxModule, MaxPackage, MaxLocal, and MaxKind are the field capacities, MaxBuiltinKind the highest builtin code, and Layout the layout name a database records.symbolhandle.BuiltinKinds, Builtins, NewKinds, Kinds.Lookup, Kinds.Spec, Kinds.InCategory, ValidateCustomKind, KindNamespace, ParseCategoryThe builtin kinds and a registry over them and a database's custom kinds, by name, code, and category; an unregistered name or code is an error.RegisterKind(ctx, db, name, category), KindCode(ctx, db, name), LoadSymbolKinds(ctx, db)Register a namespaced custom kind and get its code; look a kind's code up; load the database's registry.DecodeDocument(document, source, WithKinds(kinds))Without WithKinds a document may use only the builtin kinds; the query layer passes the database's registry. A file declares any registered kind except a container or builtin, and only the builtin type kind has a Go type form. The query layer reads postings through these mappings (query/module_index.go): it resolves ids to handles, roles to codes, and each scope's active documents to ordinals, filters symbol_postings by (symbol_handle IN, role IN, root_ordinal), and maps the rows back. Whether a scope defines a symbol comes from DefinedSymbols, remembered per snapshot for the query (query/module_index_handles.go), so a definition lookup skips a root whose every scope is known not to define the symbol, and name resolution reads reference postings, then the scopes' implements facts, only for the symbols no scope defines. Typed selectors read their candidates through symbolhandle ranges (query/selector_ranges.go): a pkg: selector, or a symbol selector qualified by a package path, becomes the ranges of the matching registered packages, and any other selector each admitted root module's whole range, ORed into handle BETWEEN conditions over symbols_handle_key instead of a scan of symbols. symboldiff reads both sides' ActiveDocuments without content, classifies from EffectiveSymbols and the changed documents' DefinitionPostings, names rows it did not decode with OwnedSymbols, and loads only the documents its output needs with DocumentContents.
364.title: API for query and diff consumers

365.text: PruneHistory(ctx, db, rootKey, keep) (PruneResult, error) deletes, in one transaction per root, the root's snapshots older than its newest keep (by ordinal) and the rows only they used; uir prune [root] --keep N (POST /api/v1/modules/prune) runs it for one root or for every root in turn. keep below 1 and an unregistered root are errors. Kept: the newest keep snapshots, every location head of the root whatever its age, and, until none is added, every snapshot that a dependency edge of a surviving snapshot of any root targets.Rebased: a kept snapshot whose base is deleted gets one set source delta and one set document delta per effective path and one set symbol and implements delta per effective symbol and implements fact, loses its base, and has its stats recorded again (so it counts every file as added). It serves exactly the sources, symbols, and documents it served before.Deleted, in foreign-key order: the superseded snapshots, newest first, whose source, document, and symbol deltas, package coverage, and outgoing dependency edges cascade; the root's documents no kept snapshot activates, with their postings; the root's source revisions no remaining source delta or document names; the source blobs whose content hash no remaining revision of any root has; and the symbols a deleted posting or delta named that no remaining posting or symbol delta names, except an owner of a symbol that stays, deleting owned symbols before their owner.Epoch: a prune that deletes anything advances the one-row history_prunes.epoch (11_history_prunes.hcl). A deleted symbol published again gets a new handle, so query.Pipeline reads the epoch in its cache token and discards the symbols, snapshots, and documents it kept when it moves. PruneResult reports the root key, the snapshots kept and rebased, and the rows deleted from snapshots, documents, symbol_postings, source_revisions, source_blobs, and symbols; a second prune with the same keep deletes nothing and leaves the epoch alone.
365.title: Pruning history

366.text: Discovery, type-checking, hashing, and document rendering complete before publication. Source-revision writes, symbol writes, document writes, and posting writes occur inside the IndexModules transaction, which then writes the snapshot row, its source deltas, package coverage, and symbol deltas, and advances the location head with a version check; a failed check rolls every row back. Symbols needed by new documents get their handles, are upserted owners first, and are re-read, and an existing row whose canonical_key, facts, or handle differ from the extraction's is a hard error (a different handle is an allocation conflict). Every document is validated by DecodeDocument against its revision before it is written; the extraction verifies that each typed entry's kind and visibility equal its symbol row and that every referenced id is a known symbol. Revisions, documents, and package rows are inserted with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING and re-read, so a re-run never duplicates them; postings are written only by the publication that inserted their document, so an existing document's postings are skipped, not duplicated. A forced re-extraction whose document differs from the stored one under the same key fails, because a changed extractor needs a new indexer version. A syntax error or conflicting writer aborts that call. Selected external go.work use paths are indexed in a later call and therefore a separate transaction. A snapshot can have zero source deltas: a revision-only change, a dependency-manifest change, or a configuration change publishes one. A run avoids a new snapshot only when its Git revision, content-set hash, configuration hash, and context hash all equal the base snapshot's and --force is not used. The content-set hash covers the included .go files plus go.mod, go.sum, and the enclosing workspace's go.work and go.work.sum when present; those manifests are hashed, never stored as source revisions. The configuration hash covers the indexer version, test inclusion, and the go env build variant (GOOS, GOARCH, CGO_ENABLED, GOVERSION, build tags). Multiple Git roots and clones: Git repository boundaries and Go module boundaries are different. go.mod defines root identity; the nearest checkout supplies Git provenance. Two modules in one Git repository have distinct roots; two clones of the same module path share a root but retain distinct heads. Remote URI is diagnostic, not identity.Nested modules and submodules: discovery excludes a nested module's Go files from its parent scan. The child location stores its nearest parent and mount path; .gitmodules may mark a declared submodule. A nested module without .git is still separate. Not every Git submodule contains a go.mod, and not every nested go.mod is a submodule.External workspace modules: go.work can refer outside the selected directory. Add indexes only the selected directory unless --all is given, which also adds those external use paths and fails on a missing one. Because publication calls are separate, inspect every returned result.Moved checkout: canonical path is the location key. Moving a directory registers a new location; it does not rewrite the old location or historical snapshots. The primary remains first-registered, so default queries can still point to an unavailable checkout. Select --location or --snapshot when needed. Primary reassignment does not exist.Branch switches and dirty trees: snapshots describe indexed bytes, not branch names. A Git revision change creates a new snapshot even if the content set is unchanged. worktree_state includes changes under the module, its active workspace manifest, and linked local dependencies. Dirty Git-backed snapshots record git-{commit}-dirty-{latest UTC file mtime} in revision and keep the raw SHA in git_commit; unknown has an empty revision outside a Git checkout. source_blobs retain source bytes for dirty and non-Git snapshots, and source reads always verify the saved hash.Symlinks and mounts: input paths are canonicalized, directory symlinks are not traversed during discovery, and source viewing rejects paths escaping a registered location. The database cannot prove that a path still points to the same physical mount.Call graph ambiguity: typed documents record each call's canonical symbol id, and compact <, >, <<, and >> queries read those edges from active documents. Ambiguous spellings return candidates. Known interface dispatch through a receiver's recorded implementations is included; syntax packages, which have no ids or postings, and dependencies outside indexed roots prevent a sound whole-program graph. Unresolved call locators remain in documents but have no canonical query edge.Retention and read cost: snapshots, dependency edges, source blobs, source revisions, and documents are retained until PruneHistory deletes them; nothing prunes on its own. Documents are keyed by content digest, so editing one file re-renders its package but stores a new document only for each file whose rendering changed. Long base chains cost more to reconstruct, and browse currently materializes all nodes in a snapshot. Never delete a base snapshot by hand while descendants reference it; PruneHistory rebases them first. Pre-existing snapshots have a null dependency_set_hash and report dependencies as not captured. See module indexing, querying, and serving for the operational contracts. HCL and integration tests are the executable schema specification.
366.title: Publication and adversarial boundaries

367.text:
uir records which tests ran against exactly which indexed snapshot, with what outcome and coverage, so it can tell a regression from a flaky test. It never runs tests, parses test runner output, or finds tests in source: a producer such as gavel reports what the runner ran. uir add .
go test -coverprofile=cover.out ./...   # through gavel, which writes results.json
uir tests import results.json --coverprofile cover.out
uir tests flaky --since 168h
uir query 'SELECT symbol.name, symbol.generation, symbol.test_coverage FROM func:* WHERE symbol.test_coverage < 0.5'
367.title: Test runs, coverage and flakiness

368.title: Import contract

369.text: Each run says which code it ran on, and the import stores it against that code's snapshot. git_commit is the full SHA of HEAD when the tests ran. It is required.dirty is true when the worktree had uncommitted changes to indexed inputs.git_tree is required when dirty is true. It is the Git tree hash of the repository's working tree when the tests ran, uncommitted and untracked non-ignored files included, without the producer's own results file. The producer computes it at the repository's top level through a temporary index: GIT_INDEX_FILE=<tmp> git read-tree HEAD && git add -A && git write-tree. RunBound toCleanThe newest clean snapshot of git_commit that serves test files. When there is none, the commit is indexed with its test files in a temporary worktree, as uir diff --auto-index does, from --location first, then any registered checkout of the root that has the commit. No checkout's worktree, index or head changes, and the checkout's own state does not matter: results from an old commit import while the checkout is many commits ahead and dirty.DirtyA fresh snapshot of the checkout, if it is still exactly the code the tests ran on: its HEAD is git_commit and its working tree, hashed the same way (excluding the imported results file when it lies inside the repository), is git_tree. The checkout is then indexed with its test files, as uir reindex --include-tests does, producing a dirty snapshot. Checkouts are tried from --location first. If no registered checkout matches, the code changed since the tests ran, and the import fails: rerun the tests. The hash uses a temporary index, so the checkout's own index and working tree are untouched.Dirty without git_tree, or no git_commitNothing: the import fails. The root is --root, by default the module of the working directory's checkout. A snapshot "serves test files" when it holds at least one _test.go document; a snapshot indexed without --include-tests holds none. The runs of one file may be bound to different snapshots of the same root. A run's id derives from its snapshot and content, so importing the same file twice records it once.
369.title: Which snapshot a run is bound to

370.text: 24_tests.hcl adds: TableHoldstest_casesOne row per test ever reported for a root: framework, package, length-delimited suite path and name. symbol_handle links it to the declaration it is: a go test test to the func of its top-level name in its file, any other framework to the innermost proven declaration enclosing its reported line. A test whose file the snapshot did not index has no link. Pruning counts the link as a reference.test_runsOne row per run: its snapshot (set to null when pruning deletes the snapshot), producer, environment and its digest.test_resultsOne row per test, run and attempt, with the result's closure fingerprint and closure source.test_coveragePer run, or per test for per-test profiles, the statements and covered statements per document and proven declaration (symbol_handle 0 is file scope), with the declaration's content_fp and content_generation at the run's snapshot. Rows cascade with their document.
370.title: Tables

371.text: Each coverage block is attributed to the innermost proven declaration whose extent lines contain it, or to file scope. Lines are compared, not columns, because profiles count columns in bytes and documents in UTF-16 units. A block naming a path the snapshot does not serve, or crossing a declaration boundary, fails the import with its position. symbol.test_coverage is the share of a symbol's statements the newest run's aggregate coverage executed, and symbol.test_coverage_generation the generation it was measured at. Coverage is reused on a later snapshot only while the symbol's content_fp there equals the one it was measured at, so an unrelated edit keeps it and a body edit drops it to NULL. Neither field decodes documents.
371.title: Coverage

372.text: closure_fingerprint digests the source, the snapshot's dependency set hash, the run's inputs_digest, and the sorted (canonical id, content_fp) pairs of the symbols the test depends on. closure_source says how that set was found, without silent fallback between groups: SourceSymbolsWhencoverageDeclarations with covered statements in the test's own coverage, plus the static setThe test carried its own coverage and the static set is completestaticThe test symbol and the symbols its graph reaches inside the indexed roots through calls, variable reads and variable writes, to depth 8 and 1000 nodesThe test is linked and the graph is complete: no unresolved call, nothing cut by depth or limitsnapshotThe whole snapshot (content set and context hashes)Otherwise uir tests flaky reports a test when results with the same closure source, closure fingerprint and environment both passed and failed, or when one run's attempts both failed and passed. Results across a changed closure or a different environment are never compared. It is computed from test_results on each call; nothing is stored.
372.title: Flakiness

373.text: Non-Go inputs. Embedded SQL, testdata, templates and configuration files are not symbols, so they are in no closure. A test that fails because such a file changed looks flaky unless the producer supplies inputs_digest.Directive comments. //go:embed and marker comments do not change content_fp.Test code is not instrumented by Go coverage, so a coverage closure always includes the test's static set; a test without one gets snapshot.Ginkgo specs are not symbols. A spec links only when a proven declaration encloses its line, and then its static graph is that declaration's; an unlinked spec falls back to snapshot.Static graphs follow a function a variable's value names, such as map[string]func(){"x": Other}, through the read of that variable. A function stored into a variable elsewhere, such as by a registration call, is reached only if the walk passes through the code that stores it.Dirty runs import only while the checkout still holds the code they ran on, so import them right after the tests.Only tests a run reported are known: a test that never ran is not in test_cases.Only aggregate coverage is collected by default. Per-test coverage needs one profile per test from the producer.
373.title: Limits

374.text: The current document format is 12. Format 8 added resolved declared_type for proven package-level variables, format 9 made declaration keys unique within a document (including separate Go init functions), format 10 added producer metric measures, format 11 records file imports and syntax-level package variables and constants, and format 12 records each Go declaration's own effects under effects_recorded. Older supported documents remain immutable; queries that require unavailable facts fail with reindex or republish guidance. See the query guide, stored metrics, and diff guide for the current user-facing contracts. Status: Implemented. The schema is created by migrations 04_module_roots.hcl, 05_source_deltas.hcl, 06_symbol_index.hcl, and 07_symbol_handles.hcl; this document is the design record of that change, which renamed and revised the seven uir_-prefixed tables and added four, and of the compact handles that followed it. The ERD shows the model. Compact handles (landed 2026-09-27). The SHA-256 symbol id is still the identity everywhere outside the database: documents, canonical keys, export shape hashes, input hashes, and every API and JSON result. Inside it, each symbol also has a database-local 64-bit handle (H64b: 0 | module 11 | package 16 | visibility 1 | kind 6 | local 29, numbered through the symbol_modules, symbol_packages, and symbol_kinds registries), and modules, snapshots, and documents have dense database-local ordinals. Postings are keyed by document ordinal, symbol handle, and an integer role, and a new symbol_deltas table records per snapshot how its defined-symbol set changed, with layered (public, private, content) fingerprints. Queries answer "does this snapshot define it" from the deltas and read selector candidates through handle ranges; the diff classifies from the fingerprints and reads only the documents its output needs. A database of the previous generation keeps its registrations and loses its index on open, and uir reindex rebuilds it. The tables below describe the landed schema; the evaluation and measurements are in compact symbol handles and symbol deltas, and the operational detail in the storage design. The query syntax in the original design record below has been superseded by the compact query grammar.
374.title: Snapshot-aware symbol index: schema review

375.text: Store, for every indexed file version, one document holding the facts extracted from it: the symbols it declares with their signatures and hashes, the symbols it mentions, and where. When the package type-checks those facts are compiler-proven; otherwise the document holds the syntax-only projection the AST extractor produces today. A reference result must include the source filename and exact range from the selected snapshot. Resolving a symbol's declaration is a second lookup against files active in the selected branch or snapshot, so one symbol identity may have several declaration locations across checkout heads. A diff between two commits must list symbols added, removed, and changed, filtered by visibility, and attribute line additions and removals to file and symbol. Clean Go source bytes can be read from the pinned Git commit or a hash-matching checkout. Dirty, non-Git, and generated external sources are stored as blobs; external producers can also supply explicit Git source bindings. The database retains hashes, symbol identities, immutable content-addressed documents, an inverted index from symbol to the documents that mention it, and per-snapshot deltas. Documents retain positions and full per-symbol public, private, and content hashes; symbol deltas keep a 64-bit fingerprint of each. Historical source viewing and line diffs require hash-verified bytes. Stored file and callable metrics remain queryable without those bytes: migration 19_metrics.hcl adds immutable source_metrics by source revision and metric version, plus declaration_metrics by document ordinal and declaration key, projecting canonical handles, name positions, parameter counts, and optional body spans. Publication writes them atomically with their source revisions and documents; pruning cascades their deletion. Migration does not backfill metrics, so a query requesting unavailable metrics fails with reindex or republish guidance. Document format 10 adds measures, a producer's own integer metric values per declaration, which 22_producer_metrics.hcl stores in declaration_measures beside the kinds' declared metrics in symbol_kind_metrics (producer metrics). The schema uses the repository's portable Atlas HCL subset: uuid, text, integer/bigint, jsonb, and timestamptz; column-based B-tree indexes; primary, unique, foreign-key, and check constraints. PostgreSQL uses those types directly. The SQLite adapter maps them to compatible types and keeps keys and indexes. No view, materialized view, trigger, GIN, trigram, expression index, sequence, or column collation is required, because none of those is portable. In the tables below, every column is NOT NULL unless suffixed with ?. PK and UQ each imply an index. All paths are module-relative slash-separated path_key values. All line and UTF-16 column numbers are one-based; byte offsets are zero-based, with an exclusive end offset. Every foreign key uses ON UPDATE NO ACTION; its ON DELETE action is shown with the reference, and unqualified NO ACTION means deletion is blocked while a referencing row remains.
375.title: Goal and storage boundary

376.text: TableColumnsKeysReferences and checksuir_module_rootsid uuid, root_key text, name text, created_at timestamptzPK id; UQ root_keylength(root_key) > 0uir_module_locationsid uuid, root_id uuid, canonical_path text, parent_location_id uuid?, mount_path text, kind text, repository_uri text?, created_at timestamptzPK id; UQ (root_id,id); UQ (root_id,canonical_path)root_id → roots.id CASCADE; parent_location_id → locations.id NO ACTION; length(canonical_path) > 0uir_module_snapshotsid uuid, root_id uuid, location_id uuid, base_snapshot_id uuid?, state text, revision text, content_set_hash text, configuration_hash text, extractor_version text, started_at timestamptz, completed_at timestamptz?PK id; UQ (root_id,id); index (location_id,started_at)root_id → roots.id CASCADE; (root_id,location_id) → locations(root_id,id) CASCADE; (root_id,base_snapshot_id) → snapshots(root_id,id) NO ACTION; state IN ('building','ready','failed')uir_module_location_headsroot_id uuid, location_id uuid, snapshot_id uuid, version bigintPK location_id(root_id,location_id) → locations(root_id,id) CASCADE; UQ (root_id,id); UQ (root_id,path_key,content_hash,package_path,extractor_version)root_id → roots.id CASCADE; length(path_key) > 0; size_bytes >= 0uir_source_deltassnapshot_id uuid, root_id uuid, path_key text, revision_id uuid?, operation textPK (snapshot_id,path_key); index (revision_id)(root_id,snapshot_id) → snapshots(root_id,id) CASCADE; (root_id,revision_id) → source_revisions(root_id,id) NO ACTION; set requires a revision and delete forbids one Weaknesses in this model, each fixed in the base schema below: a head's snapshot is not tied to the head's location; a delta's revision is not tied to the delta's path; building and failed are never observable, because publication is one transaction; extractor_version on snapshots duplicates configuration_hash; the syntax projection is a second document per file once typed documents exist, and every nodes query decodes all of them; base_snapshot_id and parent_location_id have no index behind their NO ACTION references; kind is unchecked; revision may be empty; and the snapshot trigger hashes only .go bytes.

377.title: Base schema

378.text: Before this design, indexer/discovery.go hashed only .go files into ContentSetHash, and indexer/modules.go skipped snapshot creation when revision, content-set hash, configuration hash, and extractor version matched the base. Under that rule a go get -u, a go.work edit, or an exported-type change in a workspace sibling produces no snapshot and has nowhere to record new facts. Three changes to that seam are part of this design. ContentSetHash also covers the dependency manifests: go.mod and go.sum under their module-relative paths, and the workspace's go.work and go.work.sum (found through go env GOWORK, which may sit above the module) under the fixed keys go.work and go.work.sum. A dependency bump then yields a snapshot with zero source deltas, which the storage layer already permits.ConfigurationHash covers the indexer version and the build variant: GOOS, GOARCH, build tags, CGO_ENABLED, and the Go toolchain version. Exactly one variant is indexed per snapshot; a second variant is a configuration change and a new snapshot.The unchanged check compares revision, content_set_hash, configuration_hash, and context_hash (defined below) with the base snapshot. The last catches a workspace sibling whose export shape changed while this module's bytes did not. worktree_state is clean when git status --porcelain reports no changes under the module and every indexed file is tracked by Git (git ls-files), dirty otherwise, and unknown without Git, in which case revision is empty. Discovery excludes Git-ignored files, while the tracked-file check ensures that an untracked source is not recorded as clean. A commit-to-commit diff must know whether a snapshot's bytes are the commit's bytes.
378.title: Snapshot trigger

379.text: All digests are lowercase hexadecimal SHA-256 of a versioned, length-delimited canonical encoding. Symbol identity. symbols.id digests (identity_version, module_key, package_path, kind, owner_id, name, ordered parameter type identities). canonical_key stores that encoding and is unique, so an insert verifies that an existing digest has exactly the expected value. Parameter names, return types, field types, source path, line, and bodies do not enter identity. module_key is the Go module path (root_key for indexed roots), std for the standard library, and empty only for kind = 'builtin'. Parameter types use fully qualified named types and recursively encoded composite types; type parameters are encoded by ordinal. Local bindings, parameters, and labels are not canonical symbols: their occurrences stay inside the document with a null symbol, because they are never referenced across files. Canonical identities exist only for typed documents; a syntax document's symbol entries carry the v1 IdentityKey() and a null id, because unresolved parameter types cannot produce a trustworthy identity. Visibility. A symbol is exported when its name is exported and every owner in its chain is exported; otherwise it is internal. A method on an unexported type is therefore internal even though its name is capitalised. Symbol layers. Every proven symbol carries three Merkle-nested hashes, the same layers uir.Fingerprint defines for UIR nodes: LayerHashWhat it digestspublicpublic_hashpublic_shape: what a consumer outside the symbol's package observes. A struct's exported fields (an embedded exported type counts) with their tags, an interface's exported methods and type-set terms, each followed by an opaque line when unexported members exist, since those still decide comparability and whether an unkeyed literal compiles. For functions, methods, variables, constants, aliases, and other named types the public shape is the whole declaration.privateprivate_hashpublic_hash and shape, the full declared structure: the complete signature including parameter names, results, and variadic-ness; every field with its name, type, tag, and embedding; the method set; the underlying type; the type and, for constants, the value. Because it digests public_hash, a public change is always a private change.contentcontent_hashThe token stream of the declaration's extent with comments, whitespace, and layout tokens removed, and every name the declaration binds renamed to its position: the implementation. Layout tokens are statement separators before a closing ) or }, another separator, or the end; trailing commas before ) or }; and the var, const, or type keyword of an ungrouped declaration, so moving it into a group changes nothing. The renamed names are the receiver, parameters, results, type parameters, and local variables, constants, and types; a selector, a label, a field or method name, and an identifier key of a composite literal keep their spelling. A renamed parameter therefore changes public_hash and private_hash but not content_hash. Equal identity and equal public_hash mean the same interface to code outside the package; a differing private_hash with an equal public_hash is a structure-only change (adding an unexported field to an exported struct that already had one), and a differing content_hash with equal shape hashes is an implementation-only change. shape and public_shape are rendered in a canonical layout chosen so that two shapes diff line by line: a function or method signature is one line; a struct renders one field per line and an interface one method per line, each line gofmt-aligned, between a type Name struct { or interface { line and a closing }; a variable or constant is one line with its type and, for constants, its value. Each shape hash digests its rendering, so a shape diff never differs from a hash change. An unexported symbol's public shape follows the same rules. Export shape. export_shape_hash(P) (uir-export-shape-v4) digests the sorted (symbol id, API shape) pairs of P's exported symbols, a (type id, promoted selectors) pair for every exported defined type that promotes exported methods or fields through an embedded field (exported or not, from P or another package), and the export_shape_hash of only the packages whose named types P's exported API reaches (indexer.apiReferences: exported signatures, fields, embedded fields of any visibility, constraints, and P's own unexported types an exported signature names), so adding an unexported field to an exported type re-extracts nothing outside P, and a change in a package P imports but does not name in its API re-extracts nothing outside P either. The API shape is the public layer encoded without names an importer cannot depend on: types are qualified by import path, and receiver, parameter, result, and type parameter names are left out (type parameter constraints, variadic-ness, field names, tags, embedding, the opaque marker, and constant values stay). public_hash keeps those names, because the diff reports them as signature changes, so a parameter rename changes public_hash but no importer's input, and retargeting an import from foo/v1 to bar/v1 changes the export shape even where v1.Client reads the same. Because it recurses through the packages an API references, a public change in an exported type that an API names, directly or through another API, changes every such dependent's shape; a change behind a private import does not. That is sound only because a document holds no closure facts: implements, which once listed interfaces from the whole import closure, is a snapshot-level fact (below). A known gap the transitive shape shared: a method of an unexported type of another package that an exported API names only through inference (var V = dep.New() returning dep.impl) is in no export shape. For a package outside the indexed roots it is H(module path, module version, toolchain version); for the standard library it is H("std", toolchain version). Neither requires type-checking the dependency. A workspace package that did not reach indexed coverage has no proven shape and therefore no export_shape_hash; as an import it contributes a stand-in digest of its file hashes and its own imports' shapes, so its importers still re-extract when it changes, and an import that no module provides contributes its import path. The module's own packages must still be type-checked to compute context_hash, so the unchanged decision is cheap only for dependencies; skipping the type-check when the content set, manifests and sibling shapes are all unchanged is a benchmark-step optimization. Package input hash. input_hash(P) digests (configuration_hash, package_path, sorted (path_key, content_hash) of P's files, sorted (import path, export_shape_hash) of P's direct imports). Two files of one package share it. It is the complete input to extracting P: same input hash, same documents. The converse does not hold: a changed input hash often renders byte-identical documents, which is why documents are not keyed by it. Snapshot context hash. context_hash(S) digests (configuration_hash, sorted (package_path, input_hash) of every package in the module). Document key. A document is identified by (root_id, path_key, content_digest). content_digest (storage.DocumentDigest, uir-document-digest-v1) is the SHA-256 of a length-delimited encoding of the document's source revision id, package path, indexer version, coverage, and canonical content (decoded and re-encoded with sorted keys and numbers as written, so the digest of rendered bytes equals the digest of what PostgreSQL's jsonb returns). The same bytes extracted under a changed dependency that render the same document keep it, with its ordinal and postings; a different rendering is a new document, and the old one remains valid for older snapshots. documents.input_hash stays as provenance, the package input hash the document was first rendered under; nothing selects by it.
