length(import_path) > 0; export_shape_hash IS NULL OR length(export_shape_hash) = 64; source_digest IS NULL OR length(source_digest) = 64 (15_snapshot_sibling_shapes.hcl): every workspace package of another module the snapshot's typed load read, with the export shape a direct import presented (compared with the sibling's current package_coverage.export_shape_hash) and the digest of its sources (recomputed from disk for a sibling indexed under another go.work), to reuse the head without type-checking symbols is global and is never cascaded. A symbol with no posting and no symbol delta is unreachable; a future garbage collector deletes such rows with NOT EXISTS over the posting and delta indexes, which both lead with the handle. No other retention is proposed, matching the existing policy that snapshots and source revisions are retained. Handles. symbols.handle is a non-negative bigint laid out most significant bit first as 0 | module 11 | package 16 | visibility 1 | kind 6 | local 29 (H64b, storage/symbolhandle). The module and package numbers come from symbol_modules, which reserves 0 for builtins ('') and 1 for std because neither has a modules row, and symbol_packages, which numbers each module's package paths from 0. The kind code comes from symbol_kinds: 0 is reserved, the 18 builtin kinds hold 1–18, and a database's custom kinds (oipa.rule) are allocated from 63 downward; symbols.kind references the registry by name. symbol_layout records the layout, and a database without it (H64a, kind 3 | local 32) has its index discarded on open. The local is one past the largest stored handle of its (module, package, visibility, kind) bucket. Handles therefore sort by module, package, visibility, and kind, so "every symbol of a package", "every exported symbol of a package", and "every exported func of a package" are each one inclusive B-tree range. A handle depends on the order symbols were first published, so it is local to one database: it never enters a document, a hash, a canonical key, or a query result. Visibility is part of the handle, so a symbol whose derived visibility changes cannot be re-published under its old handle and fails loudly; a reindex into a fresh database is then required. Ordinals. modules.ordinal, snapshots.ordinal, and documents.ordinal are dense database-local numbers from 1, allocated as one past the current maximum inside the publication transaction; a PostgreSQL publisher that loses an allocation race retries the whole publication, at most three times. Postings and symbol deltas carry the root's ordinal as a plain column rather than through a composite key with the document or snapshot, so the publisher takes it from the row it just wrote. Coverage has one vocabulary at every level. indexed: type-checked without diagnostics. partial: type-checked with diagnostics; only proven facts are recorded. syntax: the package did not type-check, so the document holds the AST extractor's declarations and unresolved calls, and has no postings. excluded: not extracted (build constraints, testdata, generated exclusions); the document is empty and says why. A snapshot's coverage is the weakest of indexed, partial and syntax among its packages; excluded packages do not count unless every package is excluded, and a module with no packages is indexed.
380.title: Symbol and document tables

381.title: The document

382.text: Document membership is stored as deltas, beside source and symbol deltas. document_deltas records how a snapshot's path → document binding differs from its base's: set binds a path to an immutable document by ordinal, delete drops a path the base served; a snapshot without a base holds a set for every path. storage.ActiveDocuments resolves it: Effective sources for the snapshot give (path_key, source_revision) per path, from the source deltas.storage.EffectiveDocumentOrdinals walks the same base chain and takes the newest document delta per path, tombstones dropping their path.The bound documents are loaded by ordinal in batches. Every effective path must be bound, every bound document must belong to the snapshot's root and the path and describe the path's effective revision, and the snapshot's package_coverage rows must account for exactly its packages and their file counts; any gap is an error. content is loaded only when ActiveDocumentOptions{Content: true} asks for it; without it a reader gets each document's id, ordinal, digest, coverage, and revision, finds the paths it needs, and loads just those with storage.DocumentContents. The foreign keys make a mis-binding unrepresentable: a delta's root must be its snapshot's ((root_id, snapshot_ordinal)), and its document must be of that root and path ((root_id, path_key, document_ordinal)). Publication. The publisher renders every file of a package whose input hash differs from the base's, digests each rendered document, and binds the path to the document stored under (root, path, digest): the base's bound document when its digest matches, otherwise a paired-key lookup ((path_key, content_digest) IN (…) within the root, at most 256 pairs per batch). Only a digest no document holds is inserted, with its postings. It then writes a set delta for each path whose bound document differs from the base's and a delete for each path the base served and the snapshot does not. A package whose input hash equals the base's keeps the base's bindings without rendering (basePackages reads its input hash from the base's package_coverage). Package coverage stays the package-analysis record (input hash, export shape, coverage, diagnostics); it no longer selects documents. Under --force every document is rendered and verified instead: a stored document under the same digest must equal the rendering (sameJSON), and a file whose package has the base's input hash must render the base's digest, or the publication fails with "changed without an indexer version change". Per-file failures. A failure confined to one file never fails the module. A file whose document cannot be rendered, or whose rendered document fails a check its writes repeat (storage validation, or two symbols sharing the key its declaration_metrics rows are keyed by), is published, before anything is written, with its syntax extraction instead, else an empty document. Its package's coverage drops to partial, and its package_coverage.diagnostics gain {path, rule: "uir/index", message}; the snapshot's diagnostics summarize the same list, which ModuleResult.Warnings and uir lint report in lint's shape. A file that does not parse drops its whole package to syntax coverage, since its declarations are missing from type checking: the package's other files keep their syntax documents, the parse errors are uir/coverage diagnostics, and the file itself is published as an empty document with a uir/index warning. A package whose own load is clean but whose exported API names a type an erroring import left invalid gets the unproven export shape (its files' bytes) rather than failing. Database, transaction and input-change failures, and invariants across documents, still fail the module. So a snapshot that changed only a dependency's API keeps every document of an importer whose rendering did not change, and an edit to one file of a package inserts one document and writes one delta. Browse, nodes queries, and typed queries all read the same documents.
382.title: Membership: which documents a snapshot activates

383.text:
A database published before document deltas selected documents by package input hash. Opening it read-write (storage.UirDB) drops the (root_id, path_key, input_hash) key (on SQLite before migration, which refuses to drop an index; PostgreSQL's migration drops it), migrates, and completes the cutover in bounded, resumable transactions recorded in document_membership: every document gets its digest in batches of 64 in ordinal order, then every snapshot in ordinal order gets the deltas of the membership its package input hashes selected, a full set for a snapshot without a base and only the differences from its base's otherwise. Before the cutover, an unchanged file of a re-keyed package got a new, byte-identical document; the earliest such document of a path keeps the digest and the rest keep a null content_digest, still bound by ordinal by every snapshot that bound them, so document ids, ordinals, payloads, and postings are preserved and every snapshot's ActiveDocuments is unchanged. A new publication binds the earliest one by digest. storage.OpenReadOnly refuses a database whose cutover is missing or incomplete (storage.ErrDocumentMembershipCutover). Step 1 used to issue one query per base link. storage.EffectiveSources now issues one recursive CTE that walks the base chain and returns the first delta per path, tombstones included so Go can validate them, with a named recursion cap that turns a base cycle into an error. Both engines support WITH RECURSIVE and window functions; the core of the query is: WITH RECURSIVE chain(id, base_id, depth) AS (
  SELECT id, base_snapshot_id, 0 FROM snapshots WHERE id = ?
  UNION ALL
  SELECT s.id, s.base_snapshot_id, c.depth + 1
  FROM snapshots s JOIN chain c ON s.id = c.base_id
),
ranked AS (
  SELECT d.path_key, d.revision_id, d.operation,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY d.path_key ORDER BY c.depth) AS rank
  FROM source_deltas d JOIN chain c ON c.id = d.snapshot_id
)
SELECT path_key, revision_id FROM ranked WHERE rank = 1 AND operation = 'set'; Chain length is bounded only by history depth; the CTE makes that one query rather than one per link. If measured chain walks become the dominant cost, a source checkpoint table is the follow-up. It is not part of this design.
383.title: Document membership cutover
titles: Membership: which documents a snapshot activates

384.text: Unlike documents, symbol membership is stored as deltas. A snapshot's defined-symbol set is every declaration with a canonical id in its active documents; syntax declarations and the unproven declarations of a partial document have no id and no handle and are never in it. symbol_deltas records how that set differs from the base's: set with the symbol's fingerprints when it is new or its fingerprints changed, delete when the base defined it and the snapshot does not. A set carries one fingerprint per layer, public_fp, private_fp, and content_fp: each the first eight bytes of the declaration's public_hash, private_hash, or content_hash read as a signed int64 (storage.SymbolFingerprint, DocumentSymbol.Fingerprints).
384.title: Symbol membership: which symbols a snapshot defines
titles: Membership: which documents a snapshot activates

385.text: symbol_deltas once stored two fingerprints, shape_fp and body_fp, and documents (format 4) carried shape_hash and body_hash. Neither can be converted into the three layers without re-extracting, so storage.UirDB treats such a database as another stale generation, exactly as it does a pre-handle or H64a one (storage/handle_cutover.go): the catalog query that classifies the database also reports whether symbol_deltas has a shape_fp column, and when the recorded layout is current but the column is there, the database is the two-layer fingerprint generation. Before migration, in one transaction, the cutover drops the same index tables (symbol_deltas, symbol_postings, snapshot_dependencies, package_coverage, documents, symbols, symbol_packages, symbol_modules, source_deltas, source_revisions, location_heads, snapshots, source_blobs); modules with their ordinals, locations, primary_locations, task_runs, and symbol_kinds keep their rows. Migration then creates symbol_deltas as 13_layered_fingerprints.hcl declares it, and UirDB logs a warning to run uir reindex. OpenReadOnly refuses such a database with "database predates layered symbol fingerprints; open it read-write once or run uir reindex". The publisher writes the deltas in the publication transaction from changed packages only: a package is changed when one of its paths is bound to a different document than in the base, or added or removed. It compares a changed package whole, the base's stored documents of all its paths and the extraction's of all its files, because one id may be declared in several files of a package and its fingerprints fold across all of them; documents of every other package are never read. Declarations are grouped by id across the changed packages; a symbol on both sides with equal fingerprints, such as one that moved between two files, gets no row. A snapshot without a base records every defined symbol as set, and a dependency bump that rebinds no document records nothing. This is sound because a canonical id includes its package, whose files share one directory; the publisher fails if an id it reads is declared in two package directories. Go never declares one id twice, since each func init carries its own discriminator (canonical symbols), but a producer may declare one id in several files, so storage.FoldDeclarations combines several declarations of one id order-independently into one triple of fingerprints, folding each layer apart. storage.EffectiveSymbols reads the set with the same base-chain walk as EffectiveSources, carrying each link's snapshot ordinal and joining symbol_deltas on it: the newest row per handle wins and tombstones drop out. storage.DefinedSymbols answers the question queries actually ask, "which of these handles does the snapshot define", with the same CTE restricted before ranking to an IN list of at most 256 handles, which every chain link probes on the (snapshot_ordinal, symbol_handle) primary key; its cost follows the handles asked about, not the size of the snapshot. Because a snapshot defines a symbol exactly when one of its active documents has a definition posting for it, both answer membership without reading documents or postings.
385.title: Layered fingerprint cutover
titles: Membership: which documents a snapshot activates
Symbol membership: which symbols a snapshot defines

386.text: Which interfaces a type satisfies depends on every candidate interface, not on the type's file and its imports' APIs, so it is a snapshot-level fact rather than a document field (17_implements.hcl). After a Go root's documents are extracted, indexer.snapshotImplements relates every non-interface, non-generic defined type the root's indexed or partial packages declare (proven declarations only) to each candidate interface it satisfies by value or by pointer, reused packages included. Candidates are the non-empty, non-generic, method-set package-level interfaces of the packages the root's variants reach through imports, without passing through another module's workspace package, admitted by what keys them: the root's own packages, any interface (their sources are the content set); standard-library and module-cache packages, exported interfaces (the toolchain and module versions key them); and another module's workspace package whose export shape a package input hash folds in, exported interfaces with only exported methods (that shape is all the context covers of it). The facts are therefore a function of what context_hash and the content set cover, and a type is related to an interface declared in a package it does not import. A method-name index tests a candidate only when the type's method set has every one of its method names. TableColumnsKeysReferences and checksimplements_deltassnapshot_ordinal bigint, root_ordinal integer, type_handle bigint, interface_handle bigint, operation textPK (snapshot_ordinal,type_handle,interface_handle); index (interface_handle,snapshot_ordinal); index (type_handle,snapshot_ordinal)snapshot_ordinal → snapshots.ordinal CASCADE; root_ordinal → modules.ordinal CASCADE; type_handle, interface_handle → symbols.handle NO ACTION; operation IN ('set','delete')implements_factssnapshot_ordinal bigint, root_ordinal integer, pair_count bigintPK snapshot_ordinalsnapshot_ordinal → snapshots.ordinal CASCADE; root_ordinal → modules.ordinal CASCADE; pair_count >= 0 Publication compares the extraction's facts with the base's effective facts and writes a set for each new pair and a delete for each pair only the base holds, then the implements_facts row with the snapshot's pair count. A base published before snapshot-level facts has no row and contributes none. storage.EffectiveImplements resolves the facts along the base chain like EffectiveSymbols, the newest row per pair winning, restricted before ranking to IN lists of at most 256 type or interface handles; an unrestricted read checks the resolved count against pair_count. A snapshot without an implements_facts row is storage.ErrNoImplementsFacts, and the query layer asks for a reindex instead of reading old documents' implements entries. Pruning rebases a survivor's facts into set rows with its sources and symbols, and counts both handle columns as references when it looks for orphan symbols.
386.title: Implements facts
titles: Membership: which documents a snapshot activates

387.text:
A diff takes two git commits A..B and a root, and is computed from the two snapshots' active documents plus, for exact line counts, the two commits' blobs. No diff table is stored: both inputs are immutable, so a result is reproducible and may be cached by the caller. Commit to snapshot. For each commit, select from the (root_id, revision) index the snapshots of the root whose revision equals the commit and whose worktree_state is clean; take the newest. Without --auto-index, missing or dirty-only snapshots fail explicitly; --snapshot-from and --snapshot-to override the selection. With --auto-index, the diff selects or creates clean snapshots from temporary Git worktrees under the current standalone module configuration, preserving registered checkout files and heads. Both snapshots must share configuration_hash, otherwise the layer hashes are not comparable and the diff fails saying so. See snapshot selection. Changed files. Derive both active document maps without content: the membership needs only each path's document id, ordinal, and coverage. Paths with equal document ids on both sides are unchanged and are skipped without reading them. Paths present on one side only are added or removed files. Symbol diff (a). Symbols are classified by identity across the whole diff, so a symbol that moved between files is still one symbol. For changed indexed documents the classification needs no document: read both snapshots' effective symbols, then the definition postings of each side's changed documents, which say which changed documents define each handle on each side and how many declarations they hold. The two must agree (a handle that a changed document defines is effective on exactly the sides whose changed documents define it, and a handle whose effective fingerprints differ between the sides must be declared by some changed document), otherwise the diff fails naming the handle. Each symbol declared once per side is classified: ClassConditionaddeddefined only in Bremoveddefined only in Asignaturedefined on both sides, public fingerprint differsstructuredefined on both sides, public fingerprint equal, private fingerprint differsbodydefined on both sides, public and private fingerprints equal, content fingerprint differsmoveddefined on both sides, fingerprints equal, defining path_key differsformatfingerprints and path equal, but declaration bytes differ; commit comparisons require --statimporta file present on both sides changes an import alias's path, or adds or removes an import; internal visibilityunchangeddefined on both sides, fingerprints, path, and bytes equal; omitted A package with a syntax or partial changed document on either side (a keyed package), and a symbol declared more than once on a side, are instead matched over their decoded documents, first by id and then by key, and classified from the full hashes. Everywhere else a fingerprint stands for its hash, so two different shapes or bodies whose hashes share their first eight bytes would read as unchanged. Which documents are read. Only those the output needs: with --stat, every changed document, for line counts; otherwise the documents of keyed packages, excluded documents, both sides of a symbol declared more than once, and, for a row the visibility filter shows, the new side of an added symbol, the old side of a removed one, and both sides of a signature or structure change, whose shapes the row prints. With internal or all visibility, both documents of every changed file present on both sides are read for import comparisons. A shown body or moved row prints no shape, so it can be named from its symbols row and its owners' names (storage.OwnedSymbols, storage.DeclarationIdentifier). A rename appears as removed plus added, because identity includes the name. A parameter-type change likewise appears as removed plus added of the old and new identities, grouped under the old symbol's owner and name when the pair is unique. The diff guide describes cross-package move pairing. The --visibility filter is exported by default and keeps a symbol when its visibility on either side matches; internal and all are the other values, and only they show structure and import rows. Exported output can include body, move, and formatting rows as well as signature changes; --change-type restricts the classes. Each row carries kind, owner, name, both shape strings when they differ (the public shapes for signature rows, the private ones otherwise), a shape diff for signature and structure rows, and both file paths. Shape diff rendering. A signature or structure row shows what changed in the shape, not only that it changed. Each class diffs the shapes of the layer it names: a signature row the public shapes (public_shape, where a struct shows its exported fields and opaque), a structure row the private (full) shapes (shape). The two canonical renderings are line-diffed with Myers, treating lines that differ only in whitespace (gofmt realignment) as equal. Within a changed hunk, the i-th removed line and the i-th added line form a replaced pair when their token diff shares at least one non-blank token; short equal runs between edits are folded into the edit, so a changed tail reads as one replacement. Tokens are split by the root's tokenizer (symboldiff.Tokenizer): a Go root's lines by go/scanner (go), an external root's language-neutrally (text: identifiers, which may start with @, #, or $, numbers, quoted strings and identifiers, and runs of other non-space characters). The plain form prints unchanged lines with two spaces, removed lines with - , and added lines with + ; the rich forms print a replaced pair as one ~  line through clicky api.Text, removed tokens red and struck through, added tokens green and bold, which is ANSI in a terminal, ~~removed~~ and **added** in markdown, and clicky's <s> and <strong> in HTML. JSON carries the structured form: shape_diff is a list of lines {op, text, paired, tokenizer, tokens: [{op, text}]}, where op is equal, delete, or insert, a paired line names the tokenizer (go or text) its tokens were split by, and a paired delete line's tokens are its equal and deleted runs while the paired insert line's are its equal and inserted runs. The same renderer serves the removed-plus-added grouping of a parameter-type change, diffing the old identity's shape against the new one so a type change reads as one signature edit. The package-level export_shape_hash pre-check is not applied, because skipping a package would hide its exported body rows and line counts (diff.md). A syntax document on either side has no ids, so its symbols are matched by key and can only be classified added, removed, body, or moved; the row is marked syntax. Line attribution (b). For each changed file, read both commits' bytes from Git (git cat-file on the blob at that commit in a registered checkout of the root) and verify each against the source revision's content_hash; a mismatch or a missing checkout fails the diff for that file with the reason, and the symbol diff for that file is still reported. Each side's document gives symbol extents in bytes. The file is partitioned into segments: one per outermost symbol extent, plus the gaps between them, which form a single (file scope) segment covering package clause, imports, comments, and anything not inside a declaration. Segments are paired by symbol id (or by key for syntax documents), and the gap segments are paired with each other. Each pair is line-diffed independently (Myers over lines), which yields +added -removed per symbol exactly, because a change inside one declaration cannot be attributed to another. A symbol present on one side only contributes all of its extent lines as added or removed. A moved symbol is diffed across files and reported under the destination file with the source path noted. Per-file totals are the sums of their segment pairs, and per-package totals the sums of their files, so store.go +14 -5 equals the sum of its symbol rows plus its file-scope row. example.org/service/invoices                          +14 -5
  invoices/store.go                                   +14 -5
    Store.Save          signature   +10 -3
      - func (s *Store) Save(ctx context.Context, inv Invoice) error
      + func (s *Store) Save(ctx context.Context, inv Invoice, opts ...SaveOption) (Receipt, error)
    Store.load          body        +4  -2
    (file scope)                    +0  -0
  invoices/model.go                                   +6  -6
    Invoice             signature   +1  -1
        type Invoice struct {
          ID       InvoiceID
      -   Total    int
      +   Total    Money
      +   Notes    string
        }
    Invoice.Total       added       +6  -0   func (i Invoice) Total() Money
    Invoice.total       removed     +0  -6   func (i Invoice) total() Money In a terminal the Store.Save pair renders as one line with token marks rather than two full lines: the removed ) error tail is red and struck through, and , opts ...SaveOption) (Receipt, error) is green and bold, so the reader sees the added variadic parameter and the new result tuple without comparing the lines by eye. In markdown the same pair is func (s *Store) Save(ctx context.Context, inv Invoice~~) error~~**, opts ...SaveOption) (Receipt, error)**. The plain-text form above is what --format text and non-TTY output print. With --visibility exported the Store.load and Invoice.total rows are hidden; the file totals then state that hidden rows exist rather than silently summing to less than the file's diff. Coverage. A partial file on either side still diffs the symbols it proved; the row is marked partial so a missing symbol is not read as removed. An excluded file is listed as excluded with its line diff attributed entirely to file scope. Cost. Two content-free membership derivations, two effective-symbol walks, the definition postings of the changed documents, and batched content loads of the documents chosen above. A sibling file of a re-keyed package keeps its document when its rendering did not change, so changed files are exactly the files whose documents differ. Git reads are bounded by changed files.
387.title: Diffing two commits

388.text: All indexes are listed with their tables above. Named secondary indexes, in HCL naming: locations_parent_idx, snapshots_location_started_idx, snapshots_base_idx, snapshots_root_revision_idx, source_deltas_revision_id_idx, symbols_lookup_idx, symbols_search_idx, documents_source_idx, symbol_postings_symbol_idx over (symbol_handle, role, root_ordinal, document_ordinal), symbol_deltas_handle_idx over (symbol_handle, snapshot_ordinal), document_deltas_document_idx over (document_ordinal) (the reverse lookup a document delete's foreign key check needs), package_coverage_input_idx. Unique indexes are named <table>_<columns>_key; among them symbols_handle_key is the B-tree that handle ranges scan (selector candidates, and the largest handle of a bucket when a local is allocated), and modules_ordinal_key, snapshots_ordinal_key, and documents_ordinal_key are the targets of the posting and delta foreign keys. symbols.owner_id still has no index of its own: a lookup by owner alone scans symbols, and owner chains are loaded by id in batches instead. search_name is the symbol's name lowercased and restricted to [a-z0-9], with every other character (including _) removed; a name with none of those characters, such as _, stores an empty search_name and is found only by exact name. storage.SearchName is the one implementation, shared by the indexer and the query layer. A prefix search is then search_name >= ? AND search_name < ?, which uses the B-tree on both engines. The upper bound increments the prefix within the ordered alphabet 0-9 then a-z with carry (9 becomes a; a trailing z is dropped and the character before it increments), and a prefix of only z has no upper bound. The bound never leaves the alphabet, because a punctuation byte sorts below digits and letters under glibc and ICU collations and would make the range empty. The query layer still keeps only the rows whose search_name starts with the prefix, so a collation that orders the range differently can only over-fetch. Because search_name and visibility are derived, publication upserts a symbol on conflict of id and refreshes both columns from the incoming row, so a reindex after a normalization change rewrites existing rows; canonical_key and the other identity facts are still verified against the stored row. Column collations and operator classes are outside the portable subset, so a general LIKE 'prefix%' must not be relied on. Qualified input such as Store.Save is split by the query layer: resolve owners by search_name = 'store', then filter children by owner_id. Substring and fuzzy search need a separate design.
388.title: Index inventory

389.text: References to B at every head. Resolve B through symbols_lookup_idx; a selector matching several symbols returns candidates first. Map B's id to its handle once per query. For each selected location head, derive its active document ordinals. Then read symbol_postings_symbol_idx for (handle(B), 1, root_ordinal) and intersect with the active set; the query layer reads the root's posting range when it holds no more rows than the active set (bounded at one row past it), and otherwise probes the posting key with the active ordinals in batched IN lists. Load the matching documents, filter occurrences with symbol = B, and return one row per occurrence with path, range, role, and enclosing symbol, mapping handles back to ids. Declaration locations come from the same intersection with role 0 (definition); before reading those postings, DefinedSymbols tells which snapshots define B at all, and a root none of whose scopes does is skipped. A same-location declaration is preferred for display and other heads remain visible as candidates. Reference rows are never multiplied by the number of declaration locations. References in a historical snapshot. Identical, with the active set derived for that snapshot. A syntax or excluded package in scope is reported as such so an empty result is not mistaken for proven absence. Callers of B, interface-aware. Each scope's implements facts for interface I give the concrete types that satisfy I. Callers of a concrete method T.M are the references to T.M plus the references to I.M for every I that T implements, when the caller asks for dispatch-inclusive results. Dispatch through an interface the facts do not consider is not proven. Callees of A. Load A's defining document (the definition posting of handle(A) intersected with the active set) and return occurrences whose enclosing is A and whose role is call. Nodes and browse. The existing nodes where … predicates and the explorer read symbols entries from active documents, typed or syntax, so the current AST-only behaviour is preserved for packages that do not type-check. Typed selectors. A pkg: selector, or a symbol selector qualified by a package path, reads its candidates through the handle ranges of the registered packages it can match; any other selector reads each admitted root module's whole range. The ranges are merged and ORed into handle BETWEEN conditions over symbols_handle_key, and the candidates are then kept only where a selected snapshot of their own root defines them (DefinedSymbols). Name search and resolution. Range-scan symbols_search_idx (spelling resolution and suggestions both take this path), keep symbols that a selected snapshot defines (DefinedSymbols, from symbol deltas) or that an active document references (postings) or a scope's type implements (implements facts), both read only for the symbols no snapshot defines, and rank by kind and module. Diff. uir diff <from>..<to> --root example.org/service lists exported symbol changes; --visibility all includes internal symbols; --stat adds per-file and per-symbol line counts and requires readable Git blobs. EditSymbolsDocuments, postings, and symbol deltasDiff classificationInsert a comment above a use of BUnchangedPackage input hash changes and the package is re-rendered; the edited file gets a new document (its ranges moved) and one document delta, its siblings keep theirs; no symbol delta, because content_hash ignores commentsformat (with --stat for commit comparisons) if inside a symbol's extent, otherwise file scope +1 -0Add a second call from A to BUnchangedA new document for A's file; posting (doc, B, reference) count becomes 2; set for A with a new content fingerprintbody on AChange A's parameter nameUnchangedA new document for A's file; set for A with new public and private fingerprints and the same content fingerprint; the export shape is unchanged, so no dependent is re-extractedsignature on A (names are in the shape, not the identity)Change A's parameter typeNew symbol for A; old retainedA new document for A's file and, if A is exported, for every dependent file that names A; delete for old A, set for new Aremoved old A, added new A, groupedMove B to another file in the same packageUnchangedNew documents for both files; B's definition posting moves; no symbol delta, because B's fingerprints are equalmovedChange an exported return or field typeIdentity may remainExport shape changes; every directly importing package is re-rendered, and only its files whose documents change get new ones; set for the changed symbolsignaturego get bumping a dependencyUnchangedNew snapshot with zero source deltas; importing packages are re-rendered, and keep their documents unless their rendering changes; their symbols get deltas only if their fingerprints changeNo rows when import paths and declaration facts stay equal; manifest changes have file-scope lines with --stat Cost note on package granularity. A package's input hash covers all of its files, so editing one file still re-renders every file of the package, but publication stores only the documents whose rendering changed: one document and one document delta for a one-file edit whose siblings render as before. Rendering, not storage, is now what package granularity costs; moving the input comparison ahead of packages.Load is Phase 3 of the incremental snapshot plan.
389.title: Query and update examples

390.text: Let F be files per module, P packages, S snapshots, c files re-extracted per snapshot, k distinct symbols mentioned per file, and L active location heads. Documents: one row per (path, content_digest). History grows by c documents per snapshot, each a few kilobytes; this replaces the projection column rather than adding to it.Document deltas: one row per path whose bound document changed per snapshot, plus every path for a snapshot without a base.Postings: k rows per document, typically 3 to 5 times fewer than occurrences in real files, each five integers (document ordinal, root ordinal, handle, role, count) plus two index entries.Package coverage: P rows per snapshot, O(S × P).Symbols: one row per distinct identity ever observed, retained, each with its handle.Symbol registry: one symbol_modules row per module key and one symbol_packages row per package path ever observed.Symbol deltas: one row per symbol added, changed, or removed per snapshot, plus every defined symbol for a snapshot without a base.Membership: two recursive CTEs (source and document deltas) plus P package rows plus F / 256 batched ordinal lookups per snapshot derivation. Symbol membership is one recursive CTE over the deltas.Reference lookup: one derivation, one posting range scan bounded by (handle, role, root ordinal), then document reads equal to the number of matching files. No O(L × R) posting tables exist.Diff: two content-free derivations, two symbol-delta walks, definition postings of changed documents, document reads only where the output needs shapes, keys, or line counts, Git reads for changed files, and in-memory line diffs per symbol pair. Using the earlier illustration (100 modules, 500 files, 10,000 occurrences per module, 1,000 snapshots, one 20-occurrence file changing per snapshot, 5-file packages): about 550,000 documents, roughly 8 million posting rows at 15 distinct symbols per document, 5 million package coverage rows, and no occurrence, checkpoint, head, or diff rows. The occurrence-row design stored about 3 million occurrence rows plus 1 million head postings plus 800,000 checkpoint pointers under an assumption that ignored package re-typing. With realistic files of 200 to 500 occurrences and 60 to 100 distinct symbols the posting design stores four to five times fewer rows; with the toy 20-occurrence file it does not, and its saving is row width and the absence of position rows. These are algorithmic expectations, not measured latency guarantees; step 8 below measures them. Measured (step 8, benchmarks, SQLite and PostgreSQL 16 on this repository and flanksource/commons): Documents average 145 KB, which is 1.4 KB per declared symbol and 235 B per occurrence. That is far above the "few kilobytes" assumed above, and documents are 66 to 72 % of the database.A single-file body edit re-stores the whole package: 8 to 10 documents, 790 to 880 postings, and 1.4 to 1.7 MB on SQLite. After 200 such commits the commons database grew from 17.5 MB to 350 MB, with 1,708 documents and 182,568 postings.Postings cost about 490 B each in SQLite once both indexes are included. Under compact handles they cost 73 B on SQLite and 165 B on PostgreSQL (cold five-checkout corpus, compact symbol handles).The recursive CTE over a 200-link chain takes 1 ms. Posting lookups are covering range scans of symbol_postings_symbol_idx on both engines.Per head, the membership derivation's real cost is reading every active document's content (about 15 MB). That motivates a content-free membership lookup, not the phase-2 head table. ActiveDocuments now omits content unless asked; the diff uses that, while the query layer still loads content for every active document.Unchanged runs now skip type-checking: 3.3 to 4.5 s before, 0.14 to 0.67 s after. Other runs are dominated by the 4 to 15 s go/packages load. Discovery still reads and hashes all included files on each run. Extraction runs through go/packages on changed packages and their dependents and completes before the publication transaction opens: the transaction allocates handles for new symbols and ordinals for new documents and the snapshot, writes symbols, documents, postings, package rows, the snapshot row, and its symbol deltas, then advances the head with the existing version check. SQLite's single connection is never held across type-checking.
390.title: Expected size and cost

391.text: If measured head queries across many locations are too slow because each head derivation repeats the CTE and key lookups, add head_documents (location_id, root_id, path_key, document_id) with PK (location_id, path_key), replaced for changed paths in the publication transaction. It holds O(L × F) small rows, not O(L × R), and reference queries join it directly with postings. The criterion for adding it is a benchmark on a real workspace showing derivation above a fixed budget per head; it is not part of the initial schema.
391.title: Phase-2 option: head materialization

392.text: Cutover. Rewrite 04_module_roots.hcl and 05_source_deltas.hcl to the base schema above and add 06_symbol_index.hcl for the four proposed tables; add it to the //go:embed list in storage/database.go. Extend storage/legacy_cutover.go to drop the uir_* tables before migration, child tables first, one transaction, refusing if an unmanaged table references them. Update the GORM models and TableName() methods, drop SnapshotState, storage/README.md, docs/module-indexing.md, docs/symbols.md, docs/query.md, and the ERD. This discards the local index; uir reindex rebuilds it. Test that an old database opens, loses the prefixed tables, and reindexes cleanly on both engines, and add schema assertions for SQLite and PostgreSQL.Extend ContentSetHash and ConfigurationHash in indexer/discovery.go and indexer/modules.go, record worktree_state, and compare context_hash in the unchanged check, with tests showing that a go.sum change and a variant change each produce a new snapshot with zero source deltas.Replace the per-link loop in storage.EffectiveSources with the recursive CTE and a lean row type. Test a 1,000-link chain and a branch that bases on another location's head.Move the AST extractor's output into syntax documents and port query/modules.go, storage/module_browse.go, and the explorer to read documents. Existing query and browse tests must pass unchanged in behaviour.Add identity canonicalization, visibility, shape and body hashing, export-shape and input hashing, and typed document extraction over go/packages with go/types.Info, falling back to a syntax document per package that fails to type-check. Test parameter-name stability of identity, parameter-type changes, shape changes on return and field types, body-only changes, duplicate use sites, file moves, interface implements, builtins excluded from postings, syntax fallback, and the context_hash unchanged decision with and without a changed sibling module.Add publication: symbols and documents with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING, postings, package rows, and the snapshot row inside the existing head compare-and-swap transaction. Test rollback after a failed compare-and-swap and idempotent republication.Add the diff: commit-to-snapshot selection with the clean-worktree rule and overrides, symbol classification with the visibility filter, line attribution by symbol extent over hash-verified Git blobs, and the shape diff (line diff of canonical shapes, token diff of replaced lines, rendered through clicky api.Text with Strikethrough() for removed tokens). Test each classification row in the edit table above, a moved symbol across files, a partial file, a syntax file, an excluded file, a dirty-only snapshot rejection, a hash mismatch failing one file while the rest of the diff completes, and the shape diff in ANSI, markdown, HTML, and JSON for a one-line signature, a struct field change, and a parameter-type change grouped as removed plus added.Extend the PEG query (references, definitions, callers, callees, implements, search) and the CLI and API (diff), then wire the explorer tree, Monaco ranges, a symbol search box, and a diff view. Test exact positions, several heads defining the same symbol, incomplete coverage reporting, and pagination. Verify the visible actions in the local browser.Benchmark initial, unchanged, body-only, exported-shape, dependency-bump, deep-history, multi-head, and diff runs on a real workspace; inspect both engines' plans for the posting semi-join and the CTE. Decide the phase-2 head table from those numbers. Run make build, make lint, and go test ./....Compact handles (landed 2026-09-27, evaluation). Add ordinal to modules, snapshots, and documents and handle to symbols in 04 and 06 in place, rekey symbol_postings by ordinals and handles, and add 07_symbol_handles.hcl for symbol_modules, symbol_packages, and symbol_deltas. Allocate handles and ordinals in the publication transaction, retrying PostgreSQL allocation conflicts up to three times, and write symbol deltas from changed paths only. Answer existence checks with DefinedSymbols, read selector candidates through handle ranges, and classify the diff from delta fingerprints, decoding only the documents the output needs. A database of the previous generation is recognised on open by modules lacking ordinal: before migration, in one transaction, its index tables (symbol_postings, package_coverage, documents, symbols, source_deltas, source_revisions, location_heads, snapshots) are dropped, and modules, locations, and primary_locations keep their rows, with modules numbered densely by created_at then root_key. uir reindex rebuilds each checkout; until then uir list and uir get show the root with no snapshot, and a query that selects it fails saying it is registered but not indexed. OpenReadOnly refuses such a database. Tests cover the cutover on both engines, handle allocation and its concurrency, delta publication, the effective and defined sets, and the fingerprint diff; the query fixtures and the history fixture pass unchanged.
392.title: Implementation and verification sequence

393.text: UIR SQL selects symbols, source files, and recorded relationship witnesses from immutable snapshots. It reads the same facts as compact queries, independently of whether UIR stores them in SQLite or PostgreSQL. This page describes the implemented language; the SQL examples show every source function and common investigations. uir query 'SELECT symbol.name, path, line FROM callers(method:Store.Save) WHERE symbol IN func:* ORDER BY symbol.name LIMIT 20' Ordinary SQL strings use single quotes. When passing an expression containing those strings to a shell, enclose the whole expression in double quotes: uir query "SELECT symbol.name, depth FROM traverse(func:Entry, depth => 3) WHERE symbol.name IMATCH '*handle*'" The first example above uses no string literals; double quotes inside selectors delimit names containing spaces or punctuation, such as http.route:"Create order". A leading unquoted SELECT selects SQL automatically. Use --language sql to force SQL, including when the query begins with a comment. Parsing and binding errors retain their diagnostics; they do not fall back to compact parsing.
393.title: SQL language reference

394.text:
Queries read saved snapshots and do not index or modify source. Index a Go module with uir add /path/to/module, or import the domain example, before querying it. uir query 'SELECT symbol.name FROM func:*' --root example.org/service
uir query 'SELECT path FROM files()' --location /path/to/service-worktree
uir query 'SELECT symbol.name FROM func:*' --snapshot SNAPSHOT_UUID
uir query 'SELECT symbol.name FROM func:*' --all --format json --root selects a registered module path, --location a checkout, and --snapshot one immutable published snapshot. Location and snapshot cannot be combined. Inside a registered Go checkout, the CLI defaults to that checkout; outside one it searches available primary heads. --all searches every registered root and cannot combine with root, location, or snapshot. HTTP requests never infer scope from the server's working directory. Query scope describes missing heads and incomplete coverage. Execution resolves the source and finishes navigation before applying WHERE, ordering, projection, and the row limit. A filter therefore does not prune intermediate traversal nodes. Witness rows are not a distinct-symbol list: two uses of the same symbol can return two rows.
394.title: Scope and execution

395.text:
The following notation uses brackets for optional parts and braces for repetition; they are not query characters. query       = SELECT projection FROM source [AS alias]
              [WHERE predicate] [ORDER BY ordering {, ordering}]
              [LIMIT integer] [;]
projection  = * | field [AS name] {, field [AS name]}
source      = selector | function([arguments])
arguments   = source {, source} [, options] | options
options     = option {, option}
option      = name => literal
ordering    = field_or_projection_alias [ASC | DESC]
predicate   = conjunction {OR conjunction}
conjunction = condition {AND condition}
condition   = NOT condition | (predicate) | comparison
comparison  = field (= | != | < | <= | > | >=) literal
            | symbol [NOT] IN selector
            | field IS [NOT] NULL
            | field [NOT] (MATCH | IMATCH) 'glob'
            | file.build_constraint [NOT] REQUIRES 'tag'
literal     = 'string' | signed_decimal | TRUE | FALSE | NULL Exactly one statement is accepted. Clauses must appear in the order shown. * is the entire projection; it cannot be mixed with explicit columns. Projections accept fields, not expressions or literals. AS is required for column and source aliases. Column aliases name output keys and can be used in ORDER BY, but not WHERE. Duplicate output names are errors. SELECT symbol.name AS name, path, line
FROM callers(method:Store.Save)
WHERE symbol.visibility = 'exported'
ORDER BY name ASC, path ASC, line DESC
LIMIT 20; Keywords, function names, and option names are case insensitive. Field names, aliases, selector prefixes/patterns, relationship names, and literal values retain their spelling. -- line comments and /* ... */ block comments are accepted. Strings escape a single quote by doubling it ('Reader''s guide'); backslashes in SQL strings remain literal and can escape glob characters. Numbers are signed integers or decimals, without exponent notation. Double quotes belong to selector values, not SQL string literals or field identifiers. Rows default to 100. SQL LIMIT overrides the CLI/API limit; either must be an integer from 1 to 1,000. total counts matching rows before the limit. ASC is the default, sorting uses scalar values, and NULL sorts last in ascending order and first in descending order. There is no OFFSET clause.
395.title: Statement grammar

396.text: Every symbol source is a typed selector or a navigation function consuming one. An empty selector result returns no rows. Short selectors can match several canonical identities; qualify the module/package or narrow the scope when that matters. SelectorSelectsExamplefunc:patternThe callable category: functions, methods, constructors, endpoints, and custom callable kinds.func:Store.Savemethod:patternMethod symbols.method:Store.*field:patternField symbols.field:Order.Totalvar:patternPackage variables.var:Currenttype:patternThe type category, including custom type kinds.type:Repositorystruct:patternDefined, non-alias Go types whose underlying form is a struct.struct:Orderpkg:patternSymbols declared in matching package paths.pkg:example.org/service/internal/**pkg:module:relative_packageSymbols in matching modules and module-relative packages; . means the root package.pkg:example.org/service:internal/**mod:patternSymbols declared in matching registered roots.mod:example.org/servicekind:name[:pattern]One exact registered kind, optionally restricted by name.kind:sql.procedure:Load*registered_kind:patternThe entity name within one registered kind.table:orders, column:total, http.route:Ordersapi:patternAlias for the registered endpoint kind.api:CreateOrder Registered prefixes include builtin kinds such as const, table, column, record, and interface, plus producer kinds such as http.route. An unregistered kind fails. pkg: and mod: return declarations within containers, rather than creating container rows. SQL does not accept bare compact spellings such as Store.Save <, compact set operators, or a free-form compact expression inside FROM. Selector values can use double quotes, for example func:"Premium Calc (Annual)" or pkg:"Regional Plan":"Group Life/**". Quoting permits spaces and punctuation; glob characters still describe patterns and must be escaped to match literally. See typed selectors for contextual name matching and identity rules.
396.title: Selectors

397.text: symbol is the canonical symbol projected by the source. path, line, package, and module describe the witness site, which can be in a different package or root from that symbol. For example, references(field:Order.Total) projects the field while its witness is each use; callers(method:Store.Save) projects the enclosing caller while preserving the call site. FieldCatalog typeMeaningsymbolsymbolThe full projected symbol object; supports identity membership with IN.symbol.idstringCanonical identity, independent of the witness path.symbol.kind, symbol.name, symbol.query_namestringRegistered kind, simple name, and qualified query name.symbol.module, symbol.packagestringThe projected symbol's module key and package path.symbol.owner, symbol.visibilitystringOwning declaration's name and exported or internal visibility.symbol.props, symbol.props.<field>object or schema typeProducer properties, including declared nested fields.symbol.typestringResolved package-variable type; see variable types.symbol.metrics.param_count, symbol.metrics.body_linesintegerCallable measures; see metrics.symbol.metrics.<name>integerA producer metric declared by a selected kind.path, package, module, snapshotstringWitness source path, package, root key, and snapshot ID.line, columnnumberOne-based witness line and UTF-16 column when positioned.rolestringRecorded occurrence role or native relationship name.dispatchbooleanWhether a witness was reached through known interface dispatch.depthnumberRecorded traversal hop distance.relationship.kind, relationship.resolutionstringNative kind and static, dynamic, ambiguous, or unresolved resolution.relationship.props, relationship.props.<field>object or schema typeNative relationship properties, when present. Symbol SELECT * includes the symbol, its identity/name/ownership/property fields, witness fields, and relationship fields. It does not automatically include variable types or metrics; request them explicitly. Missing optional facts are NULL; unavailable required type/metric capabilities fail as described below. File sources have a separate field set: path, module, package, snapshot, file.lines, file.definitions, file.functions, file.structs, and file.build_constraint. Their wildcard includes the first eight fields, omitting file.build_constraint. Symbol sources do not expose file metrics, and file sources do not expose symbol fields. A source alias on a symbol source abbreviates properties: FROM http.route:* AS r makes r.method mean symbol.props.method, not symbol.method. Continue to write symbol.name for the symbol name. A file alias supports both site fields (f.path) and file fields (f.lines, f.functions, f.build_constraint). Alias names must match exactly.
397.title: Fields

398.text:
FormExample predicateBehavior=, !=, <, <=, >, >=symbol.metrics.param_count >= 4Compares a scalar field with a type-compatible literal.symbol IN selectorsymbol IN pkg:example.org/service:api/**Retains the projected canonical identities selected on the right.symbol NOT IN selectorsymbol NOT IN method:Store.*Excludes those projected identities.IS NULL, IS NOT NULLrelationship.kind IS NOT NULLTests absence/presence explicitly.MATCH, NOT MATCHpath MATCH 'internal/**'Anchored, case-sensitive glob matching on a string field.IMATCH, NOT IMATCHsymbol.name IMATCH '*save*'Anchored glob matching with Unicode simple case folding.REQUIRES, NOT REQUIRESfile.build_constraint REQUIRES 'hack'Exact Boolean analysis of a modern Go header; file sources only.NOT, AND, OR, parenthesesNOT (role = 'write' OR line IS NULL)Combines predicates, with precedence NOT, then AND, then OR. Comparisons take literal values on the right, not another field. IN accepts a selector, not a literal list, and its left operand must be symbol. Objects, arrays, and the whole symbol object cannot be scalar-compared or ordered; project a typed scalar property instead. An unknown property or one whose selected schemas disagree about its type fails binding. NULL follows three-valued logic: a comparison or match with a missing value is unknown, NOT unknown is unknown, and WHERE retains only true rows. Use IS NULL, rather than = NULL, to find missing values. For example, retain routes with an absent description or a nonempty POST description: SELECT symbol.name, r.description
FROM http.route:* AS r
WHERE r.description IS NULL OR (r.method = 'POST' AND r.description != '') Globs are anchored to the whole string. * matches within one slash segment, ? matches one character, ** matches whole segments, /... abbreviates /**, and backslashes escape glob characters. Thus '*save*' is a name substring search, 'internal/*' covers one directory level, and 'internal/**' covers descendants. % and _ are not SQL wildcards. IMATCH uses simple case folding, so it does not expand ß into ss. Selector patterns remain case sensitive, and matching never changes canonical identity.
398.title: Predicates and globs

399.text: FunctionResult and optionsfiles()Non-excluded indexed files, including files with zero definitions. Standalone source; include_excluded => TRUE also includes build-excluded snapshot members.definitions(s)Declaration witnesses, projecting the declared symbol. No options.callers(s)Incoming witnesses to callables, projecting the enclosing caller; depth defaults to 1.callees(s)Outgoing call witnesses, projecting the callee; depth defaults to 1.references(s)All recorded non-definition uses, projecting the referenced symbol. No options.reads(s)Recorded read uses, projecting the referenced symbol. No options.writes(s)Recorded write uses, projecting the written symbol. No options.methods(s)Owned method declarations, projecting each method. No options.implementers(s)Recorded types implementing the selected interfaces. No options.inheritors(s)Direct struct/interface embedding declarations. No options.incoming(s)Native witnesses, projecting each relationship's source; optional via.outgoing(s)Native witnesses, projecting each relationship's target; optional via.traverse(s)Reachable symbols with minimum hop distances; direction defaults to outgoing, depth to 3, optional via.path(a, b)One shortest recorded path; depth defaults to 8, optional via.graph(s)Nodes, native kinds, sites, properties, and omissions; direction defaults to both, depth to 2, nodes to 150; optional via, exclude, or access. Nested functions consume their inner source's canonical symbol projection, not its printed strings. For example, callers(callees(func:Entry)) finds callers of the functions Entry calls. references, reads, and writes with a direct selector also match referenced dependency identities without a local declaration; a bare selector normally selects declarations. files() is standalone and cannot feed symbol navigation. There is no SQL uses() function; the compact language's :uses relation is documented separately. Depth-one callees reports the declared call target, including an interface method. Multi-hop callee traversal (depth > 1), traverse, and call paths expand known interface implementations; those implementation witnesses carry dispatch = TRUE. Callers of a concrete method can also include recorded interface-dispatch sites. These facts describe possible targets in the selected snapshots, not a guarantee of runtime execution. Source arguments precede named options, which use =>. Each option may appear once and only on a function listing it above. For example, callers(func:Save, depth => 2) is valid; callers(depth => 2, func:Save) and reads(field:Total, depth => 2) fail. OptionAllowed values and defaultsdepthInteger 1–8. Defaults: callers/callees 1, traverse 3, path 8, graph 2.nodesGraph-only integer 1–1,000; default 150. Bounds nodes, not SQL rows.directionTraverse: 'incoming' or 'outgoing' (default). Graph also accepts 'both' (default), unioning independent directional walks.viaNonempty comma-separated string of exact registered native relationship names. No wildcard expansion.excludeGraph-only comma-separated package patterns/keywords; default 'std,builtin,gorm.io/...'. 'none' disables exclusions. See graph exclusions.accessGraph-only comma-separated 'call', 'read', 'write' selections. Omission uses calls. Mutually exclusive with via.include_excludedFiles-only TRUE or FALSE (default); includes snapshot members excluded by build selection. Without via, traversal and paths follow calls and known dispatch. With via, they follow only the selected native kinds. incoming/outgoing always use native relationships; omitting via there admits all recorded native kinds. Empty list items, unknown relationships, unsupported options, and out-of-range bounds fail explicitly. Traversal fails beyond 10,000 symbols; graph bounds report omissions. Paths and graphs are terminal sources: use SELECT * without WHERE, ORDER BY, or SQL LIMIT, and do not nest them in other functions. Control a graph with depth, nodes, and exclude. A path follows the source-to-target direction and returns one shortest recorded path; no path means total: 0 with no path. Graphs return nodes, edges, sites, and omission metadata; inspect candidates when a call-graph source is ambiguous. Traversal describes recorded possible reachability. It does not guarantee execution. Ambiguous candidates and unresolved references remain visible without inferred links between similar names.
399.title: Functions and bounds

400.text:
symbol.type is the resolved type of a package-level variable, available in projection, predicates and ordering. For example: SELECT symbol.name, path, line, symbol.type
FROM var:*
WHERE symbol.type = 'context.Context' OR symbol.type = '*gorm.io/gorm.DB' Types use canonical import paths and preserve pointers/composites. Import aliases and type aliases resolve to their targets; distinct named types keep their identity. Local variables and fields are outside this initial type field; non-variable symbols return NULL. Request the field explicitly; SELECT * is unchanged. Types come from immutable document declarations in format 8, never from current source files. Queries requesting types require complete typed coverage and fail before filtering if a variable's type was not recorded; reindex or republish with type facts. Historical snapshots retain their original availability. External producers may supply a nonempty declared_type string on a proven var declaration in format 8. Metric-only queries retain their document-free path; type queries use the existing decoded document cache.
400.title: Resolved variable types

401.text: symbol.generation (integer) counts the distinct implementations a symbol has had along the base chain of the snapshot that declares it: 1 where the chain first defines it, plus one at every later snapshot whose content_fp differs. A signature-only change (a parameter rename), a comment-only edit and a move between files keep it; a re-add after a delete continues the count. It is read from symbol_deltas without decoding documents, and symbols no selected snapshot declares, such as standard library callees, read NULL. Request it explicitly; SELECT * is unchanged. SELECT symbol.name, path, symbol.generation FROM func:* WHERE symbol.generation > 10 ORDER BY symbol.generation DESC uir history symbol <selector> lists the snapshots, with their commits, at which one symbol's generation advanced. The selector must match exactly one declaration in the current checkout. Generations follow publication order: a historical import published on top of a newer head counts in import order, not commit order.
401.title: Content generations

402.text: symbol.effects (string) lists, sorted and comma-separated, the external effects of a function, method or package-level variable through everything it calls, references as a function value, or reads or writes as a package-level variable, however deep: time.read, random.read, env.read, env.write, process.read, process.write, file.read, file.write, network.io, db.read, db.write, global.read (a package-level variable indexed code writes), global.write, goroutine, channel, lock.read, lock.write, map.order and unknown. symbol.deterministic (boolean) is true when none applies other than the lock and map.order effects. Library calls are classified by the catalog in effects/catalog.go; Methods a catalogued library calls back on the values passed to it (String and Error for fmt, MarshalJSON for encoding/json including nested fields, Less for sort, and so on) count as calls. unknown is a call through an interface, a function value or a type parameter, a value of interface type or a function value passed to a catalogued library, a function without a body (linkname or assembly), an uncatalogued library function, an unresolved call, or a document indexed before format 12, so determinism is never over-claimed. time.Date, time.Unix and time.Parse are env.read, whatever zone they are given. Any file read counts, including files tracked in the repository. Other symbols read NULL. Request the fields explicitly; SELECT * is unchanged. uir effects <selector> reports one symbol's effects with the shortest path to each. SELECT symbol.query_name FROM func:* WHERE symbol.deterministic = TRUE
402.title: Effects and determinism

403.text: Inspect the explicit modern Go build constraint, including files excluded from the indexed build: uir query "SELECT path, file.build_constraint FROM files(include_excluded => TRUE) WHERE path MATCH '**/hack/**/*.go' AND file.build_constraint NOT REQUIRES 'hack' ORDER BY path" include_excluded accepts TRUE or FALSE and defaults to false. The option exposes source revisions and excluded documents already in the selected snapshot. Gitignore, module scope and test-file discovery still apply. Excluded documents have no extracted symbols; their zero file.definitions is an extraction count. The option does not type-check excluded code. file.build_constraint is a string containing the normalized expression without //go:build. A Go source without a recognized modern header returns an empty string; a non-Go source returns NULL. File aliases support f.build_constraint. Request the field explicitly: the file wildcard's eight columns do not include it. REQUIRES 'hack' accepts a single case-sensitive positive Go tag and performs exact Boolean analysis. The expression must be satisfiable and impossible to satisfy without the tag. hack, hack && linux, and (hack || linux) && !linux require hack; ignore, !hack, hack || linux, and hack && !hack do not. Tags are Boolean variables independent of the host environment. Filename suffixes and legacy-only // +build directives do not satisfy this explicit modern-header rule. NOT REQUIRES negates the result; non-Go NULL remains unknown under either operator. The field reads hash-verified source bytes belonging to the immutable snapshot through the existing checkout/stored-blob/pinned-Git recovery path. No schema migration or reindex is required when those bytes remain available. Unavailable or corrupt source bytes and malformed or duplicate recognized directives are execution errors with source and snapshot context. Exact analysis fails explicitly beyond 65,536 decision nodes or on cancellation. Ordinary file and metric queries perform no additional source reads. Constraint queries recover source bytes on cache misses and reuse a bounded, per-pipeline cache of parsed headers keyed by content hash. Cold queries can read all selected Go source candidates before WHERE filtering; LIMIT limits returned rows, not this work. Querying historical snapshots never silently substitutes current checkout content.
403.title: Build constraints

404.text:
Find small files with few definitions, or callables with many parameters or long bodies: uir query 'SELECT path, file.lines, file.definitions FROM files() WHERE file.lines < 100 AND file.definitions < 3 ORDER BY path LIMIT 1000'
uir query 'SELECT symbol.name, path, line, symbol.metrics.param_count, symbol.metrics.body_lines FROM func:* WHERE symbol.metrics.param_count > 3 OR symbol.metrics.body_lines > 50 ORDER BY path, line' FieldMeaningfile.linesPhysical source lines, including blanks and comments. Empty content has zero lines; a terminating newline adds no extra line; CRLF counts once.file.definitionsThe active document's indexed declaration count, including fields, package variables and constants, excluding references and function-local bindings.file.functionsNumber of declared functions and concrete methods; excludes interface signatures, function literals and function-valued variables.file.structsNumber of declared struct types; excludes fields, interfaces and type aliases.symbol.metrics.param_countValue parameters, expanding grouped names and counting a variadic parameter once. Receivers and type parameters do not count.symbol.metrics.body_linesInclusive physical span of the body's delimiters. Documentation and signature-only lines do not count. A one-line body counts as one; a declaration without a body returns NULL. All six metric/count fields above have catalog type integer. files() also exposes path, module, package, and snapshot; its SELECT * projects those four site fields and all four file counts. FROM files() AS f supports f.path, f.lines, f.definitions, f.functions, and f.structs. Symbol navigation cannot consume a file source. Symbol SELECT * retains its existing fields; request callable metrics explicitly. Standard root, location, snapshot and limit options apply. Test files participate when the snapshot indexed them. Existing coverage warnings describe syntax/partial extraction. Source line counts and callable metrics are recorded during indexing/publication, with immutable source revisions and document membership deciding which values a snapshot serves. file.definitions reads the active document header; file.functions and file.structs count declarations from decoded active documents. The line/definition and callable-metric examples above read neither source bytes nor full document JSON. Navigation and requested symbol properties can require document content. Filtering and ordering still inspect matching candidates before limiting; LIMIT caps returned rows rather than scanning work. Existing snapshots remain readable. Metrics are not backfilled during migration or query execution. When a requested metric was not recorded, the query fails with its snapshot/path/declaration and reindex or republish guidance; it never substitutes zero. Reindexing a historical revision provides a metric-bearing snapshot while leaving earlier documents intact. Ordinary SQL NULL rules apply to a known bodyless declaration and to metric fields on non-callable symbols. External producers may include metrics on a callable DocumentSymbol in document format 7: {"version": 1, "param_count": 2, "body_lines": 4} Here version is the metric semantics version, param_count is nonnegative, and body_lines is positive or null for a declaration without a body. Omit the entire metric record when it is unavailable; queries requesting it then fail with republish guidance. File lines are derived from the publication's verified source. Go indexing records function/method parameters and body spans, including bodyless interface signatures. Metrics do not change canonical symbol identities or semantic fingerprints. Run the focused and repository acceptance checks with gavel fixtures fixtures/queryable-metrics.md. Real-corpus benchmark instructions are in the metric plan.
404.title: Stored metrics

405.title: Producer metrics

406.text:
From the repository root, build the CLI and generate a publication containing HTTP → handler → topic → consumer links plus parallel Kubernetes relationships: make build
mkdir -p .tmp
go run -tags hack ./hack/sql-domains > .tmp/sql-domains.json
.bin/uir --dsn .tmp/sql-example.db import .tmp/sql-domains.json
.bin/uir --dsn .tmp/sql-example.db query "SELECT r.method, r.path, r.description FROM http.route:* AS r WHERE r.path IMATCH '/orders/**'"
.bin/uir --dsn .tmp/sql-example.db query "SELECT * FROM path(http.route:Orders, messaging.consumer:Consume, via => 'http.handled_by,messaging.publishes_to,messaging.delivers_to')" --format json
.bin/uir --dsn .tmp/sql-example.db query "SELECT * FROM graph(k8s.service:checkout, via => 'k8s.selects,k8s.uses_config', direction => 'outgoing')" --format json
.bin/uir --dsn .tmp/sql-example.db serve --host localhost --port 8080 The generator in hack/sql-domains/main.go is a complete producer example. kinds registers each custom name, handle category, and optional object JSON Schema. relationships registers namespaced native names, coarse UIR types, and optional property schemas. Immutable declarations store queryable props and preserve the producer's full payload. Schemas are immutable for a registered name and use local references; use a new kind name to change its schema. Document format 4 adds relationships: source canonical ID, target IDs or reference, native kind, typed properties, resolution (static, dynamic, ambiguous, or unresolved), and source range/byte/text evidence. Publication validates schemas and all identities before updating the head. Source and target postings use the existing posting index; relationship details stay in snapshot-selected documents. Include distinguishing tenant, service, broker, cluster, or namespace context in canonical identities' module, package, and owner fields. Concrete HTTP, messaging, and Kubernetes extractors are separate producers. This implementation consumes their explicit links. Older snapshots still answer queries over their existing facts; native navigation on documents before format 4 fails with reindex/reimport guidance.
406.title: Runnable domain publication

407.title: API and browser

408.text: Syntax and binding errors report a message, source line/column when available, and a hint. Queries are bounded to 65,536 bytes, 64 nested parentheses, and 64 NOT tokens. Correct the query rather than switching database dialect: this grammar is the same on both storage backends. Missing required stored facts ask for reindexing or republishing; historical snapshots do not gain new capabilities in place. Partial/syntax coverage and missing heads remain evidence gaps, not proof that a symbol has no uses. UIR SQL does not implement joins, SQL subqueries, CTEs, aggregation (COUNT, SUM, GROUP BY, HAVING), DISTINCT, UNION, OFFSET, arithmetic, scalar function calls, field-to-field comparisons, literal-list IN, LIKE, <>, or writes. Use nested navigation instead of joins, MATCH/IMATCH instead of LIKE, and != instead of <>. A graph or path query cannot have row clauses. The cookbook includes valid alternatives. The implementation sources are sqlsyntax/ast.go and sqlsyntax/parser.go for syntax, sql_bind.go for functions/options/selectors, and sql_rows.go and sql_files.go for fields and projection. go test ./query -run TestQuery -ginkgo.focus='SQL documentation examples' parses every SQL fence in this reference and the cookbook and checks that every registered source function has an example.
408.title: Errors and unsupported SQL
